The definite article always comes after its noun.

For singular nouns:

- For masculine singular nouns, the article is ûgœ. For example, in the phrase "vcéø ûgœ" (the cat), ûgœ shows that the noun vcéø (cat) is both singular and masculine.
- For feminine singular nouns, the article is cgœ. An example is "ldîucge cgœ" (the house), where cgœ shows that ldîucge (house) is singular and feminine.

For plural nouns, regardless of gender:

- The article is îûgœ for both masculine and feminine plural nouns. (e.g., "îvcéø îûgœ", the cats; "îldîucge îûgœ", the houses.)

In summary, ûgœ is used with masculine singular nouns, cgœ with feminine singular nouns, and îûgœ with all plural nouns. This variation in definite articles reflects the grammatical gender and number of nouns in Éølûizê.

After c, û, u, d, o, p, ç, xà and some occurrences of é, the singular masculine article ûgœ becomes 'gœ.


-----
NOUNS
-----
* Gender
Every Éølûizê noun has a grammatical gender, either masculine or feminine.

* Number
As in English, Éølûizê nouns inflect for number, however they do so through prefixation rather than suffixation.

The plural is usually formed from the singular by adding the prefix morpheme î- (e.g., ldîucge > îldîucge 'houses'). 

Nouns beginning with oc- and oû- take the prefix fe- instead of î- (e.g., ocpov > feocpov 'pipes', oûqô > feoûqô 'games'), except for the nouns ocbelcgœ, ociicî, oûlæ, and oûgœy which form their plural by prefixing the morpheme î- (e.g., oûlæ > îoûlæ 'tires').

Seven nouns beginning with od- form their plural with fe-. These are odlûs, odgœgœucø, odyué, odqôuy, odæ, odéø, and odqôodqô (e.g., odlûs > feodlûs 'knees'). All other nouns beginning with od-, such as odîuy or odiv, follow the regular plural pattern and take î- (e.g., odiv > îodiv 'holes').

Nouns that begin with î-, fe- or n- in the singular do not change in the plural (e.g., feudiø cgœ 'the cross' > feudiø îûgœ 'the crosses').

Nouns that begin with gœc- typically change to feoc- in the plural (e.g., gœcliodqô > feocliodqô 'newspapers'). However, several nouns beginning with gœc- are exceptions to this rule and form their plural by adding î- instead. These are gœcy, gœcø, gœcrêclicø, gœcøcéø, gœcrêuvîûzê, gœcvuøçi, gœcrêiûî and gœcsçi (e.g., gœcrêuvîûzê ûgœ > îgœcrêuvîûzê îûgœ).

Similarly, most nouns beginning with gœuc- change to feoc- in the plural. Examples of this pattern include gœucy, gœucidø, gœucgeç, gœuciuæodî, gœucrêciv, and gœucivurê (e.g., gœucivurê lo > feocivurê îûbe 'stained-glass windows'). However, some gœuc- nouns do not follow this pattern and form their plural with î-, notably gœuci, gœuciuvvc, gœucbelcéø, gœucvçbe, gœucliûrêods and gœucvidæ (e.g., gœuci ûgœ > îgœuci îûgœ 'the rails').

* Case
Nouns in Éølûizê are not inflected for any other grammatical categories. (However, personal pronouns are inflected for case and person.)

----------
Adjectives
----------

An adjective must agree in gender and number with the noun it modifies. Éølûizê adjectives therefore have four forms: masculine singular, feminine singular, masculine plural, and feminine plural. A few adjectives, like ocûy and ocûrêodl, have a fifth form, viz. an additional masculine singular form for use after a noun ending in c, û, u, d, o, p, ç, xà and some occurrences of é, e.g. lubeicqô ocûy lo (a beautiful garden), ûgegedé gœûy lo (a handsome man), ûgegeûzê ûgœgœûy ûlo (a beautiful woman), îvlczêlû feocûy îûgœ (the beautiful children), îldîucge îûgœgœûy îûgœ (the beautiful houses).

The masculine singular, an adjective's basic form, is listed in dictionaries. Most feminine forms are formed by adding the prefix û- to the masculine form, e.g., belcis > ûbelcis, vlûgœ > ûvlûgœ, lcîiûæ > ûlcîiûæ. 

Under certain circumstances, other minor changes occur in the formation of feminine forms. Specifically, masculine adjectives beginning with gœû-, gœu-, ld-, lû-, îd- or îc- double their initial consonant before adding the prefix û- (e.g., gœûoiø > ûgœgœûoiø, gœuvlûs > ûgœgœuvlûs, ldy > ûlldy, lûuølc > ûllûuølc, îdis > ûîîdis, and îcy > ûîîcy).

Additionally, adjectives beginning with ø- change to ûéø- (e.g., ølcgœy > ûéølcgœy); those beginning with ioû- or feoû- change to ûîoû- (e.g., ioûvvûgediæ > ûîoûvvûgediæ, feoûuiozê > ûîoûuiozê), with the exception of the irregular feoûurê (old) whose feminine form is ûgœgœuûurê; s- changes to ûos- (e.g., sldgœ > ûosldgœ); zêu- changes to ûrêu- (e.g., zêuvøc > ûrêuvøc); zêû- changes to ûrêxà- (e.g., zêûiy > ûrêxàiy); iû- changes to ûixà- (e.g., iûslcivç > ûixàslcivç); vû- changes to ûvxà- (e.g., vûuohlu > ûvxàuohlu); and adjectives beginning with od- have a special form gœd- (becoming ûgœgœd- in feminine) that appears after c, û, u, d, o, p, ç, xà and some occurrences of é, (e.g., odzê/gœdzê > ûgœgœdzê, odge/gœdge > ûgœgœdge).

If an adjective's basic form beginning with û-, it does not change in the feminine (cf. ûéøui ûgegedé lo 'a rich man' > ûéøui ûgegeûzê ûlo 'a rich woman').

The plural is normally formed by adding the prefix î- to the singular (masculine and feminine; e.g., ugœdqô > îugœdqô, ûugœdqô > îûugœdqô). If the basic form beginning with î-, fe-, or n-, an adjective does not change in the masculine plural (e.g., îcy > îcy, feoûiçlçs > feoûiçlçs, feodbe > feodbe), but its feminine plural form follows the rules detailed above. All Éølûizê adjectives beginning with ocû- take the prefix fe- in the masculine plural (e.g., ocûrêodl > feocûrêodl). Distinctive plural forms occur with adjectives beginning with gœc-, which normally change to feoc- in the masculine plural (e.g., gœcliûrêué > feocliûrêué, gœcivlûø > feocivlûø), with only two exceptions: gœcvczê > îgœcvczê and gœcrêcl > îgœcrêcl which follow the regular pattern. By contrast, the feminine plural is always formed according to the general rule: ûgœcivlûø > îûgœcivlûø.

Adjective placement follows specific patterns. Most adjectives are placed after the noun they modify, and this is particularly true for colors, as in ûsodi ûgœ lurê (the red wine). However, certain short, commonly used adjectives – those dealing with beauty, age, goodness, or size (sometimes remembered by the acronym "BAGS") – typically precede their nouns. These are ocûy (beautiful), ldy (good), zêûiy (brief), belcis (big/tall), îdis (fat/large), feoczê (false), vocé (high), sldgœ (long), zêûiy (brief), ûloûqô (young), ugœdqô (pretty), îucrêocge (bad), ioûgœgœuûge (better), ocûrêodl (new), vuvûæ (small), feoûurê (old); e.g., ûgegeûzê ûlo ûgœgœûy ("a beautiful woman").

--------
PRONOUNS
--------
In Éølûizê, pronouns are inflected to indicate their role in the sentence (subject, direct object, and so on), as well as to reflect the person, gender, and number of their referents. 

*Personal Pronouns
éølûizê personal pronouns (analogous to English I, you, he/she, we, and they) reflect the person and number of their referent, and in the case of the third person, its gender as well. They also reflect the role they play in their clause: subject, direct object, indirect object, or other.

The personal pronouns change form to reflect the role they play in their clause. The forms used for subjects are called the subject pronouns, subjective pronouns, or nominative pronouns. They are as follows: 

**Subject Pronouns
------------------------
Number   | Person           | Subject Pronoun
------------------------
Singular | 1st              | ûqô
         | 2nd (informal)   | ov
         | 2nd (formal)     | îodrê
         | 3rd (masculine)  | gœu
         | 3rd (feminine)   | ûgœgœû
         | 3rd (neutral)    | ld
------------------------
Plural   | 1st              | îodl
         | 2nd              | îodrê
         | 3rd (masculine)  | îgœu
         | 3rd (feminine)   | îûgœgœû
------------------------

Note: Whenever the subject pronoun ûqô occurs after c, û, u, d, o, p, ç, xà, a and some occurrences of é, it becomes 'qô.

-----
VERBS
-----
Verbs in Éølûizê are conjugated to reflect the following information:

    a mood (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, or conditional)
    a tense (past, present, or future, though not all tenses can be combined with all moods)
    an aspect (perfective or imperfective)
    a voice (active, passive, or reflexive)
    Nonfinite forms (e.g., participles, gerunds, infinitives)


Verbs in the finite moods (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, and conditional) are also conjugated to agree with their subjects in person (first, second, or third) and number (singular or plural). As in English, the subject must be included (except in the imperative mood); in other words Éølûizê is neither a null-subject nor a pro-drop language.

Auxiliary verbs are combined with past participles of main verbs to produce compound tenses, including the compound past. For most main verbs the auxiliary is (the appropriate form of) iudrêc ("to have"), but for reflexive verbs and certain intransitive verbs the auxiliary is a form of ûiva ("to be"). The participle agrees with the subject when the auxiliary is ûiva, and with a following direct object (if any) when the auxiliary is iudrêc. Forms of ûiva are also used with the past participles of transitive verbs to form the passive voice.

*Morphology

In Éølûizê, a verb is inflected to reflect its mood and tense, as well as to agree with its subject in person and number.

**Stems and conjugation prefixes

éølûizê verbs have a large number of simple (one-word) forms. These are composed of two distinct parts: the stem (or root, or radix), which indicates which verb it is, and the prefix (inflection), which indicates the verb's tense (imperfect, present, future etc.) and mood and its subject's person (I, you, he/she etc.) and number, though many prefixes can correspond to multiple tense-mood-subject combinations. In certain parts of the second conjugation there is also a prefix -îîu- between the stem and the ending.

    In vlûucgœicæ, the stem -gœicæ indicates that the verb is iûgœicæ (to speak) and the prefix vlûuc- marks the third-person plural imperfect indicative. "Third person plural" meaning the subject of the verb is "they". The "imperfect indicative" being a tense.
    In îldîîuluzê, the stem -luzê indicates that the verb is iuluzê (to finish), the prefix -îîu- precedes it, and the inflection îld- marks the first-person plural present indicative or imperative. The "first-person plural" is the "we" form of a verb. The "present indicative" being a tense and "imperative" being a mood, but in Éølûizê they are indistinguishable without context.

These verb conjugations are coupled with a subject pronoun in order to convey who the subject of the verb is (i.e. who is doing the action).

***The principle of the fixed stem

The stem normally stays fixed in the first two conjugations:

    iûgœicæ: îuciûgœicæ ûqô, îcgœicæ ov, vlûîîcgœicæ îgœu'oh, îldugœicæ îodl ûoh, nûgœicæ...
    iuluzê: îuciuluzê ûqô, îûvmeluzê îodrê, vlûîîuluzê îgœu'oh, îuluzê, îlduîîuluzê îodl ûoh...

In the third it is often modified, sometimes even between persons in the same tense:

    iudgœodrê: feoûrê ûqô, feoûrê ov, voûrê gœu, îldgœodrê îodl, nûgœodrê îodrê, vlûgœoûrê îgœu.

But such irregularities apart, the principle is that nothing is removed from the stem. 


**Conjugation prefixes

The conjugation prefix tells us:

    For all verbs, the mood and the tense;
    For finite verbs, the person and the number; and
    For the past participle alone, the gender and the number.

Apart from a few frequent verbs which are considered totally irregular (mainly iudrêc, ûiva, iûgœgœc and ûiuczê), for each tense of each mood a series of six prefixes (one for each person singular and plural) is associated with a group or subgroup of verbs.


*Formation of simple tenses active

These tenses are not formed with an auxiliary, and their formation is discussed in the following section.

**Infinitive

A verb is normally named by its present infinitive. Starting from this infinitive, the conjugations can be classified into three different groups:

    The first group or first conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with iû- (with the exception of iûgœgœc, which due to its numerous irregularities is usually classed as being in the third conjugation):

    iûgeuc, iûpcgœcy, iûvlcéø, iûpdrêlû, iûgeiûzê, iûslcge, iûîîcæ, iûpcæ, iûlûgediæ, iûbeicsûi, etc.

        For example, for the verb iûgœicæ, the stem is -gœicæ and the infinitive prefix is iû-.

    The second group or second conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with iu- whose present participle begins with vlcîîu-:

    iulçy, iuvcægedø, iuæiûosçbe, iuioûgœzê, iubelcis, iïcé, iuvîûrêlu, iugœdæ, iusodi, iusoi, iugœcî, etc.

        For example, for the verb iuluzê, the stem is -luzê and the infinitive prefix is iu-.

    The third group or third conjugation. This contains all the other verbs.
    
Note that the auxiliaries ûiva and iudrêc, although they would naturally seem to belong to the third conjugation, are traditionally classed separately. 

**Present indicative

The present indicative is the form of the verb used to describe an action in the present e.g. ûbeicsûi ûqô means "I watch".

The stem of the present indicative is not always regular and can vary (especially in the third conjugation) and there are three main sets of prefixes:

    Verbs beginning with iû- (all verbs of the first group): û-, îû-, û-, îld-, nû-, vlû-.
    Verbs beginning with iu- (all verbs of the second group and most of the third): îu-, îu-, vu-, îldîîu-, nûîîu-, vlûîîu-. But there are numerous irregularities, especially in the third group.
    Verbs beginning with ûi- (part of the third group): î-, î-, - , îld-, nû-, vlû-.

**Imperfect indicative

The imperfect indicative is a past tense describing states and actions that were ongoing in the past, e.g. "îucbeicsûi ûqô" means "I was watching".

**Past participle

Past participles, unlike present participles and gerundives, may be inflected to show gender and number by adding û- and î- prefixes, as with a normal adjective. Hence, "vuzêldø vuoizê lo", "ûvuzêldø ûiudæ ûlo", "îvuzêldø îvuoizê îûbe", and "îûvuzêldø îûiudæ îûbe."

The plain (masculine singular) form of a past participle begins with ç- for the 1st group verbs, and with u- for the 2nd group verbs. Third group verbs have more diverse prefixes : o- (ûibelûvlû obelûvlû, ûiudy oy, ûiugœ ogœ, etc. and iudrêcî oî, iudrê orê, iudrêodæ oæ), îu- (ûivvûge îuge, ûibelûiæ îuiæ, etc.), îo- (ûiogœølu îogœølu and ûiogœøûi îogœøûi and only these verbs), vu- (ûiubeocge vubeocge, ûiube vube, etc.), v- (verbs in ûibelu- : ûibeluûæ vluûæ), viû- (iuirêod viûrêod, iuirêodø viûrêodø, iuizêzêd viûzêzêd and iuizêzêodî viûzêzêodî), or oû (iudrêc oû). 

*Compound Tenses

éølûizê compound tenses are verb forms that combine an auxiliary verb (either iudrêc or ûiva) with the past participle of the main verb. These tenses are used to indicate actions that are completed or relate to another point in time. There are several compound tenses in Éølûizê, each serving a specific purpose and adding nuance to the timeline of events.

**Compound Past

The compound past is perhaps the most commonly used compound tense in Éølûizê. It is used to describe actions that have been completed in the past and is translated by the English simple past. The auxiliary verb is either iudrêc or ûiva in the present tense, preceded by the past participle of the main verb. For example, "çslcge uc'qô" (I ate) or "çrêuiic vîû gœu" (He arrived). iudrêc is used with most verbs, while ûiva is used with a specific group of verbs, particularly those indicating movement or change of state, and with all reflexive verbs. When in doubt, iudrêc should be used by default.

- The article is vmuy for both masculine and feminine plural nouns. (e.g., "vgwejlà vmuy", the cats; "vràavwiwef vmuy", the houses.)

In summary, muy is used with masculine singular nouns, wey with feminine singular nouns, and vmuy with all plural nouns. This variation in definite articles reflects the grammatical gender and number of nouns in Jlàràmubx.

After we, mu, wi, a, zà, re, k, c and some occurrences of j, the singular masculine article muy becomes 'y.


-----
NOUNS
-----
* Gender
Every Jlàràmubx noun has a grammatical gender, either masculine or feminine.

* Number
As in English, Jlàràmubx nouns inflect for number, however they do so through prefixation rather than suffixation.

The plural is usually formed from the singular by adding the prefix morpheme v- (e.g., ràavwiwef > vràavwiwef 'houses'). 

Nouns beginning with zàwe- and zàmu- take the prefix p- instead of v- (e.g., zàwerezàg > pzàwerezàg 'pipes', zàmudi > pzàmudi 'games'), except for the nouns zàwemiràwey, zàwebbwev, zàmuràç, and zàmuyle which form their plural by prefixing the morpheme v- (e.g., zàmuràç > vzàmuràç 'tires').

Seven nouns beginning with zàa- form their plural with p-. These are zàaràmut, zàayywiwelà, zàalewij, zàadiwile, zàaç, zàajlà, and zàadizàadi (e.g., zàaràmut > pzàaràmut 'knees'). All other nouns beginning with zàa-, such as zàavwile or zàabg, follow the regular plural pattern and take v- (e.g., zàabg > vzàabg 'holes').

Nouns that begin with v-, p- or qu- in the singular do not change in the plural (e.g., pwiablà wey 'the cross' > pwiablà vmuy 'the crosses').

Nouns that begin with ywe- typically change to pzàwe- in the plural (e.g., yweràbzàadi > pzàweràbzàadi 'newspapers'). However, several nouns beginning with ywe- are exceptions to this rule and form their plural by adding v- instead. These are ywele, ywelà, ywehweràbwelà, ywelàwejlà, ywehwigvmux, ywegwilàkb, ywehbmuv and ywetkb (e.g., ywehwigvmux muy > vywehwigvmux vmuy).

Similarly, most nouns beginning with ywiwe- change to pzàwe- in the plural. Examples of this pattern include ywiwele, ywiwebalà, ywiwefk, ywiwebwiçzàav, ywiwehwebg, and ywiwebgwih (e.g., ywiwebgwih ràzà > pzàwebgwih vmumi 'stained-glass windows'). However, some ywiwe- nouns do not follow this pattern and form their plural with v-, notably ywiweb, ywiwebwiggwe, ywiwemiràwejlà, ywiwegkmi, ywiweràbmuhzàat and ywiwegbaç (e.g., ywiweb muy > vywiweb vmuy 'the rails').

* Case
Nouns in Jlàràmubx are not inflected for any other grammatical categories. (However, personal pronouns are inflected for case and person.)

----------
Adjectives
----------

An adjective must agree in gender and number with the noun it modifies. Jlàràmubx adjectives therefore have four forms: masculine singular, feminine singular, masculine plural, and feminine plural. A few adjectives, like zàwemule and zàwemuhzàarà, have a fifth form, viz. an additional masculine singular form for use after a noun ending in we, mu, wi, a, zà, re, k, c and some occurrences of j, e.g. ràwimibwedi zàwemule ràzà (a beautiful garden), muffaj ymule ràzà (a handsome man), muffmux muyymule muràzà (a beautiful woman), vgràwexràmu pzàwemule vmuy (the beautiful children), vràavwiwef vmuyymule vmuy (the beautiful houses).

The masculine singular, an adjective's basic form, is listed in dictionaries. Most feminine forms are formed by adding the prefix mu- to the masculine form, e.g., miràwebt > mumiràwebt, gràmuy > mugràmuy, ràwevbmuç > muràwevbmuç. 

Under certain circumstances, other minor changes occur in the formation of feminine forms. Specifically, masculine adjectives beginning with ymu-, ywi-, ràa-, ràmu-, va- or vwe- double their initial consonant before adding the prefix mu- (e.g., ymuzàblà > muyymuzàblà, ywigràmut > muyywigràmut, ràale > muràràale, ràmuwilàràwe > muràràmuwilàràwe, vabt > muvvabt, and vwele > muvvwele).

Additionally, adjectives beginning with là- change to mujlà- (e.g., làràweyle > mujlàràweyle); those beginning with bzàmu- or pzàmu- change to muvzàmu- (e.g., bzàmuggmufabç > muvzàmuggmufabç, pzàmuwibzàx > muvzàmuwibzàx), with the exception of the irregular pzàmuwih (old) whose feminine form is muyywimuwih; t- changes to muzàt- (e.g., tràay > muzàtràay); xwi- changes to muhwi- (e.g., xwiglàwe > muhwiglàwe); xmu- changes to muhc- (e.g., xmuble > muhcble); bmu- changes to mubc- (e.g., bmutràwebgk > mubctràwebgk); gmu- changes to mugc- (e.g., gmuwizàoràwi > mugcwizàoràwi); and adjectives beginning with zàa- have a special form ya- (becoming muyya- in feminine) that appears after we, mu, wi, a, zà, re, k, c and some occurrences of j, (e.g., zàax/yax > muyyax, zàaf/yaf > muyyaf).

If an adjective's basic form beginning with mu-, it does not change in the feminine (cf. mujlàwib muffaj ràzà 'a rich man' > mujlàwib muffmux muràzà 'a rich woman').

The plural is normally formed by adding the prefix v- to the singular (masculine and feminine; e.g., wiyadi > vwiyadi, muwiyadi > vmuwiyadi). If the basic form beginning with v-, p-, or qu-, an adjective does not change in the masculine plural (e.g., vwele > vwele, pzàmubkràkt > pzàmubkràkt, pzàami > pzàami), but its feminine plural form follows the rules detailed above. All Jlàràmubx adjectives beginning with zàwemu- take the prefix p- in the masculine plural (e.g., zàwemuhzàarà > pzàwemuhzàarà). Distinctive plural forms occur with adjectives beginning with ywe-, which normally change to pzàwe- in the masculine plural (e.g., yweràbmuhwij > pzàweràbmuhwij, ywebgràmulà > pzàwebgràmulà), with only two exceptions: ywegwex > vywegwex and ywehwerà > vywehwerà which follow the regular pattern. By contrast, the feminine plural is always formed according to the general rule: muywebgràmulà > vmuywebgràmulà.

Adjective placement follows specific patterns. Most adjectives are placed after the noun they modify, and this is particularly true for colors, as in mutzàab muy ràwih (the red wine). However, certain short, commonly used adjectives – those dealing with beauty, age, goodness, or size (sometimes remembered by the acronym "BAGS") – typically precede their nouns. These are zàwemule (beautiful), ràale (good), xmuble (brief), miràwebt (big/tall), vabt (fat/large), pzàwex (false), gzàwej (high), tràay (long), xmuble (brief), muràzàmudi (young), wiyadi (pretty), vwiwehzàwef (bad), bzàmuyywimuf (better), zàwemuhzàarà (new), gwigmuç (small), pzàmuwih (old); e.g., muffmux muràzà muyymule ("a beautiful woman").

--------
PRONOUNS
--------
In Jlàràmubx, pronouns are inflected to indicate their role in the sentence (subject, direct object, and so on), as well as to reflect the person, gender, and number of their referents. 

*Personal Pronouns
jlàràmubx personal pronouns (analogous to English I, you, he/she, we, and they) reflect the person and number of their referent, and in the case of the third person, its gender as well. They also reflect the role they play in their clause: subject, direct object, indirect object, or other.

The personal pronouns change form to reflect the role they play in their clause. The forms used for subjects are called the subject pronouns, subjective pronouns, or nominative pronouns. They are as follows: 

**Subject Pronouns
------------------------
Number   | Person           | Subject Pronoun
------------------------
Singular | 1st              | mudi
         | 2nd (informal)   | zàg
         | 2nd (formal)     | vzàah
         | 3rd (masculine)  | ywi
         | 3rd (feminine)   | muyymu
         | 3rd (neutral)    | ràa
------------------------
Plural   | 1st              | vzàarà
         | 2nd              | vzàah
         | 3rd (masculine)  | vywi
         | 3rd (feminine)   | vmuyymu
------------------------

Note: Whenever the subject pronoun mudi occurs after we, mu, wi, a, zà, re, k, c, ê and some occurrences of j, it becomes 'di.

-----
VERBS
-----
Verbs in Jlàràmubx are conjugated to reflect the following information:

    a mood (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, or conditional)
    a tense (past, present, or future, though not all tenses can be combined with all moods)
    an aspect (perfective or imperfective)
    a voice (active, passive, or reflexive)
    Nonfinite forms (e.g., participles, gerunds, infinitives)


Verbs in the finite moods (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, and conditional) are also conjugated to agree with their subjects in person (first, second, or third) and number (singular or plural). As in English, the subject must be included (except in the imperative mood); in other words Jlàràmubx is neither a null-subject nor a pro-drop language.

Auxiliary verbs are combined with past participles of main verbs to produce compound tenses, including the compound past. For most main verbs the auxiliary is (the appropriate form of) bwiahwe ("to have"), but for reflexive verbs and certain intransitive verbs the auxiliary is a form of mubgê ("to be"). The participle agrees with the subject when the auxiliary is mubgê, and with a following direct object (if any) when the auxiliary is bwiahwe. Forms of mubgê are also used with the past participles of transitive verbs to form the passive voice.

*Morphology

In Jlàràmubx, a verb is inflected to reflect its mood and tense, as well as to agree with its subject in person and number.

**Stems and conjugation prefixes

jlàràmubx verbs have a large number of simple (one-word) forms. These are composed of two distinct parts: the stem (or root, or radix), which indicates which verb it is, and the prefix (inflection), which indicates the verb's tense (imperfect, present, future etc.) and mood and its subject's person (I, you, he/she etc.) and number, though many prefixes can correspond to multiple tense-mood-subject combinations. In certain parts of the second conjugation there is also a prefix -vvwi- between the stem and the ending.

    In gràmuwiweybweç, the stem -ybweç indicates that the verb is bmuybweç (to speak) and the prefix gràmuwiwe- marks the third-person plural imperfect indicative. "Third person plural" meaning the subject of the verb is "they". The "imperfect indicative" being a tense.
    In vràavvwiràwix, the stem -ràwix indicates that the verb is bwiràwix (to finish), the prefix -vvwi- precedes it, and the inflection vràa- marks the first-person plural present indicative or imperative. The "first-person plural" is the "we" form of a verb. The "present indicative" being a tense and "imperative" being a mood, but in Jlàràmubx they are indistinguishable without context.

These verb conjugations are coupled with a subject pronoun in order to convey who the subject of the verb is (i.e. who is doing the action).

***The principle of the fixed stem

The stem normally stays fixed in the first two conjugations:

    bmuybweç: vwiwebmuybweç mudi, vweybweç zàg, gràmuvvweybweç vywi'zào, vràawiybweç vzàarà muzào, qumuybweç...
    bwiràwix: vwiwebwiràwix mudi, vmugîràwix vzàah, gràmuvvwiràwix vywi'zào, vwiràwix, vràawivvwiràwix vzàarà muzào...

In the third it is often modified, sometimes even between persons in the same tense:

    bwiayzàah: pzàmuh mudi, pzàmuh zàg, gzàmuh ywi, vràayzàah vzàarà, qumuyzàah vzàah, gràmuyzàmuh vywi.

But such irregularities apart, the principle is that nothing is removed from the stem. 


**Conjugation prefixes

The conjugation prefix tells us:

    For all verbs, the mood and the tense;
    For finite verbs, the person and the number; and
    For the past participle alone, the gender and the number.

Apart from a few frequent verbs which are considered totally irregular (mainly bwiahwe, mubgê, bmuyywe and mubwiwex), for each tense of each mood a series of six prefixes (one for each person singular and plural) is associated with a group or subgroup of verbs.


*Formation of simple tenses active

These tenses are not formed with an auxiliary, and their formation is discussed in the following section.

**Infinitive

A verb is normally named by its present infinitive. Starting from this infinitive, the conjugations can be classified into three different groups:

    The first group or first conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with bmu- (with the exception of bmuyywe, which due to its numerous irregularities is usually classed as being in the third conjugation):

    bmufwiwe, bmureweywele, bmugràwejlà, bmureahràmu, bmufbmux, bmutràwef, bmuvvweç, bmureweç, bmuràmufabç, bmumibwetmub, etc.

        For example, for the verb bmuybweç, the stem is -ybweç and the infinitive prefix is bmu-.

    The second group or second conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with bwi- whose present participle begins with gràwevvwi-:

    bwiràkle, bwigweçfalà, bwiçbmuzàtkmi, bwibzàmuyx, bwimiràwebt, bïwej, bwigvmuhràwi, bwiyaç, bwitzàab, bwitzàb, bwiywev, etc.

        For example, for the verb bwiràwix, the stem is -ràwix and the infinitive prefix is bwi-.

    The third group or third conjugation. This contains all the other verbs.
    
Note that the auxiliaries mubgê and bwiahwe, although they would naturally seem to belong to the third conjugation, are traditionally classed separately. 

**Present indicative

The present indicative is the form of the verb used to describe an action in the present e.g. mumibwetmub mudi means "I watch".

The stem of the present indicative is not always regular and can vary (especially in the third conjugation) and there are three main sets of prefixes:

    Verbs beginning with bmu- (all verbs of the first group): mu-, vmu-, mu-, vràa-, qumu-, gràmu-.
    Verbs beginning with bwi- (all verbs of the second group and most of the third): vwi-, vwi-, gwi-, vràavvwi-, qumuvvwi-, gràmuvvwi-. But there are numerous irregularities, especially in the third group.
    Verbs beginning with mub- (part of the third group): v-, v-, - , vràa-, qumu-, gràmu-.
    
    Example:

-------------------------------
Person         | Singular             | Plural
-------------------------------
1st person     | mumibwetmub mudi         | vràamibwetmub vzàarà
2nd person     | vmumibwetmub zàg        | qumumibwetmub vzàah
3rd person     | mumibwetmub ràa/muyymu/ywi | gràmumibwetmub vmuyymu/vywi
-------------------------------

-------------------------------
1st person     | vwivwiajlà mudi         | vràavvwivwiajlà vzàarà
2nd person     | vwivwiajlà zàg         | qumuvvwivwiajlà vzàah
3rd person     | gwivwiajlà ràa/muyymu/ywi | gràmuvvwivwiajlà vmuyymu/vywi

    Verbs of the second group take an -vvwi- in the plural conjugations.
        
        
**Imperfect indicative

The imperfect indicative is a past tense describing states and actions that were ongoing in the past, e.g. "vwiwemibwetmub mudi" means "I was watching".

    The stem of the imperfect indicative is always invariant for a single verb. It is derived in various ways depending on the verb group.
    For the first group, the stem is the infinitive minus the bmu- prefix, e.g., bmumibwetmub -> -mibwetmub.
    For the second group, the stem is the infinitive minus the bwi- prefix plus the vvwi- prefix, e.g., bwivwiajlà -> -vvwivwiajlà. 
    And for the third group, the stem is derived from the first person plural of the present indicative.

    The conjugation prefixes of this tense are for any of the three groups always: vwiwe-, vwiwe-, gwiwe-, vràawi-, qumuwi-, gràmuwiwe-.

2nd person     | vwiwemibwetmub zàg         | qumuwimibwetmub vzàah

3rd person     | gwiwevvwivwiajlà ràa/muyymu/ywi | gràmuwiwevvwivwiajlà vmuyymu/vywi
-------------------------------



    Verb mubgê : the stem is -gk, endings are the same.
    

**Future

The future prefixes correspond to the present indicative of the verb bwiahwe. They are always regular: wiwe-, vwe-, we-, vràa-, qumu-, gràa-.

    The future stem is simply the infinitive (dictionary form). In other words, to form the future tense these prefixes are added to the infinitive:

        wiwebwivwiajlà mudi ('I will choose'), vwebmumibwetmub zàg ('you will watch'), webwigbav muyymu ('she will exit'), vràabmuyywiwehwebg vzàarà ('we will work'), qumubwitzàab vzàah ('you will blush'), gràabwigbweç vywi ('they will leave').

    But there are several irregular future stems, especially in the third group.

**Past participle

Past participles, unlike present participles and gerundives, may be inflected to show gender and number by adding mu- and v- prefixes, as with a normal adjective. Hence, "gwixràalà gwizàbx ràzà", "mugwixràalà mubwiaç muràzà", "vgwixràalà vgwizàbx vmumi", and "vmugwixràalà vmubwiaç vmumi."

The plain (masculine singular) form of a past participle begins with k- for the 1st group verbs, and with wi- for the 2nd group verbs. Third group verbs have more diverse prefixes : zà- (mubmiràmugràmu zàmiràmugràmu, mubwiale zàle, mubwiy zày, etc. and bwiahwev zàv, bwiah zàh, bwiahzàaç zàç), vwi- (mubggmuf vwif, mubmiràmubç vwibç, etc.), vzà- (mubzàylàràwi vzàylàràwi and mubzàylàmub vzàylàmub and only these verbs), gwi- (mubwimizàwef gwimizàwef, mubwimi gwimi, etc.), g- (verbs in mubmiràwi- : mubmiràwimuç gràwimuç), gbmu- (bwibhzàa gbmuhzàa, bwibhzàalà gbmuhzàalà, bwibxxa gbmuxxa and bwibxxzàav gbmuxxzàav), or zàmu (bwiahwe zàmu). 

*Compound Tenses

jlàràmubx compound tenses are verb forms that combine an auxiliary verb (either bwiahwe or mubgê) with the past participle of the main verb. These tenses are used to indicate actions that are completed or relate to another point in time. There are several compound tenses in Jlàràmubx, each serving a specific purpose and adding nuance to the timeline of events.

**Compound Past

The compound past is perhaps the most commonly used compound tense in Jlàràmubx. It is used to describe actions that have been completed in the past and is translated by the English simple past. The auxiliary verb is either bwiahwe or mubgê in the present tense, preceded by the past participle of the main verb. For example, "ktràwef wiwe'di" (I ate) or "khwibbwe gvmu ywi" (He arrived). bwiahwe is used with most verbs, while mubgê is used with a specific group of verbs, particularly those indicating movement or change of state, and with all reflexive verbs. When in doubt, bwiahwe should be used by default.

Nouns beginning with ku- and kî- take the prefix y- instead of ap- (e.g., kuenki > ykuenki 'pipes', kîû > ykîû 'games'), except for the nouns kuhsuæt, kuœcœcuap, kîsev, and kîætè which form their plural by prefixing the morpheme ap- (e.g., kîsev > apkîsev 'tires').

Seven nouns beginning with kat- form their plural with y-. These are katsîø, katætætæcuq, katèæcr, katûæcè, katev, katrq, and katûkatû (e.g., katsîø > ykatsîø 'knees'). All other nouns beginning with kat-, such as katapæcè or katœci, follow the regular plural pattern and take ap- (e.g., katœci > apkatœci 'holes').

Nouns that begin with ap-, y- or ef- in the singular do not change in the plural (e.g., yæcatœcq uæt 'the cross' > yæcatœcq apîæt 'the crosses').

Nouns that begin with ætu- typically change to yku- in the plural (e.g., ætusœckatû > ykusœckatû 'newspapers'). However, several nouns beginning with ætu- are exceptions to this rule and form their plural by adding ap- instead. These are ætuè, ætuq, ætuejusœcuq, ætuqurq, ætuejæciapîo, ætuiæcqxœc, ætuejœcîap and ætuøxœc (e.g., ætuejæciapîo îæt > apætuejæciapîo apîæt).

Similarly, most nouns beginning with ætæcu- change to yku- in the plural. Examples of this pattern include ætæcuè, ætæcuœcatq, ætæcuàx, ætæcuœcæcevkatap, ætæcuejuœci, and ætæcuœciæcej (e.g., ætæcuœciæcej sk > ykuœciæcej apîh 'stained-glass windows'). However, some ætæcu- nouns do not follow this pattern and form their plural with ap-, notably ætæcuœc, ætæcuœcæciiu, ætæcuhsurq, ætæcuixh, ætæcusœcîejkatø and ætæcuiœcatev (e.g., ætæcuœc îæt > apætæcuœc apîæt 'the rails').

* Case
Nouns in Rqsîœco are not inflected for any other grammatical categories. (However, personal pronouns are inflected for case and person.)

----------
Adjectives
----------

An adjective must agree in gender and number with the noun it modifies. Rqsîœco adjectives therefore have four forms: masculine singular, feminine singular, masculine plural, and feminine plural. A few adjectives, like kuîè and kuîejkats, have a fifth form, viz. an additional masculine singular form for use after a noun ending in u, î, æc, at, k, en, x, l and some occurrences of r, e.g. sæchœcuû kuîè sk (a beautiful garden), îààatr ætîè sk (a handsome man), îààîo îætætîè îsk (a beautiful woman), apisuosî ykuîè apîæt (the beautiful children), apsatapæcuà apîætætîè apîæt (the beautiful houses).

The masculine singular, an adjective's basic form, is listed in dictionaries. Most feminine forms are formed by adding the prefix î- to the masculine form, e.g., hsuœcø > îhsuœcø, isîæt > îisîæt, suapœcîev > îsuapœcîev. 

Under certain circumstances, other minor changes occur in the formation of feminine forms. Specifically, masculine adjectives beginning with ætî-, ætæc-, sat-, sî-, apat- or apu- double their initial consonant before adding the prefix î- (e.g., ætîkœcq > îætætîkœcq, ætæcisîø > îætætæcisîø, satè > îssatè, sîæcqsu > îssîæcqsu, apatœcø > îapapatœcø, and apuè > îapapuè).

Additionally, adjectives beginning with q- change to îrq- (e.g., qsuætè > îrqsuætè); those beginning with œckî- or ykî- change to îapkî- (e.g., œckîiiîàatœcev > îapkîiiîàatœcev, ykîæcœcko > îapkîæcœcko), with the exception of the irregular ykîæcej (old) whose feminine form is îætætæcîæcej; ø- changes to îkø- (e.g., øsatæt > îkøsatæt); oæc- changes to îejæc- (e.g., oæciqu > îejæciqu); oî- changes to îejl- (e.g., oîœcè > îejlœcè); œcî- changes to îœcl- (e.g., œcîøsuœcix > îœcløsuœcix); iî- changes to îil- (e.g., iîæckzsæc > îilæckzsæc); and adjectives beginning with kat- have a special form ætat- (becoming îætætat- in feminine) that appears after u, î, æc, at, k, en, x, l and some occurrences of r, (e.g., kato/ætato > îætætato, katà/ætatà > îætætatà).

If an adjective's basic form beginning with î-, it does not change in the feminine (cf. îrqæcœc îààatr sk 'a rich man' > îrqæcœc îààîo îsk 'a rich woman').

The plural is normally formed by adding the prefix ap- to the singular (masculine and feminine; e.g., æcætatû > apæcætatû, îæcætatû > apîæcætatû). If the basic form beginning with ap-, y-, or ef-, an adjective does not change in the masculine plural (e.g., apuè > apuè, ykîœcxsxø > ykîœcxsxø, ykath > ykath), but its feminine plural form follows the rules detailed above. All Rqsîœco adjectives beginning with kuî- take the prefix y- in the masculine plural (e.g., kuîejkats > ykuîejkats). Distinctive plural forms occur with adjectives beginning with ætu-, which normally change to yku- in the masculine plural (e.g., ætusœcîejæcr > ykusœcîejæcr, ætuœcisîq > ykuœcisîq), with only two exceptions: ætuiuo > apætuiuo and ætuejus > apætuejus which follow the regular pattern. By contrast, the feminine plural is always formed according to the general rule: îætuœcisîq > apîætuœcisîq.

Adjective placement follows specific patterns. Most adjectives are placed after the noun they modify, and this is particularly true for colors, as in îøkatœc îæt sæcej (the red wine). However, certain short, commonly used adjectives – those dealing with beauty, age, goodness, or size (sometimes remembered by the acronym "BAGS") – typically precede their nouns. These are kuîè (beautiful), satè (good), oîœcè (brief), hsuœcø (big/tall), apatœcø (fat/large), ykuo (false), ikur (high), øsatæt (long), oîœcè (brief), îskîû (young), æcætatû (pretty), apæcuejkuà (bad), œckîætætæcîà (better), kuîejkats (new), iæciîev (small), ykîæcej (old); e.g., îààîo îsk îætætîè ("a beautiful woman").

PRONOUNS
--------
In Rqsîœco, pronouns are inflected to indicate their role in the sentence (subject, direct object, and so on), as well as to reflect the person, gender, and number of their referents. 

*Personal Pronouns
rqsîœco personal pronouns (analogous to English I, you, he/she, we, and they) reflect the person and number of their referent, and in the case of the third person, its gender as well. They also reflect the role they play in their clause: subject, direct object, indirect object, or other.

The personal pronouns change form to reflect the role they play in their clause. The forms used for subjects are called the subject pronouns, subjective pronouns, or nominative pronouns. They are as follows:

-----
VERBS
-----
Verbs in Rqsîœco are conjugated to reflect the following information:

    a mood (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, or conditional)
    a tense (past, present, or future, though not all tenses can be combined with all moods)
    an aspect (perfective or imperfective)
    a voice (active, passive, or reflexive)
    Nonfinite forms (e.g., participles, gerunds, infinitives)


Verbs in the finite moods (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, and conditional) are also conjugated to agree with their subjects in person (first, second, or third) and number (singular or plural). As in English, the subject must be included (except in the imperative mood); in other words Rqsîœco is neither a null-subject nor a pro-drop language.

Auxiliary verbs are combined with past participles of main verbs to produce compound tenses, including the compound past. For most main verbs the auxiliary is (the appropriate form of) œcæcateju ("to have"), but for reflexive verbs and certain intransitive verbs the auxiliary is a form of îœcid ("to be"). The participle agrees with the subject when the auxiliary is îœcid, and with a following direct object (if any) when the auxiliary is œcæcateju. Forms of îœcid are also used with the past participles of transitive verbs to form the passive voice.

*Morphology

In Rqsîœco, a verb is inflected to reflect its mood and tense, as well as to agree with its subject in person and number.

**Stems and conjugation prefixes

rqsîœco verbs have a large number of simple (one-word) forms. These are composed of two distinct parts: the stem (or root, or radix), which indicates which verb it is, and the prefix (inflection), which indicates the verb's tense (imperfect, present, future etc.) and mood and its subject's person (I, you, he/she etc.) and number, though many prefixes can correspond to multiple tense-mood-subject combinations. In certain parts of the second conjugation there is also a prefix -apapæc- between the stem and the ending.

    In isîæcuætœcuev, the stem -ætœcuev indicates that the verb is œcîætœcuev (to speak) and the prefix isîæcu- marks the third-person plural imperfect indicative. "Third person plural" meaning the subject of the verb is "they". The "imperfect indicative" being a tense.
    In apsatapapæcsæco, the stem -sæco indicates that the verb is œcæcsæco (to finish), the prefix -apapæc- precedes it, and the inflection apsat- marks the first-person plural present indicative or imperative. The "first-person plural" is the "we" form of a verb. The "present indicative" being a tense and "imperative" being a mood, but in Rqsîœco they are indistinguishable without context.

These verb conjugations are coupled with a subject pronoun in order to convey who the subject of the verb is (i.e. who is doing the action).

***The principle of the fixed stem

The stem normally stays fixed in the first two conjugations:

    œcîætœcuev: apæcuœcîætœcuev îû, apuætœcuev ki, isîapapuætœcuev apætæc'kz, apsatæcætœcuev apkats îkz, efîætœcuev...
    œcæcsæco: apæcuœcæcsæco îû, apîietsæco apkatej, isîapapæcsæco apætæc'kz, apæcsæco, apsatæcapapæcsæco apkats îkz...

In the third it is often modified, sometimes even between persons in the same tense:

    œcæcatætkatej: ykîej îû, ykîej ki, ikîej ætæc, apsatætkatej apkats, efîætkatej apkatej, isîætkîej apætæc.

But such irregularities apart, the principle is that nothing is removed from the stem. 


**Conjugation prefixes

The conjugation prefix tells us:

    For all verbs, the mood and the tense;
    For finite verbs, the person and the number; and
    For the past participle alone, the gender and the number.

Apart from a few frequent verbs which are considered totally irregular (mainly œcæcateju, îœcid, œcîætætu and îœcæcuo), for each tense of each mood a series of six prefixes (one for each person singular and plural) is associated with a group or subgroup of verbs.


*Formation of simple tenses active

These tenses are not formed with an auxiliary, and their formation is discussed in the following section.

**Infinitive

A verb is normally named by its present infinitive. Starting from this infinitive, the conjugations can be classified into three different groups:

    The first group or first conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with œcî- (with the exception of œcîætætu, which due to its numerous irregularities is usually classed as being in the third conjugation):

    œcîàæcu, œcîenuætuè, œcîisurq, œcîenatejsî, œcîàœcîo, œcîøsuà, œcîapapuev, œcîenuev, œcîsîàatœcev, œcîhœcuøîœc, etc.

    The second group or second conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with œcæc- whose present participle begins with isuapapæc-:

    The third group or third conjugation. This contains all the other verbs.

*Compound Tenses

rqsîœco compound tenses are verb forms that combine an auxiliary verb (either œcæcateju or îœcid) with the past participle of the main verb. These tenses are used to indicate actions that are completed or relate to another point in time. There are several compound tenses in Rqsîœco, each serving a specific purpose and adding nuance to the timeline of events.

**Compound Past

The compound past is perhaps the most commonly used compound tense in Rqsîœco. It is used to describe actions that have been completed in the past and is translated by the English simple past. The auxiliary verb is either œcæcateju or îœcid in the present tense, preceded by the past participle of the main verb. For example, "xøsuà æcu'û" (I ate) or "xejæcœcœcu iapî ætæc" (He arrived). œcæcateju is used with most verbs, while îœcid is used with a specific group of verbs, particularly those indicating movement or change of state, and with all reflexive verbs. When in doubt, œcæcateju should be used by default.

    hçèfanàñnàkuñ ofa oqnàmçè’ty (I love chocolate).

------------------------
ARTICLES AND DETERMINERS 
------------------------
In Kuñtàoqçà, articles and determiners are required on almost every common noun, much more so than in English. They are inflected to agree in gender (masculine or feminine) and number (singular or plural) with the noun they determine, though most have only one plural form (for masculine and feminine).

* Articles
kuñtàoqçà has three articles: a definite article, corresponding in many cases to English the; an indefinite article, corresponding to English a/an; and a partitive article, used roughly like some in English. 

** Definite article
 	
In Kuñtàoqçà, the definite article, analogously to the English word the, is used to indicate a specific noun. However, unlike English, the Kuñtàoqçà article changes based on the noun's gender (masculine or feminine) and number (singular or plural).

The definite article always comes after its noun.

For singular nouns:

- For masculine singular nouns, the article is ofa. For example, in the phrase "hçèkuñ ofa" (the cat), ofa shows that the noun hçèkuñ (cat) is both singular and masculine.
- For feminine singular nouns, the article is çèfa. An example is "tànàfuxçèé çèfa" (the house), where çèfa shows that tànàfuxçèé (house) is singular and feminine.

For plural nouns, regardless of gender:

- The article is fuofa for both masculine and feminine plural nouns. (e.g., "fuhçèkuñ fuofa", the cats; "futànàfuxçèé fuofa", the houses.)

In summary, ofa is used with masculine singular nouns, çèfa with feminine singular nouns, and fuofa with all plural nouns. This variation in definite articles reflects the grammatical gender and number of nouns in Kuñtàoqçà.

After çè, o, x, nà, wy, wu, va, nu and some occurrences of ku, the singular masculine article ofa becomes 'fa.


-----
NOUNS
-----
* Gender
Every Kuñtàoqçà noun has a grammatical gender, either masculine or feminine.

* Number
As in English, Kuñtàoqçà nouns inflect for number, however they do so through prefixation rather than suffixation.

The plural is usually formed from the singular by adding the prefix morpheme fu- (e.g., tànàfuxçèé > futànàfuxçèé 'houses'). 

Nouns beginning with wyçè- and wyo- take the prefix ça- instead of fu- (e.g., wyçèwuwyh > çawyçèwuwyh 'pipes', wyoty > çawyoty 'games'), except for the nouns wyçèmtàçèfa, wyçèqqçèfu, wyotàçy, and wyofag which form their plural by prefixing the morpheme fu- (e.g., wyotàçy > fuwyotàçy 'tires').

Seven nouns beginning with wynà- form their plural with ça-. These are wynàtàozu, wynàfafaxçèñ, wynàgxku, wynàtyxg, wynàçy, wynàkuñ, and wynàtywynàty (e.g., wynàtàozu > çawynàtàozu 'knees'). All other nouns beginning with wynà-, such as wynàfuxg or wynàqh, follow the regular plural pattern and take fu- (e.g., wynàqh > fuwynàqh 'holes').

Nouns that begin with fu-, ça- or p- in the singular do not change in the plural (e.g., çaxnàqñ çèfa 'the cross' > çaxnàqñ fuofa 'the crosses').

Nouns that begin with façè- typically change to çawyçè- in the plural (e.g., façètàqwynàty > çawyçètàqwynàty 'newspapers'). However, several nouns beginning with façè- are exceptions to this rule and form their plural by adding fu- instead. These are façèg, façèñ, façècaçètàqçèñ, façèñçèkuñ, façècaxhfuoçà, façèhxñvaq, façècaqofu and façèzuvaq (e.g., façècaxhfuoçà ofa > fufaçècaxhfuoçà fuofa).

Similarly, most nouns beginning with faxçè- change to çawyçè- in the plural. Examples of this pattern include faxçèg, faxçèqnàñ, faxçèéva, faxçèqxçywynàfu, faxçècaçèqh, and faxçèqhxca (e.g., faxçèqhxca tàwy > çawyçèqhxca fuom 'stained-glass windows'). However, some faxçè- nouns do not follow this pattern and form their plural with fu-, notably faxçèq, faxçèqxhhçè, faxçèmtàçèkuñ, faxçèhvam, faxçètàqocawynàzu and faxçèhqnàçy (e.g., faxçèq ofa > fufaxçèq fuofa 'the rails').

* Case
Nouns in Kuñtàoqçà are not inflected for any other grammatical categories. (However, personal pronouns are inflected for case and person.)

----------
Adjectives
----------

An adjective must agree in gender and number with the noun it modifies. Kuñtàoqçà adjectives therefore have four forms: masculine singular, feminine singular, masculine plural, and feminine plural. A few adjectives, like wyçèog and wyçèocawynàtà, have a fifth form, viz. an additional masculine singular form for use after a noun ending in çè, o, x, nà, wy, wu, va, nu and some occurrences of ku, e.g. tàxmqçèty wyçèog tàwy (a beautiful garden), oéénàku faog tàwy (a handsome man), oééoçà ofafaog otàwy (a beautiful woman), fuhtàçèçàtào çawyçèog fuofa (the beautiful children), futànàfuxçèé fuofafaog fuofa (the beautiful houses).

The masculine singular, an adjective's basic form, is listed in dictionaries. Most feminine forms are formed by adding the prefix o- to the masculine form, e.g., mtàçèqzu > omtàçèqzu, htàofa > ohtàofa, tàçèfuqoçy > otàçèfuqoçy. 

Under certain circumstances, other minor changes occur in the formation of feminine forms. Specifically, masculine adjectives beginning with fao-, fax-, tànà-, tào-, funà- or fuçè- double their initial consonant before adding the prefix o- (e.g., faowyqñ > ofafaowyqñ, faxhtàozu > ofafaxhtàozu, tànàg > otàtànàg, tàoxñtàçè > otàtàoxñtàçè, funàqzu > ofufunàqzu, and fuçèg > ofufuçèg).

Additionally, adjectives beginning with ñ- change to okuñ- (e.g., ñtàçèfag > okuñtàçèfag); those beginning with qwyo- or çawyo- change to ofuwyo- (e.g., qwyohhoénàqçy > ofuwyohhoénàqçy, çawyoxqwyçà > ofuwyoxqwyçà), with the exception of the irregular çawyoxca (old) whose feminine form is ofafaxoxca; zu- changes to owyzu- (e.g., zutànàfa > owyzutànàfa); çàx- changes to ocax- (e.g., çàxhñçè > ocaxhñçè); çào- changes to ocanu- (e.g., çàoqg > ocanuqg); qo- changes to oqnu- (e.g., qozutàçèqhva > oqnuzutàçèqhva); ho- changes to ohnu- (e.g., hoxwykètàx > ohnuxwykètàx); and adjectives beginning with wynà- have a special form fanà- (becoming ofafanà- in feminine) that appears after çè, o, x, nà, wy, wu, va, nu and some occurrences of ku, (e.g., wynàçà/fanàçà > ofafanàçà, wynàé/fanàé > ofafanàé).

If an adjective's basic form beginning with o-, it does not change in the feminine (cf. okuñxq oéénàku tàwy 'a rich man' > okuñxq oééoçà otàwy 'a rich woman').

The plural is normally formed by adding the prefix fu- to the singular (masculine and feminine; e.g., xfanàty > fuxfanàty, oxfanàty > fuoxfanàty). If the basic form beginning with fu-, ça-, or p-, an adjective does not change in the masculine plural (e.g., fuçèg > fuçèg, çawyoqvatàvazu > çawyoqvatàvazu, çawynàm > çawynàm), but its feminine plural form follows the rules detailed above. All Kuñtàoqçà adjectives beginning with wyçèo- take the prefix ça- in the masculine plural (e.g., wyçèocawynàtà > çawyçèocawynàtà). Distinctive plural forms occur with adjectives beginning with façè-, which normally change to çawyçè- in the masculine plural (e.g., façètàqocaxku > çawyçètàqocaxku, façèqhtàoñ > çawyçèqhtàoñ), with only two exceptions: façèhçèçà > fufaçèhçèçà and façècaçètà > fufaçècaçètà which follow the regular pattern. By contrast, the feminine plural is always formed according to the general rule: ofaçèqhtàoñ > fuofaçèqhtàoñ.

Adjective placement follows specific patterns. Most adjectives are placed after the noun they modify, and this is particularly true for colors, as in ozuwynàq ofa tàxca (the red wine). However, certain short, commonly used adjectives – those dealing with beauty, age, goodness, or size (sometimes remembered by the acronym "BAGS") – typically precede their nouns. These are wyçèog (beautiful), tànàg (good), çàoqg (brief), mtàçèqzu (big/tall), funàqzu (fat/large), çawyçèçà (false), hwyçèku (high), zutànàfa (long), çàoqg (brief), otàwyoty (young), xfanàty (pretty), fuxçècawyçèé (bad), qwyofafaxoé (better), wyçèocawynàtà (new), hxhoçy (small), çawyoxca (old); e.g., oééoçà otàwy ofafaog ("a beautiful woman").

--------
PRONOUNS
--------
In Kuñtàoqçà, pronouns are inflected to indicate their role in the sentence (subject, direct object, and so on), as well as to reflect the person, gender, and number of their referents. 

*Personal Pronouns
kuñtàoqçà personal pronouns (analogous to English I, you, he/she, we, and they) reflect the person and number of their referent, and in the case of the third person, its gender as well. They also reflect the role they play in their clause: subject, direct object, indirect object, or other.

The personal pronouns change form to reflect the role they play in their clause. The forms used for subjects are called the subject pronouns, subjective pronouns, or nominative pronouns. They are as follows: 

**Subject Pronouns
------------------------
Number   | Person           | Subject Pronoun
------------------------
Singular | 1st              | oty
         | 2nd (informal)   | wyh
         | 2nd (formal)     | fuwynàca
         | 3rd (masculine)  | fax
         | 3rd (feminine)   | ofafao
         | 3rd (neutral)    | tànà
------------------------
Plural   | 1st              | fuwynàtà
         | 2nd              | fuwynàca
         | 3rd (masculine)  | fufax
         | 3rd (feminine)   | fuofafao
------------------------

Note: Whenever the subject pronoun oty occurs after çè, o, x, nà, wy, wu, va, nu, ê and some occurrences of ku, it becomes 'ty.

-----
VERBS
-----
Verbs in Kuñtàoqçà are conjugated to reflect the following information:

    a mood (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, or conditional)
    a tense (past, present, or future, though not all tenses can be combined with all moods)
    an aspect (perfective or imperfective)
    a voice (active, passive, or reflexive)
    Nonfinite forms (e.g., participles, gerunds, infinitives)


Verbs in the finite moods (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, and conditional) are also conjugated to agree with their subjects in person (first, second, or third) and number (singular or plural). As in English, the subject must be included (except in the imperative mood); in other words Kuñtàoqçà is neither a null-subject nor a pro-drop language.

Auxiliary verbs are combined with past participles of main verbs to produce compound tenses, including the compound past. For most main verbs the auxiliary is (the appropriate form of) qxnàcaçè ("to have"), but for reflexive verbs and certain intransitive verbs the auxiliary is a form of oqhê ("to be"). The participle agrees with the subject when the auxiliary is oqhê, and with a following direct object (if any) when the auxiliary is qxnàcaçè. Forms of oqhê are also used with the past participles of transitive verbs to form the passive voice.

*Morphology

In Kuñtàoqçà, a verb is inflected to reflect its mood and tense, as well as to agree with its subject in person and number.

**Stems and conjugation prefixes

kuñtàoqçà verbs have a large number of simple (one-word) forms. These are composed of two distinct parts: the stem (or root, or radix), which indicates which verb it is, and the prefix (inflection), which indicates the verb's tense (imperfect, present, future etc.) and mood and its subject's person (I, you, he/she etc.) and number, though many prefixes can correspond to multiple tense-mood-subject combinations. In certain parts of the second conjugation there is also a prefix -fufux- between the stem and the ending.

    In htàoxçèfaqçèçy, the stem -faqçèçy indicates that the verb is qofaqçèçy (to speak) and the prefix htàoxçè- marks the third-person plural imperfect indicative. "Third person plural" meaning the subject of the verb is "they". The "imperfect indicative" being a tense.
    In futànàfufuxtàxçà, the stem -tàxçà indicates that the verb is qxtàxçà (to finish), the prefix -fufux- precedes it, and the inflection futànà- marks the first-person plural present indicative or imperative. The "first-person plural" is the "we" form of a verb. The "present indicative" being a tense and "imperative" being a mood, but in Kuñtàoqçà they are indistinguishable without context.

These verb conjugations are coupled with a subject pronoun in order to convey who the subject of the verb is (i.e. who is doing the action).

***The principle of the fixed stem

The stem normally stays fixed in the first two conjugations:

    qofaqçèçy: fuxçèqofaqçèçy oty, fuçèfaqçèçy wyh, htàofufuçèfaqçèçy fufax'wykè, futànàxfaqçèçy fuwynàtà owykè, pofaqçèçy...
    qxtàxçà: fuxçèqxtàxçà oty, fuohîtàxçà fuwynàca, htàofufuxtàxçà fufax'wykè, fuxtàxçà, futànàxfufuxtàxçà fuwynàtà owykè...

In the third it is often modified, sometimes even between persons in the same tense:

    qxnàfawynàca: çawyoca oty, çawyoca wyh, hwyoca fax, futànàfawynàca fuwynàtà, pofawynàca fuwynàca, htàofawyoca fufax.

But such irregularities apart, the principle is that nothing is removed from the stem. 


**Conjugation prefixes

The conjugation prefix tells us:

    For all verbs, the mood and the tense;
    For finite verbs, the person and the number; and
    For the past participle alone, the gender and the number.

Apart from a few frequent verbs which are considered totally irregular (mainly qxnàcaçè, oqhê, qofafaçè and oqxçèçà), for each tense of each mood a series of six prefixes (one for each person singular and plural) is associated with a group or subgroup of verbs.


*Formation of simple tenses active

These tenses are not formed with an auxiliary, and their formation is discussed in the following section.

**Infinitive

A verb is normally named by its present infinitive. Starting from this infinitive, the conjugations can be classified into three different groups:

    The first group or first conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with qo- (with the exception of qofafaçè, which due to its numerous irregularities is usually classed as being in the third conjugation):

    qoéxçè, qowuçèfaçèg, qohtàçèkuñ, qowunàcatào, qoéqoçà, qozutàçèé, qofufuçèçy, qowuçèçy, qotàoénàqçy, qomqçèzuoq, etc.

        For example, for the verb qofaqçèçy, the stem is -faqçèçy and the infinitive prefix is qo-.

    The second group or second conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with qx- whose present participle begins with htàçèfufux-:

    qxtàvag, qxhçèçyénàñ, qxçyqowyzuvam, qxqwyofaçà, qxmtàçèqzu, qïçèku, qxhfuocatàx, qxfanàçy, qxzuwynàq, qxzuwyq, qxfaçèfu, etc.

        For example, for the verb qxtàxçà, the stem is -tàxçà and the infinitive prefix is qx-.

    The third group or third conjugation. This contains all the other verbs.
    
Note that the auxiliaries oqhê and qxnàcaçè, although they would naturally seem to belong to the third conjugation, are traditionally classed separately. 

**Present indicative

The present indicative is the form of the verb used to describe an action in the present e.g. omqçèzuoq oty means "I watch".

The stem of the present indicative is not always regular and can vary (especially in the third conjugation) and there are three main sets of prefixes:

    Verbs beginning with qo- (all verbs of the first group): o-, fuo-, o-, futànà-, po-, htào-.
    Verbs beginning with qx- (all verbs of the second group and most of the third): fux-, fux-, hx-, futànàfufux-, pofufux-, htàofufux-. But there are numerous irregularities, especially in the third group.
    Verbs beginning with oq- (part of the third group): fu-, fu-, - , futànà-, po-, htào-.
    
    Example:

-------------------------------
1st person     | omqçèzuoq oty         | futànàmqçèzuoq fuwynàtà
2nd person     | fuomqçèzuoq wyh        | pomqçèzuoq fuwynàca
3rd person     | omqçèzuoq tànà/ofafao/fax | htàomqçèzuoq fuofafao/fufax
-------------------------------

-------------------------------

2nd person     | fuxfuxnàkuñ wyh         | pofufuxfuxnàkuñ fuwynàca
3rd person     | hxfuxnàkuñ tànà/ofafao/fax | htàofufuxfuxnàkuñ fuofafao/fufax

    Verbs of the second group take an -fufux- in the plural conjugations.
        
        
**Imperfect indicative

The imperfect indicative is a past tense describing states and actions that were ongoing in the past, e.g. "fuxçèmqçèzuoq oty" means "I was watching".

    The stem of the imperfect indicative is always invariant for a single verb. It is derived in various ways depending on the verb group.
    For the first group, the stem is the infinitive minus the qo- prefix, e.g., qomqçèzuoq -> -mqçèzuoq.
    For the second group, the stem is the infinitive minus the qx- prefix plus the fufux- prefix, e.g., qxfuxnàkuñ -> -fufuxfuxnàkuñ. 
    And for the third group, the stem is derived from the first person plural of the present indicative.

    The conjugation prefixes of this tense are for any of the three groups always: fuxçè-, fuxçè-, hxçè-, futànàx-, pox-, htàoxçè-.



    Example:

-------------------------------

2nd person     | fuxçèmqçèzuoq wyh         | poxmqçèzuoq fuwynàca
3rd person     | hxçèmqçèzuoq tànà/ofafao/fax | htàoxçèmqçèzuoq fuofafao/fufax
-------------------------------

-------------------------------

2nd person     | fuxçèfufuxfuxnàkuñ wyh        | poxfufuxfuxnàkuñ fuwynàca
3rd person     | hxçèfufuxfuxnàkuñ tànà/ofafao/fax | htàoxçèfufuxfuxnàkuñ fuofafao/fufax
-------------------------------



    Verb oqhê : the stem is -hva, endings are the same.
    

**Future

The future prefixes correspond to the present indicative of the verb qxnàcaçè. They are always regular: xçè-, fuçè-, çè-, futànà-, po-, htànà-.

    The future stem is simply the infinitive (dictionary form). In other words, to form the future tense these prefixes are added to the infinitive:

        xçèqxfuxnàkuñ oty ('I will choose'), fuçèqomqçèzuoq wyh ('you will watch'), çèqxhqnàfu ofafao ('she will exit'), futànàqofafaxçècaçèqh fuwynàtà ('we will work'), poqxzuwynàq fuwynàca ('you will blush'), htànàqxhqçèçy fufax ('they will leave').

    But there are several irregular future stems, especially in the third group.

**Past participle

Past participles, unlike present participles and gerundives, may be inflected to show gender and number by adding o- and fu- prefixes, as with a normal adjective. Hence, "hxçàtànàñ hxwyqçà tàwy", "ohxçàtànàñ oqxnàçy otàwy", "fuhxçàtànàñ fuhxwyqçà fuom", and "fuohxçàtànàñ fuoqxnàçy fuom."

The plain (masculine singular) form of a past participle begins with va- for the 1st group verbs, and with x- for the 2nd group verbs. ----------
WORD ORDER
----------

The most common word order in Bésxkàçèg is the rare object-verb-subject (OVS).

ARTICLES AND DETERMINERS 
------------------------
In Bésxkàçèg, articles and determiners are required on almost every common noun, much more so than in English. They are inflected to agree in gender (masculine or feminine) and number (singular or plural) with the noun they determine, though most have only one plural form (for masculine and feminine).

* Articles
bésxkàçèg has three articles: a definite article, corresponding in many cases to English the; an indefinite article, corresponding to English a/an; and a partitive article, used roughly like some in English. 

** Definite article
 	
In Bésxkàçèg, the definite article, analogously to the English word the, is used to indicate a specific noun. However, unlike English, the Bésxkàçèg article changes based on the noun's gender (masculine or feminine) and number (singular or plural).

The definite article always comes after its noun.

For singular nouns:

- For masculine singular nouns, the article is kèn. For example, in the phrase "aubés kèn" (the cat), kèn shows that the noun aubés (cat) is both singular and masculine.
- For feminine singular nouns, the article is uèn. An example is "xpvzut uèn" (the house), where uèn shows that xpvzut (house) is singular and feminine.

For plural nouns, regardless of gender:

- The article is vkèn for both masculine and feminine plural nouns. (e.g., "vaubés vkèn", the cats; "vxpvzut vkèn", the houses.)

In summary, kèn is used with masculine singular nouns, uèn with feminine singular nouns, and vkèn with all plural nouns. This variation in definite articles reflects the grammatical gender and number of nouns in Bésxkàçèg.

After u, k, z, p, yw, h, àw, yg and some occurrences of b, the singular masculine article kèn becomes 'èn.

NOUNS
-----
* Gender
Every Bésxkàçèg noun has a grammatical gender, either masculine or feminine.

* Number
As in English, Bésxkàçèg nouns inflect for number, however they do so through prefixation rather than suffixation.

The plural is usually formed from the singular by adding the prefix morpheme v- (e.g., xpvzut > vxpvzut 'houses'). 

Nouns beginning with ywu- and ywk- take the prefix él- instead of v- (e.g., ywuhywa > élywuhywa 'pipes', ywkm > élywkm 'games'), except for the nouns ywuèdxuèn, ywuàçàçuv, ywkxàc, and ywkènéc which form their plural by prefixing the morpheme v- (e.g., ywkxàc > vywkxàc 'tires').

Seven nouns beginning with ywp- form their plural with él-. These are ywpxkiq, ywpènènzués, ywpéczb, ywpmzéc, ywpàc, ywpbés, and ywpmywpm (e.g., ywpxkiq > élywpxkiq 'knees'). All other nouns beginning with ywp-, such as ywpvzéc or ywpàça, follow the regular plural pattern and take v- (e.g., ywpàça > vywpàça 'holes').

Nouns that begin with v-, él- or ig- in the singular do not change in the plural (e.g., élzpàçés uèn 'the cross' > élzpàçés vkèn 'the crosses').

Nouns that begin with ènu- typically change to élywu- in the plural (e.g., ènuxàçywpm > élywuxàçywpm 'newspapers'). However, several nouns beginning with ènu- are exceptions to this rule and form their plural by adding v- instead. These are ènuéc, ènués, ènueuxàçués, ènuésubés, ènuezavkèg, ènuazésàwàç, ènueàçkv and ènuiqàwàç (e.g., ènuezavkèg kèn > vènuezavkèg vkèn).

Similarly, most nouns beginning with ènzu- change to élywu- in the plural. Examples of this pattern include ènzuéc, ènzuàçpés, ènzutàw, ènzuàçzàcywpv, ènzueuàça, and ènzuàçaze (e.g., ènzuàçaze xyw > élywuàçaze vkèd 'stained-glass windows'). * Case
Nouns in Bésxkàçèg are not inflected for any other grammatical categories. (However, personal pronouns are inflected for case and person.)

An adjective must agree in gender and number with the noun it modifies. Bésxkàçèg adjectives therefore have four forms: masculine singular, feminine singular, masculine plural, and feminine plural. Verbs in Bésxkàçèg are conjugated to reflect the following information:

    an aspect (perfective or imperfective)

    Nonfinite forms (e.g., participles, gerunds, infinitives)


Verbs in the finite moods (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, and conditional) are also conjugated to agree with their subjects in person (first, second, or third) and number (singular or plural). Auxiliary verbs are combined with past participles of main verbs to produce compound tenses, including the compound past. The participle agrees with the subject when the auxiliary is kàçaê, and with a following direct object (if any) when the auxiliary is àçzpeu. Forms of kàçaê are also used with the past participles of transitive verbs to form the passive voice.

*Morphology
