The plural is usually formed from the singular by adding the prefix morpheme k- (e.g., açaxklét > kaçaxklét 'houses'). 

Nouns beginning with ucé- and ucèx- take the prefix b- instead of k- (e.g., ucégucd > bucégucd 'pipes', ucèxaz > bucèxaz 'games'), except for the nouns ucéeaçéèz, ucénnék, ucèxaçj, and ucèxèzs which form their plural by prefixing the morpheme k- (e.g., ucèxaçj > kucèxaçj 'tires').

Seven nouns beginning with ucax- form their plural with b-. These are ucaxaçèxf, ucaxèzèzléaw, ucaxslèc, ucaxazls, ucaxj, ucaxècaw, and ucaxazucaxaz (e.g., ucaxaçèxf > bucaxaçèxf 'knees'). All other nouns beginning with ucax-, such as ucaxkls or ucaxnd, follow the regular plural pattern and take k- (e.g., ucaxnd > kucaxnd 'holes').

Nouns that begin with k-, b- or àw- in the singular do not change in the plural (e.g., blaxnaw éèz 'the cross' > blaxnaw kèxèz 'the crosses').

Nouns that begin with èzé- typically change to bucé- in the plural (e.g., èzéaçnucaxaz > bucéaçnucaxaz 'newspapers'). However, several nouns beginning with èzé- are exceptions to this rule and form their plural by adding k- instead. These are èzés, èzéaw, èzéiéaçnéaw, èzéawéècaw, èzéildkèxux, èzédlawhn, èzéinèxk and èzéfhn (e.g., èzéildkèxux èxèz > kèzéildkèxux kèxèz).

Similarly, most nouns beginning with èzlé- change to bucé- in the plural. Examples of this pattern include èzlés, èzlénaxaw, èzléth, èzlénljucaxk, èzléiénd, and èzléndli (e.g., èzléndli açuc > bucéndli kèxe 'stained-glass windows'). However, some èzlé- nouns do not follow this pattern and form their plural with k-, notably èzlén, èzlénlddé, èzléeaçéècaw, èzlédhe, èzléaçnèxiucaxf and èzlédnaxj (e.g., èzlén èxèz > kèzlén kèxèz 'the rails').

* Case
Nouns in Ècawaçèxnux are not inflected for any other grammatical categories. (However, personal pronouns are inflected for case and person.)

----------
Adjectives
----------

An adjective must agree in gender and number with the noun it modifies. Ècawaçèxnux adjectives therefore have four forms: masculine singular, feminine singular, masculine plural, and feminine plural. A few adjectives, like ucéèxs and ucéèxiucaxaç, have a fifth form, viz. an additional masculine singular form for use after a noun ending in é, èx, l, ax, uc, g, h, up and some occurrences of èc, e.g. açlenéaz ucéèxs açuc (a beautiful garden), èxttaxèc èzèxs açuc (a handsome man), èxttèxux èxèzèzèxs èxaçuc (a beautiful woman), kdaçéuxaçèx bucéèxs kèxèz (the beautiful children), kaçaxklét kèxèzèzèxs kèxèz (the beautiful houses).

The masculine singular, an adjective's basic form, is listed in dictionaries. Most feminine forms are formed by adding the prefix èx- to the masculine form, e.g., eaçénf > èxeaçénf, daçèxèz > èxdaçèxèz, açéknèxj > èxaçéknèxj. 

Under certain circumstances, other minor changes occur in the formation of feminine forms. Specifically, masculine adjectives beginning with èzèx-, èzl-, açax-, açèx-, kax- or ké- double their initial consonant before adding the prefix èx- (e.g., èzèxucnaw > èxèzèzèxucnaw, èzldaçèxf > èxèzèzldaçèxf, açaxs > èxaçaçaxs, açèxlawaçé > èxaçaçèxlawaçé, kaxnf > èxkkaxnf, and kés > èxkkés).

Additionally, adjectives beginning with aw- change to èxècaw- (e.g., awaçéèzs > èxècawaçéèzs); those beginning with nucèx- or bucèx- change to èxkucèx- (e.g., nucèxddèxtaxnj > èxkucèxddèxtaxnj, bucèxlnucux > èxkucèxlnucux), with the exception of the irregular bucèxli (old) whose feminine form is èxèzèzlèxli; f- changes to èxucf- (e.g., façaxèz > èxucfaçaxèz); uxl- changes to èxil- (e.g., uxldawé > èxildawé); uxèx- changes to èxiup- (e.g., uxèxns > èxiupns); nèx- changes to èxnup- (e.g., nèxfaçéndh > èxnupfaçéndh); dèx- changes to èxdup- (e.g., dèxlucoaçl > èxduplucoaçl); and adjectives beginning with ucax- have a special form èzax- (becoming èxèzèzax- in feminine) that appears after é, èx, l, ax, uc, g, h, up and some occurrences of èc, (e.g., ucaxux/èzaxux > èxèzèzaxux, ucaxt/èzaxt > èxèzèzaxt).

If an adjective's basic form beginning with èx-, it does not change in the feminine (cf. èxècawln èxttaxèc açuc 'a rich man' > èxècawln èxttèxux èxaçuc 'a rich woman').

The plural is normally formed by adding the prefix k- to the singular (masculine and feminine; e.g., lèzaxaz > klèzaxaz, èxlèzaxaz > kèxlèzaxaz). If the basic form beginning with k-, b-, or àw-, an adjective does not change in the masculine plural (e.g., kés > kés, bucèxnhaçhf > bucèxnhaçhf, bucaxe > bucaxe), but its feminine plural form follows the rules detailed above. All Ècawaçèxnux adjectives beginning with ucéèx- take the prefix b- in the masculine plural (e.g., ucéèxiucaxaç > bucéèxiucaxaç). Distinctive plural forms occur with adjectives beginning with èzé-, which normally change to bucé- in the masculine plural (e.g., èzéaçnèxilèc > bucéaçnèxilèc, èzéndaçèxaw > bucéndaçèxaw), with only two exceptions: èzédéux > kèzédéux and èzéiéaç > kèzéiéaç which follow the regular pattern. By contrast, the feminine plural is always formed according to the general rule: èxèzéndaçèxaw > kèxèzéndaçèxaw.

Adjective placement follows specific patterns. Most adjectives are placed after the noun they modify, and this is particularly true for colors, as in èxfucaxn èxèz açli (the red wine). However, certain short, commonly used adjectives – those dealing with beauty, age, goodness, or size (sometimes remembered by the acronym "BAGS") – typically precede their nouns. These are ucéèxs (beautiful), açaxs (good), uxèxns (brief), eaçénf (big/tall), kaxnf (fat/large), bucéux (false), ducéèc (high), façaxèz (long), uxèxns (brief), èxaçucèxaz (young), lèzaxaz (pretty), kléiucét (bad), nucèxèzèzlèxt (better), ucéèxiucaxaç (new), dldèxj (small), bucèxli (old); e.g., èxttèxux èxaçuc èxèzèzèxs ("a beautiful woman").

--------
PRONOUNS
--------
In Ècawaçèxnux, pronouns are inflected to indicate their role in the sentence (subject, direct object, and so on), as well as to reflect the person, gender, and number of their referents. 

*Personal Pronouns
ècawaçèxnux personal pronouns (analogous to English I, you, he/she, we, and they) reflect the person and number of their referent, and in the case of the third person, its gender as well. They also reflect the role they play in their clause: subject, direct object, indirect object, or other.

The personal pronouns change form to reflect the role they play in their clause. The forms used for subjects are called the subject pronouns, subjective pronouns, or nominative pronouns. They are as follows: 

**Subject Pronouns
------------------------
Number   | Person           | Subject Pronoun
------------------------
Singular | 1st              | èxaz
         | 2nd (informal)   | ucd
         | 2nd (formal)     | kucaxi
         | 3rd (masculine)  | èzl
         | 3rd (feminine)   | èxèzèzèx
         | 3rd (neutral)    | açax
------------------------
Plural   | 1st              | kucaxaç
         | 2nd              | kucaxi
         | 3rd (masculine)  | kèzl
         | 3rd (feminine)   | kèxèzèzèx
------------------------

Note: Whenever the subject pronoun èxaz occurs after é, èx, l, ax, uc, g, h, up, ê and some occurrences of èc, it becomes 'az.

-----
VERBS
-----
Verbs in Ècawaçèxnux are conjugated to reflect the following information:

    a mood (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, or conditional)
    a tense (past, present, or future, though not all tenses can be combined with all moods)
    an aspect (perfective or imperfective)
    a voice (active, passive, or reflexive)
    Nonfinite forms (e.g., participles, gerunds, infinitives)


Verbs in the finite moods (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, and conditional) are also conjugated to agree with their subjects in person (first, second, or third) and number (singular or plural). As in English, the subject must be included (except in the imperative mood); in other words Ècawaçèxnux is neither a null-subject nor a pro-drop language.

Auxiliary verbs are combined with past participles of main verbs to produce compound tenses, including the compound past. For most main verbs the auxiliary is (the appropriate form of) nlaxié ("to have"), but for reflexive verbs and certain intransitive verbs the auxiliary is a form of èxndê ("to be"). The participle agrees with the subject when the auxiliary is èxndê, and with a following direct object (if any) when the auxiliary is nlaxié. Forms of èxndê are also used with the past participles of transitive verbs to form the passive voice.

*Morphology

In Ècawaçèxnux, a verb is inflected to reflect its mood and tense, as well as to agree with its subject in person and number.

**Stems and conjugation prefixes

ècawaçèxnux verbs have a large number of simple (one-word) forms. These are composed of two distinct parts: the stem (or root, or radix), which indicates which verb it is, and the prefix (inflection), which indicates the verb's tense (imperfect, present, future etc.) and mood and its subject's person (I, you, he/she etc.) and number, though many prefixes can correspond to multiple tense-mood-subject combinations. In certain parts of the second conjugation there is also a prefix -kkl- between the stem and the ending.

    In daçèxléèznéj, the stem -èznéj indicates that the verb is nèxèznéj (to speak) and the prefix daçèxlé- marks the third-person plural imperfect indicative. "Third person plural" meaning the subject of the verb is "they". The "imperfect indicative" being a tense.
    In kaçaxkklaçlux, the stem -açlux indicates that the verb is nlaçlux (to finish), the prefix -kkl- precedes it, and the inflection kaçax- marks the first-person plural present indicative or imperative. The "first-person plural" is the "we" form of a verb. The "present indicative" being a tense and "imperative" being a mood, but in Ècawaçèxnux they are indistinguishable without context.

These verb conjugations are coupled with a subject pronoun in order to convey who the subject of the verb is (i.e. who is doing the action).

***The principle of the fixed stem

The stem normally stays fixed in the first two conjugations:

    nèxèznéj: klénèxèznéj èxaz, kéèznéj ucd, daçèxkkéèznéj kèzl'uco, kaçaxlèznéj kucaxaç èxuco, àwèxèznéj...
    nlaçlux: klénlaçlux èxaz, kèxdîaçlux kucaxi, daçèxkklaçlux kèzl'uco, klaçlux, kaçaxlkklaçlux kucaxaç èxuco...

In the third it is often modified, sometimes even between persons in the same tense:

    nlaxèzucaxi: bucèxi èxaz, bucèxi ucd, ducèxi èzl, kaçaxèzucaxi kucaxaç, àwèxèzucaxi kucaxi, daçèxèzucèxi kèzl.

But such irregularities apart, the principle is that nothing is removed from the stem. 


**Conjugation prefixes

The conjugation prefix tells us:

    For all verbs, the mood and the tense;
    For finite verbs, the person and the number; and
    For the past participle alone, the gender and the number.

Apart from a few frequent verbs which are considered totally irregular (mainly nlaxié, èxndê, nèxèzèzé and èxnléux), for each tense of each mood a series of six prefixes (one for each person singular and plural) is associated with a group or subgroup of verbs.


*Formation of simple tenses active

These tenses are not formed with an auxiliary, and their formation is discussed in the following section.

**Infinitive

A verb is normally named by its present infinitive. Starting from this infinitive, the conjugations can be classified into three different groups:

    The first group or first conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with nèx- (with the exception of nèxèzèzé, which due to its numerous irregularities is usually classed as being in the third conjugation):

    nèxtlé, nèxgéèzés, nèxdaçéècaw, nèxgaxiaçèx, nèxtnèxux, nèxfaçét, nèxkkéj, nèxgéj, nèxaçèxtaxnj, nèxenéfèxn, etc.

        For example, for the verb nèxèznéj, the stem is -èznéj and the infinitive prefix is nèx-.

    The second group or second conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with nl- whose present participle begins with daçékkl-:

    nlaçhs, nldéjtaxaw, nljnèxucfhe, nlnucèxèzux, nleaçénf, nïéèc, nldkèxiaçl, nlèzaxj, nlfucaxn, nlfucn, nlèzék, etc.

        For example, for the verb nlaçlux, the stem is -açlux and the infinitive prefix is nl-.

    The third group or third conjugation. This contains all the other verbs.
    
Note that the auxiliaries èxndê and nlaxié, although they would naturally seem to belong to the third conjugation, are traditionally classed separately. 

**Present indicative

The present indicative is the form of the verb used to describe an action in the present e.g. èxenéfèxn èxaz means "I watch".

The stem of the present indicative is not always regular and can vary (especially in the third conjugation) and there are three main sets of prefixes:

    Verbs beginning with nèx- (all verbs of the first group): èx-, kèx-, èx-, kaçax-, àwèx-, daçèx-.
    Verbs beginning with nl- (all verbs of the second group and most of the third): kl-, kl-, dl-, kaçaxkkl-, àwèxkkl-, daçèxkkl-. But there are numerous irregularities, especially in the third group.
    Verbs beginning with èxn- (part of the third group): k-, k-, - , kaçax-, àwèx-, daçèx-.

**Imperfect indicative

The imperfect indicative is a past tense describing states and actions that were ongoing in the past, e.g. "kléenéfèxn èxaz" means "I was watching".

    The conjugation prefixes of this tense are for any of the three groups always: klé-, klé-, dlé-, kaçaxl-, àwèxl-, daçèxlé-.

**Past participle

Past participles, unlike present participles and gerundives, may be inflected to show gender and number by adding èx- and k- prefixes, as with a normal adjective. Hence, "dluxaçaxaw dlucnux açuc", "èxdluxaçaxaw èxnlaxj èxaçuc", "kdluxaçaxaw kdlucnux kèxe", and "kèxdluxaçaxaw kèxnlaxj kèxe."

The plain (masculine singular) form of a past participle begins with h- for the 1st group verbs, and with l- for the 2nd group verbs. Third group verbs have more diverse prefixes : uc- (èxneaçèxdaçèx uceaçèxdaçèx, èxnlaxs ucs, èxnlèz ucèz, etc. and nlaxiék uck, nlaxi uci, nlaxiucaxj ucj), kl- (èxnddèxt klt, èxneaçèxnj klnj, etc.), kuc- (èxnucèzawaçl kucèzawaçl and èxnucèzawèxn kucèzawèxn and only these verbs), dl- (èxnleucét dleucét, èxnle dle, etc.), d- (verbs in èxneaçl- : èxneaçlèxj daçlèxj), dnèx- (nlniucax dnèxiucax, nlniucaxaw dnèxiucaxaw, nlnuxuxax dnèxuxuxax and nlnuxuxucaxk dnèxuxuxucaxk), or ucèx (nlaxié ucèx). 

*Compound Tenses

ècawaçèxnux compound tenses are verb forms that combine an auxiliary verb (either nlaxié or èxndê) with the past participle of the main verb. These tenses are used to indicate actions that are completed or relate to another point in time. There are several compound tenses in Ècawaçèxnux, each serving a specific purpose and adding nuance to the timeline of events.

**Compound Past

The compound past is perhaps the most commonly used compound tense in Ècawaçèxnux. It is used to describe actions that have been completed in the past and is translated by the English simple past. The auxiliary verb is either nlaxié or èxndê in the present tense, preceded by the past participle of the main verb. For example, "hfaçét lé'az" (I ate) or "hilnné dkèx èzl" (He arrived). nlaxié is used with most verbs, while èxndê is used with a specific group of verbs, particularly those indicating movement or change of state, and with all reflexive verbs. When in doubt, nlaxié should be used by default.

Person         | Singular                     | Plural
-------------------------------
1st person     | henéfèxn lé'az               | henéfèxn kaçaxié kucaxaç

In Dècugmyi, articles and determiners are required on almost every common noun, much more so than in English. * Articles

** Definite article
 	
In Dècugmyi, the definite article, analogously to the English word the, is used to indicate a specific noun. However, unlike English, the Dècugmyi article changes based on the noun's gender (masculine or feminine) and number (singular or plural).

The definite article always comes after its noun.

After pà, g, s, mo, l, kè, r, f and some occurrences of dè, the singular masculine article ghè becomes 'hè.

Under certain circumstances, other minor changes occur in the formation of feminine forms. Specifically, masculine adjectives beginning with myqy-, myv-, qàþ-, qàqy-, ñyþ- or ñyqi- double their initial consonant before adding the prefix qy- (e.g., myqytymimà > qymymyqytymimà, myvdqàqye > qymymyvdqàqye, qàþno > qyqàqàþno, qàqyvmàqàqi > qyqàqàqyvmàqàqi, ñyþmie > qyñyñyþmie, and ñyqino > qyñyñyqino).

Additionally, adjectives beginning with mà- change to qykmà- (e.g., màqàqimyno > qykmàqàqimyno); those beginning with mityqy- or totyqy- change to qyñytyqy- (e.g., mityqyddqysoþmia > qyñytyqyddqysoþmia, totyqyvmitymu > qyñytyqyvmitymu), with the exception of the irregular totyqyvf (old) whose feminine form is qymymyvqyvf; e- changes to qytye- (e.g., eqàþmy > qytyeqàþmy); muv- changes to qyfv- (e.g., muvdmàqi > qyfvdmàqi); muqy- changes to qyfni- (e.g., muqymino > qyfnimino); miqy- changes to qymini- (e.g., miqyeqàqimidj > qyminieqàqimidj); dqy- changes to qydni- (e.g., dqyvtycqàv > qydnivtycqàv); and adjectives beginning with tyþ- have a special form myþ- (becoming qymymyþ- in feminine) that appears after qi, qy, v, þ, ty, ho, j, ni and some occurrences of k, (e.g., tyþmu/myþmu > qymymyþmu, tyþso/myþso > qymymyþso).

If an adjective's basic form beginning with qy-, it does not change in the feminine (cf. qykmàvmi qysosoþk qàty 'a rich man' > qykmàvmi qysosoqymu qyqàty 'a rich woman').

The plural is normally formed by adding the prefix ñy- to the singular (masculine and feminine; e.g., vmyþqu > ñyvmyþqu, qyvmyþqu > ñyqyvmyþqu). If the basic form beginning with ñy-, to-, or xu-, an adjective does not change in the masculine plural (e.g., ñyqino > ñyqino, totyqymijqàje > totyqymijqàje, totyþsu > totyþsu), but its feminine plural form follows the rules detailed above. All Kmàqàqymimu adjectives beginning with tyqiqy- take the prefix to- in the masculine plural (e.g., tyqiqyftyþqà > totyqiqyftyþqà). Distinctive plural forms occur with adjectives beginning with myqi-, which normally change to totyqi- in the masculine plural (e.g., myqiqàmiqyfvk > totyqiqàmiqyfvk, myqimidqàqymà > totyqimidqàqymà), with only two exceptions: myqidqimu > ñymyqidqimu and myqifqiqà > ñymyqifqiqà which follow the regular pattern. By contrast, the feminine plural is always formed according to the general rule: qymyqimidqàqymà > ñyqymyqimidqàqymà.

Adjective placement follows specific patterns. Most adjectives are placed after the noun they modify, and this is particularly true for colors, as in qyetyþmi qymy qàvf (the red wine). However, certain short, commonly used adjectives – those dealing with beauty, age, goodness, or size (sometimes remembered by the acronym "BAGS") – typically precede their nouns. These are tyqiqyno (beautiful), qàþno (good), muqymino (brief), suqàqimie (big/tall), ñyþmie (fat/large), totyqimu (false), dtyqik (high), eqàþmy (long), muqymino (brief), qyqàtyqyqu (young), vmyþqu (pretty), ñyvqiftyqiso (bad), mityqymymyvqyso (better), tyqiqyftyþqà (new), dvdqya (small), totyqyvf (old); e.g., qysosoqymu qyqàty qymymyqyno ("a beautiful woman").

--------
PRONOUNS
--------
In Kmàqàqymimu, pronouns are inflected to indicate their role in the sentence (subject, direct object, and so on), as well as to reflect the person, gender, and number of their referents. 

*Personal Pronouns
kmàqàqymimu personal pronouns (analogous to English I, you, he/she, we, and they) reflect the person and number of their referent, and in the case of the third person, its gender as well. They also reflect the role they play in their clause: subject, direct object, indirect object, or other.

The personal pronouns change form to reflect the role they play in their clause. The forms used for subjects are called the subject pronouns, subjective pronouns, or nominative pronouns. They are as follows: 

**Subject Pronouns
------------------------
Number   | Person           | Subject Pronoun
------------------------
Singular | 1st              | qyqu
         | 2nd (informal)   | tyd
         | 2nd (formal)     | ñytyþf
         | 3rd (masculine)  | myv
         | 3rd (feminine)   | qymymyqy
         | 3rd (neutral)    | qàþ
------------------------
Plural   | 1st              | ñytyþqà
         | 2nd              | ñytyþf
         | 3rd (masculine)  | ñymyv
         | 3rd (feminine)   | ñyqymymyqy
------------------------

Note: Whenever the subject pronoun qyqu occurs after qi, qy, v, þ, ty, ho, j, ni, ê and some occurrences of k, it becomes 'qu.

-----
VERBS
-----
Verbs in Kmàqàqymimu are conjugated to reflect the following information:

    a mood (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, or conditional)
    a tense (past, present, or future, though not all tenses can be combined with all moods)
    an aspect (perfective or imperfective)
    a voice (active, passive, or reflexive)
    Nonfinite forms (e.g., participles, gerunds, infinitives)


Verbs in the finite moods (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, and conditional) are also conjugated to agree with their subjects in person (first, second, or third) and number (singular or plural). As in English, the subject must be included (except in the imperative mood); in other words Kmàqàqymimu is neither a null-subject nor a pro-drop language.

Auxiliary verbs are combined with past participles of main verbs to produce compound tenses, including the compound past. For most main verbs the auxiliary is (the appropriate form of) mivþfqi ("to have"), but for reflexive verbs and certain intransitive verbs the auxiliary is a form of qymidê ("to be"). The participle agrees with the subject when the auxiliary is qymidê, and with a following direct object (if any) when the auxiliary is mivþfqi. Forms of qymidê are also used with the past participles of transitive verbs to form the passive voice.

*Morphology

In Kmàqàqymimu, a verb is inflected to reflect its mood and tense, as well as to agree with its subject in person and number.

**Stems and conjugation prefixes

kmàqàqymimu verbs have a large number of simple (one-word) forms. These are composed of two distinct parts: the stem (or root, or radix), which indicates which verb it is, and the prefix (inflection), which indicates the verb's tense (imperfect, present, future etc.) and mood and its subject's person (I, you, he/she etc.) and number, though many prefixes can correspond to multiple tense-mood-subject combinations. In certain parts of the second conjugation there is also a prefix -ñyñyv- between the stem and the ending.

    In dqàqyvqimymiqia, the stem -mymiqia indicates that the verb is miqymymiqia (to speak) and the prefix dqàqyvqi- marks the third-person plural imperfect indicative. "Third person plural" meaning the subject of the verb is "they". The "imperfect indicative" being a tense.
    In ñyqàþñyñyvqàvmu, the stem -qàvmu indicates that the verb is mivqàvmu (to finish), the prefix -ñyñyv- precedes it, and the inflection ñyqàþ- marks the first-person plural present indicative or imperative. The "first-person plural" is the "we" form of a verb. The "present indicative" being a tense and "imperative" being a mood, but in Kmàqàqymimu they are indistinguishable without context.

These verb conjugations are coupled with a subject pronoun in order to convey who the subject of the verb is (i.e. who is doing the action).

***The principle of the fixed stem

The stem normally stays fixed in the first two conjugations:

    miqymymiqia: ñyvqimiqymymiqia qyqu, ñyqimymiqia tyd, dqàqyñyñyqimymiqia ñymyv'tyc, ñyqàþvmymiqia ñytyþqà qytyc, xuqymymiqia...
    mivqàvmu: ñyvqimivqàvmu qyqu, ñyqydîqàvmu ñytyþf, dqàqyñyñyvqàvmu ñymyv'tyc, ñyvqàvmu, ñyqàþvñyñyvqàvmu ñytyþqà qytyc...

In the third it is often modified, sometimes even between persons in the same tense:

    mivþmytyþf: totyqyf qyqu, totyqyf tyd, dtyqyf myv, ñyqàþmytyþf ñytyþqà, xuqymytyþf ñytyþf, dqàqymytyqyf ñymyv.

But such irregularities apart, the principle is that nothing is removed from the stem. 


**Conjugation prefixes

The conjugation prefix tells us:

    For all verbs, the mood and the tense;
    For finite verbs, the person and the number; and
    For the past participle alone, the gender and the number.

Apart from a few frequent verbs which are considered totally irregular (mainly mivþfqi, qymidê, miqymymyqi and qymivqimu), for each tense of each mood a series of six prefixes (one for each person singular and plural) is associated with a group or subgroup of verbs.


*Formation of simple tenses active

These tenses are not formed with an auxiliary, and their formation is discussed in the following section.

**Infinitive

A verb is normally named by its present infinitive. Starting from this infinitive, the conjugations can be classified into three different groups:

    The first group or first conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with miqy- (with the exception of miqymymyqi, which due to its numerous irregularities is usually classed as being in the third conjugation):

    miqysovqi, miqyhoqimyqino, miqydqàqikmà, miqyhoþfqàqy, miqysomiqymu, miqyeqàqiso, miqyñyñyqia, miqyhoqia, miqyqàqysoþmia, miqysumiqieqymi, etc.

        For example, for the verb miqymymiqia, the stem is -mymiqia and the infinitive prefix is miqy-.

    The second group or second conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with miv- whose present participle begins with dqàqiñyñyv-:

    mivqàjno, mivdqiasoþmà, mivamiqytyejsu, mivmityqymymu, mivsuqàqimie, miïqik, mivdñyqyfqàv, mivmyþa, mivetyþmi, mivetymi, mivmyqiñy, etc.

        For example, for the verb mivqàvmu, the stem is -qàvmu and the infinitive prefix is miv-.

    The third group or third conjugation. This contains all the other verbs.
    
Note that the auxiliaries qymidê and mivþfqi, although they would naturally seem to belong to the third conjugation, are traditionally classed separately. 

**Present indicative

The present indicative is the form of the verb used to describe an action in the present e.g. qysumiqieqymi qyqu means "I watch".

The stem of the present indicative is not always regular and can vary (especially in the third conjugation) and there are three main sets of prefixes:

    Verbs beginning with miqy- (all verbs of the first group): qy-, ñyqy-, qy-, ñyqàþ-, xuqy-, dqàqy-.
    Verbs beginning with miv- (all verbs of the second group and most of the third): ñyv-, ñyv-, dv-, ñyqàþñyñyv-, xuqyñyñyv-, dqàqyñyñyv-. But there are numerous irregularities, especially in the third group.
    Verbs beginning with qymi- (part of the third group): ñy-, ñy-, - , ñyqàþ-, xuqy-, dqàqy-.
    
    Example:

**Imperfect indicative

The imperfect indicative is a past tense describing states and actions that were ongoing in the past, e.g. "ñyvqisumiqieqymi qyqu" means "I was watching".

    The stem of the imperfect indicative is always invariant for a single verb. It is derived in various ways depending on the verb group.
    For the first group, the stem is the infinitive minus the miqy- prefix, e.g., miqysumiqieqymi -> -sumiqieqymi.
    For the second group, the stem is the infinitive minus the miv- prefix plus the ñyñyv- prefix, e.g., mivñyvþkmà -> -ñyñyvñyvþkmà. 
    And for the third group, the stem is derived from the first person plural of the present indicative.

    The conjugation prefixes of this tense are for any of the three groups always: ñyvqi-, ñyvqi-, dvqi-, ñyqàþv-, xuqyv-, dqàqyvqi-.

**Future

The future prefixes correspond to the present indicative of the verb mivþfqi. They are always regular: vqi-, ñyqi-, qi-, ñyqàþ-, xuqy-, dqàþ-.

    The future stem is simply the infinitive (dictionary form). In other words, to form the future tense these prefixes are added to the infinitive:

        vqimivñyvþkmà qyqu ('I will choose'), ñyqimiqysumiqieqymi tyd ('you will watch'), qimivdmiþñy qymymyqy ('she will exit'), ñyqàþmiqymymyvqifqimid ñytyþqà ('we will work'), xuqymivetyþmi ñytyþf ('you will blush'), dqàþmivdmiqia ñymyv ('they will leave').

**Past participle

Past participles, unlike present participles and gerundives, may be inflected to show gender and number by adding qy- and ñy- prefixes, as with a normal adjective. Hence, "dvmuqàþmà dvtymimu qàty", "qydvmuqàþmà qymivþa qyqàty", "ñydvmuqàþmà ñydvtymimu ñyqysu", and "ñyqydvmuqàþmà ñyqymivþa ñyqysu."

The plain (masculine singular) form of a past participle begins with j- for the 1st group verbs, and with v- for the 2nd group verbs. Third group verbs have more diverse prefixes : ty- (qymisuqàqydqàqy tysuqàqydqàqy, qymivþno tyno, qymivmy tymy, etc. and mivþfqiñy tyñy, mivþf tyf, mivþftyþa tya), ñyv- (qymiddqyso ñyvso, qymisuqàqymia ñyvmia, etc.), ñyty- (qymitymymàqàv ñytymymàqàv and qymitymymàqymi ñytymymàqymi and only these verbs), dv- (qymivsutyqiso dvsutyqiso, qymivsu dvsu, etc.), d- (verbs in qymisuqàv- : qymisuqàvqya dqàvqya), dmiqy- (mivmiftyþ dmiqyftyþ, mivmiftyþmà dmiqyftyþmà, mivmimumuþ dmiqymumuþ and mivmimumutyþñy dmiqymumutyþñy), or tyqy (mivþfqi tyqy). 

*Compound Tenses

kmàqàqymimu compound tenses are verb forms that combine an auxiliary verb (either mivþfqi or qymidê) with the past participle of the main verb. These tenses are used to indicate actions that are completed or relate to another point in time. There are several compound tenses in Kmàqàqymimu, each serving a specific purpose and adding nuance to the timeline of events.

**Compound Past

The compound past is perhaps the most commonly used compound tense in Kmàqàqymimu. It is used to describe actions that have been completed in the past and is translated by the English simple past. The auxiliary verb is either mivþfqi or qymidê in the present tense, preceded by the past participle of the main verb. For example, "jeqàqiso vqi'qu" (I ate) or "jfvmimiqi dñyqy myv" (He arrived). mivþfqi is used with most verbs, while qymidê is used with a specific group of verbs, particularly those indicating movement or change of state, and with all reflexive verbs. When in doubt, mivþfqi should be used by default.

These are qganru (beautiful), çarèru (good), inloru (brief), çuçagaloja (big/tall), xrèloja (fat/large), moqgai (false), zqgaju (high), jaçarèçà (long), inloru (brief), nçaqnsè (young), soçàrèsè (pretty), xsogatqgagè (bad), loqnçàçàsongè (better), qgantqrèça (new), zsoznjo (small), moqnsot (old); e.g., ngègèni nçaq nçàçànru ("a beautiful woman").

PRONOUNS
--------
In Jupçanloi, pronouns are inflected to indicate their role in the sentence (subject, direct object, and so on), as well as to reflect the person, gender, and number of their referents. 

*Personal Pronouns
jupçanloi personal pronouns (analogous to English I, you, he/she, we, and they) reflect the person and number of their referent, and in the case of the third person, its gender as well. They also reflect the role they play in their clause: subject, direct object, indirect object, or other.

The personal pronouns change form to reflect the role they play in their clause. The forms used for subjects are called the subject pronouns, subjective pronouns, or nominative pronouns. They are as follows: 

**Subject Pronouns
------------------------
Number   | Person           | Subject Pronoun
------------------------
Singular | 1st              | nsè
         | 2nd (informal)   | qz
         | 2nd (formal)     | xqrèt
         | 3rd (masculine)  | çàso
         | 3rd (feminine)   | nçàçàn
         | 3rd (neutral)    | çarè
------------------------
Plural   | 1st              | xqrèça
         | 2nd              | xqrèt
         | 3rd (masculine)  | xçàso
         | 3rd (feminine)   | xnçàçàn
------------------------

Note: Whenever the subject pronoun nsè occurs after ga, n, so, rè, q, b, y, f, ê and some occurrences of ju, it becomes 'sè.

*Relative pronouns

jupçanloi, like English, uses relative pronouns to link relative clauses to their head nouns, except that in Jupçanloi, as in Amharic for instance, the relative clause precedes its head and the relative pronoun, this is why we speak of "head noun" rather than of an "antecedent." The relative pronoun used depends on its grammatical role (such as subject or direct object) within the relative clause.

If the relative pronoun is to be the subject of the relative clause's verb, soqhà is ordinarily used: nzznçàpbpsoru gagè yçàrèt ga soqhà ngègèrèju'çà ("the man who stole my bike"). Note that soqhà in this use does not change form to agree in any way with its head noun: xnyçàrèt yzy zçarè soqhà xnzznçàpbpsoru xnçà ("the bikes that were stolen").

If the relative pronoun is to be the direct object of the relative clause's verb, nqhà (or 'qhà after ga, n, so, rè, q, b, y, f, ê and some occurrences of ju) is ordinarily used: nyçàrèt ga çàso'qhà nzznçàpbpsoru gaçà ("the bicycle that he stole"). Like soqhà, nqhà does not change form to agree with its head noun.

VERBS
-----
Verbs in Jupçanloi are conjugated to reflect the following information:

    a mood (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, or conditional)
    a tense (past, present, or future, though not all tenses can be combined with all moods)
    an aspect (perfective or imperfective)
    a voice (active, passive, or reflexive)
    Nonfinite forms (e.g., participles, gerunds, infinitives)


Verbs in the finite moods (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, and conditional) are also conjugated to agree with their subjects in person (first, second, or third) and number (singular or plural). As in English, the subject must be included (except in the imperative mood); in other words Jupçanloi is neither a null-subject nor a pro-drop language.

Auxiliary verbs are combined with past participles of main verbs to produce compound tenses, including the compound past. For most main verbs the auxiliary is (the appropriate form of) losorètga ("to have"), but for reflexive verbs and certain intransitive verbs the auxiliary is a form of nlozê ("to be"). The participle agrees with the subject when the auxiliary is nlozê, and with a following direct object (if any) when the auxiliary is losorètga. Forms of nlozê are also used with the past participles of transitive verbs to form the passive voice.

*Morphology

In Jupçanloi, a verb is inflected to reflect its mood and tense, as well as to agree with its subject in person and number.

**Stems and conjugation prefixes

jupçanloi verbs have a large number of simple (one-word) forms. These are composed of two distinct parts: the stem (or root, or radix), which indicates which verb it is, and the prefix (inflection), which indicates the verb's tense (imperfect, present, future etc.) and mood and its subject's person (I, you, he/she etc.) and number, though many prefixes can correspond to multiple tense-mood-subject combinations. In certain parts of the second conjugation there is also a prefix -xxso- between the stem and the ending.

    In zçansogaçàlogajo, the stem -çàlogajo indicates that the verb is lonçàlogajo (to speak) and the prefix zçansoga- marks the third-person plural imperfect indicative. "Third person plural" meaning the subject of the verb is "they". The "imperfect indicative" being a tense.
    In xçarèxxsoçasoi, the stem -çasoi indicates that the verb is losoçasoi (to finish), the prefix -xxso- precedes it, and the inflection xçarè- marks the first-person plural present indicative or imperative. The "first-person plural" is the "we" form of a verb. The "present indicative" being a tense and "imperative" being a mood, but in Jupçanloi they are indistinguishable without context.

These verb conjugations are coupled with a subject pronoun in order to convey who the subject of the verb is (i.e. who is doing the action).

***The principle of the fixed stem

The stem normally stays fixed in the first two conjugations:

    lonçàlogajo: xsogalonçàlogajo nsè, xgaçàlogajo qz, zçanxxgaçàlogajo xçàso'qhà, xçarèsoçàlogajo xqrèça nqhà, dnçàlogajo...
    losoçasoi: xsogalosoçasoi nsè, xnzîçasoi xqrèt, zçanxxsoçasoi xçàso'qhà, xsoçasoi, xçarèsoxxsoçasoi xqrèça nqhà...

In the third it is often modified, sometimes even between persons in the same tense:

    losorèçàqrèt: moqnt nsè, moqnt qz, zqnt çàso, xçarèçàqrèt xqrèça, dnçàqrèt xqrèt, zçançàqnt xçàso.

But such irregularities apart, the principle is that nothing is removed from the stem. 


**Conjugation prefixes

The conjugation prefix tells us:

    For all verbs, the mood and the tense;
    For finite verbs, the person and the number; and
    For the past participle alone, the gender and the number.

Apart from a few frequent verbs which are considered totally irregular (mainly losorètga, nlozê, lonçàçàga and nlosogai), for each tense of each mood a series of six prefixes (one for each person singular and plural) is associated with a group or subgroup of verbs.


*Formation of simple tenses active

These tenses are not formed with an auxiliary, and their formation is discussed in the following section.

**Infinitive

A verb is normally named by its present infinitive. Starting from this infinitive, the conjugations can be classified into three different groups:

    The first group or first conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with lon- (with the exception of lonçàçàga, which due to its numerous irregularities is usually classed as being in the third conjugation):

    longèsoga, lonbgaçàgaru, lonzçagajup, lonbrètçan, longèloni, lonjaçagagè, lonxxgajo, lonbgajo, lonçangèrèlojo, lonçulogajanlo, etc.

        For example, for the verb lonçàlogajo, the stem is -çàlogajo and the infinitive prefix is lon-.

    The second group or second conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with loso- whose present participle begins with zçagaxxso-:

    losoçayru, losozgajogèrèp, losojolonqjayçu, losoloqnçài, losoçuçagaloja, loïgaju, losozxntçaso, losoçàrèjo, losojaqrèlo, losojaqlo, losoçàgax, etc.

        For example, for the verb losoçasoi, the stem is -çasoi and the infinitive prefix is loso-.

    The third group or third conjugation. This contains all the other verbs.
    
Note that the auxiliaries nlozê and losorètga, although they would naturally seem to belong to the third conjugation, are traditionally classed separately. 

**Present indicative

The present indicative is the form of the verb used to describe an action in the present e.g. nçulogajanlo nsè means "I watch".

The stem of the present indicative is not always regular and can vary (especially in the third conjugation) and there are three main sets of prefixes:

**Past participle

Past participles, unlike present participles and gerundives, may be inflected to show gender and number by adding n- and x- prefixes, as with a normal adjective. Hence, "zsoiçarèp zsoqloi çaq", "nzsoiçarèp nlosorèjo nçaq", "xzsoiçarèp xzsoqloi xnçu", and "xnzsoiçarèp xnlosorèjo xnçu."

The plain (masculine singular) form of a past participle begins with y- for the 1st group verbs, and with so- for the 2nd group verbs. Third group verbs have more diverse prefixes : q- (nloçuçanzçan qçuçanzçan, nlosorèru qru, nlosoçà qçà, etc. and losorètgax qx, losorèt qt, losorètqrèjo qjo), xso- (nlozzngè xsogè, nloçuçanlojo xsolojo, etc.), xq- (nloqçàpçaso xqçàpçaso and nloqçàpnlo xqçàpnlo and only these verbs), zso- (nlosoçuqgagè zsoçuqgagè, nlosoçu zsoçu, etc.), z- (verbs in nloçuçaso- : nloçuçasonjo zçasonjo), zlon- (losolotqrè zlontqrè, losolotqrèp zlontqrèp, losoloiirè zloniirè and losoloiiqrèx zloniiqrèx), or qn (losorètga qn). 

*Compound Tenses

jupçanloi compound tenses are verb forms that combine an auxiliary verb (either losorètga or nlozê) with the past participle of the main verb. These tenses are used to indicate actions that are completed or relate to another point in time. There are several compound tenses in Jupçanloi, each serving a specific purpose and adding nuance to the timeline of events.

**Compound Past

The compound past is perhaps the most commonly used compound tense in Jupçanloi. It is used to describe actions that have been completed in the past and is translated by the English simple past. The auxiliary verb is either losorètga or nlozê in the present tense, preceded by the past participle of the main verb. For example, "yjaçagagè soga'sè" (I ate) or "ytsolologa zxn çàso" (He arrived). losorètga is used with most verbs, while nlozê is used with a specific group of verbs, particularly those indicating movement or change of state, and with all reflexive verbs. When in doubt, losorètga should be used by default.

*Past participle agreement

The past participle is used in three ways in Jupçanloi: as an adjective, in the passive construction, and in the compound tense constructions. When it is used as an adjective, it follows all the regular adjective agreement rules. In passive constructions, it always agrees with the passive subject.

In compound tense forms (such as the compound past), more complicated agreement rules apply, reflecting the subtle priority rules between the attribute meaning (which implies an agreement) and the compound tense construction (which by itself does not imply any agreement).

A. The auxiliary verb is losorètga.

    If there is no direct object (the verb is intransitive) or the direct object appears before the past participle, then the past participle does not agree (i.e., it takes the default masculine singular form).
        (intransitive) sogèlorèçu zçarè xnçàçàn. ("They (fem.) slept.")
        (direct object before verb) xnçasonçàgaru moqnçu qt ga nlosogaçàp. ("nlosogaçàp saw two whales.")
    If there is a direct object and it appears after the past participle, then the participle must agree with it. Three cases:
        (pronoun after the auxiliary) xnçasonçàgaru moqnçu zsogatga b çàso. xnqt ga xnçà nlosogaçàp. ("There were two whales. nlosogaçàp saw them.")
        (clause-final wh-question element)  xnqt nçàçàn-z-ga nlosogaçàp xnçasonçàgaru xnçàçànqhà? ("Which whales did nlosogaçàp see?")
        (relative clause linked by nqhà) xnqt ga nlosogaçàp nqhà xnçasonçàgaru moqnçu xnçà ("the two whales that nlosogaçàp saw")
    The above rule is one of the most difficult in Jupçanloi.

B. The auxiliary is nlozê, and the verb is not reflexive. The past participle agrees with the subject:

        xnytsolologa zçarèx xnçàçàn. ("They (fem.) arrived.")

C. The auxiliary is nlozê and the verb is reflexive. The agreement rules are in fact the same as those for structures with losorètga in A, keeping in mind that the reflexive pronoun corresponds to either the direct object or the indirect object of the verb.

    There is no direct object, or the direct object appears before the past participle → no agreement. In these cases, the reflexive pronoun expresses the indirect object.
        (no direct object) yçuyppqx zçarèx nx xnçàçàn. yçàlogajo xngègèrèx xqrèça xqrèça. ("They (fem.) succeeded one another. We spoke with each other.")
        (direct object before verb) xçarèsozxnqhà xnçu yxrèjo zçarèx nx xnçàçàn. ("They (fem.) asked each other some questions.")
        
    There is a direct object and it appears after the past participle. → The past participle agrees with this object.

    The first three cases are the same as in A.2 above (the reflexive pronoun is the indirect object).
        (direct object pronoun) nzlogaz nçaq zsogai soga'sè. nyjagazlogajo zçarèx gaçà nx xzçagaiçan xnçà. ("I made a pie. The children shared it.")
        (wh-question)  nyjagazlogajo xçàso-zçarèx nx nzlogaz nçàçànqhà? ("Which pie did they share?")
        (nqhà relative) nyjagazlogajo zçarèx nx xzçagaiçan xnçà nqhà nzlogaz gaçà ("the pie that the children shared")

    The reflexive pronoun can itself be the direct object, in which case the participle agrees with it (and therefore with the subject). This also includes "inherently reflexive" verbs, for which the reflexive pronoun cannot be interpreted semantically as an object (direct or indirect) of the verb.
        (ordinary reflexive) xnsotsoqx zçarèx nx xnçàçàn. xyqçàgax xngègèrèx xqrèça xqrèça. ("They (fem.) followed each other. We greeted each other.")
        (inherently reflexive) sorègè nçu xyqhàrègè zçarèx nx xçàso. zçangènçayty'çà nçu xqçantqrèx xngègèrèx xqrèça xqrèça. ("They made fun of me. We remembered the event.")

The plural is normally formed by adding the prefix lè- to the singular (masculine and feminine; e.g., vkêd > lèvkêd, gvkêd > lègvkêd). If the basic form beginning with lè-, cè-, or cœ-, an adjective does not change in the masculine plural (e.g., lèmupè > lèmupè, cètigçuæxæjœ > cètigçuæxæjœ, cètiêté > cètiêté), but its feminine plural form follows the rules detailed above. All Hcixgçuî adjectives beginning with timug- take the prefix cè- in the masculine plural (e.g., timugmètiêx > cètimugmètiêx). Distinctive plural forms occur with adjectives beginning with kmu-, which normally change to cètimu- in the masculine plural (e.g., kmuxçugmèvh > cètimuxçugmèvh, kmuçuûxgci > cètimuçuûxgci), with only two exceptions: kmuûmuî > lèkmuûmuî and kmumèmux > lèkmumèmux which follow the regular pattern. By contrast, the feminine plural is always formed according to the general rule: gkmuçuûxgci > lègkmuçuûxgci.

Adjective placement follows specific patterns. Most adjectives are placed after the noun they modify, and this is particularly true for colors, as in gjœtiêçu gk xvmè (the red wine). However, certain short, commonly used adjectives – those dealing with beauty, age, goodness, or size (sometimes remembered by the acronym "BAGS") – typically precede their nouns. These are timugpè (beautiful), xêpè (good), îgçupè (brief), téxmuçujœ (big/tall), lèêçujœ (fat/large), cètimuî (false), ûtimuh (high), jœxêk (long), îgçupè (brief), gxtigd (young), vkêd (pretty), lèvmumètimuñu (bad), çutigkkvgñu (better), timugmètiêx (new), ûvûgcu (small), cètigvmè (old); e.g., gñuñugî gxti gkkgpè ("a beautiful woman").

--------
PRONOUNS
--------
In Hcixgçuî, pronouns are inflected to indicate their role in the sentence (subject, direct object, and so on), as well as to reflect the person, gender, and number of their referents. 

*Personal Pronouns
hcixgçuî personal pronouns (analogous to English I, you, he/she, we, and they) reflect the person and number of their referent, and in the case of the third person, its gender as well. They also reflect the role they play in their clause: subject, direct object, indirect object, or other.

The personal pronouns change form to reflect the role they play in their clause. The forms used for subjects are called the subject pronouns, subjective pronouns, or nominative pronouns. They are as follows: 

**Subject Pronouns
------------------------
Number   | Person           | Subject Pronoun
------------------------
Singular | 1st              | gd
         | 2nd (informal)   | tiû
         | 2nd (formal)     | lètiêmè
         | 3rd (masculine)  | kv
         | 3rd (feminine)   | gkkg
         | 3rd (neutral)    | xê
------------------------
Plural   | 1st              | lètiêx
         | 2nd              | lètiêmè
         | 3rd (masculine)  | lèkv
         | 3rd (feminine)   | lègkkg
------------------------

Note: Whenever the subject pronoun gd occurs after mu, g, v, ê, ti, lœ, æ, e, z and some occurrences of h, it becomes 'd.

*Relative pronouns

hcixgçuî, like English, uses relative pronouns to link relative clauses to their head nouns, except that in Hcixgçuî, as in Amharic for instance, the relative clause precedes its head and the relative pronoun, this is why we speak of "head noun" rather than of an "antecedent." The relative pronoun used depends on its grammatical role (such as subject or direct object) within the relative clause.

If the relative pronoun is to be the subject of the relative clause's verb, vticé is ordinarily used: gûûgkcilœcivpè muñu ækêmè mu vticé gñuñuêh'k ("the man who stole my bike"). Note that vticé in this use does not change form to agree in any way with its head noun: lègækêmè æûæ ûxê vticé lègûûgkcilœcivpè lègk ("the bikes that were stolen").

If the relative pronoun is to be the direct object of the relative clause's verb, gticé (or 'ticé after mu, g, v, ê, ti, lœ, æ, e, z and some occurrences of h) is ordinarily used: gækêmè mu kv'ticé gûûgkcilœcivpè muk ("the bicycle that he stole"). Like vticé, gticé does not change form to agree with its head noun.


-----
VERBS
-----
Verbs in Hcixgçuî are conjugated to reflect the following information:

    a mood (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, or conditional)
    a tense (past, present, or future, though not all tenses can be combined with all moods)
    an aspect (perfective or imperfective)
    a voice (active, passive, or reflexive)
    Nonfinite forms (e.g., participles, gerunds, infinitives)


Verbs in the finite moods (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, and conditional) are also conjugated to agree with their subjects in person (first, second, or third) and number (singular or plural). As in English, the subject must be included (except in the imperative mood); in other words Hcixgçuî is neither a null-subject nor a pro-drop language.

Auxiliary verbs are combined with past participles of main verbs to produce compound tenses, including the compound past. For most main verbs the auxiliary is (the appropriate form of) çuvêmèmu ("to have"), but for reflexive verbs and certain intransitive verbs the auxiliary is a form of gçuûz ("to be"). The participle agrees with the subject when the auxiliary is gçuûz, and with a following direct object (if any) when the auxiliary is çuvêmèmu. Forms of gçuûz are also used with the past participles of transitive verbs to form the passive voice.

*Morphology

In Hcixgçuî, a verb is inflected to reflect its mood and tense, as well as to agree with its subject in person and number.

**Stems and conjugation prefixes

hcixgçuî verbs have a large number of simple (one-word) forms. These are composed of two distinct parts: the stem (or root, or radix), which indicates which verb it is, and the prefix (inflection), which indicates the verb's tense (imperfect, present, future etc.) and mood and its subject's person (I, you, he/she etc.) and number, though many prefixes can correspond to multiple tense-mood-subject combinations. In certain parts of the second conjugation there is also a prefix -lèlèv- between the stem and the ending.

    In ûxgvmukçumucu, the stem -kçumucu indicates that the verb is çugkçumucu (to speak) and the prefix ûxgvmu- marks the third-person plural imperfect indicative. "Third person plural" meaning the subject of the verb is "they". The "imperfect indicative" being a tense.
    In lèxêlèlèvxvî, the stem -xvî indicates that the verb is çuvxvî (to finish), the prefix -lèlèv- precedes it, and the inflection lèxê- marks the first-person plural present indicative or imperative. The "first-person plural" is the "we" form of a verb. The "present indicative" being a tense and "imperative" being a mood, but in Hcixgçuî they are indistinguishable without context.

These verb conjugations are coupled with a subject pronoun in order to convey who the subject of the verb is (i.e. who is doing the action).

***The principle of the fixed stem

The stem normally stays fixed in the first two conjugations:

    çugkçumucu: lèvmuçugkçumucu gd, lèmukçumucu tiû, ûxglèlèmukçumucu lèkv'ticé, lèxêvkçumucu lètiêx gticé, cœgkçumucu...
    çuvxvî: lèvmuçuvxvî gd, lègûñixvî lètiêmè, ûxglèlèvxvî lèkv'ticé, lèvxvî, lèxêvlèlèvxvî lètiêx gticé...

In the third it is often modified, sometimes even between persons in the same tense:

    çuvêktiêmè: cètigmè gd, cètigmè tiû, ûtigmè kv, lèxêktiêmè lètiêx, cœgktiêmè lètiêmè, ûxgktigmè lèkv.

But such irregularities apart, the principle is that nothing is removed from the stem. 


**Conjugation prefixes

The conjugation prefix tells us:

    For all verbs, the mood and the tense;
    For finite verbs, the person and the number; and
    For the past participle alone, the gender and the number.

Apart from a few frequent verbs which are considered totally irregular (mainly çuvêmèmu, gçuûz, çugkkmu and gçuvmuî), for each tense of each mood a series of six prefixes (one for each person singular and plural) is associated with a group or subgroup of verbs.


*Formation of simple tenses active

These tenses are not formed with an auxiliary, and their formation is discussed in the following section.

**Infinitive

A verb is normally named by its present infinitive. Starting from this infinitive, the conjugations can be classified into three different groups:

    The first group or first conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with çug- (with the exception of çugkkmu, which due to its numerous irregularities is usually classed as being in the third conjugation):

    çugñuvmu, çuglœmukmupè, çugûxmuhci, çuglœêmèxg, çugñuçugî, çugjœxmuñu, çuglèlèmucu, çuglœmucu, çugxgñuêçucu, çugtéçumujœgçu, etc.

        For example, for the verb çugkçumucu, the stem is -kçumucu and the infinitive prefix is çug-.

    The second group or second conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with çuv- whose present participle begins with ûxmulèlèv-:

    çuvxæpè, çuvûmucuñuêci, çuvcuçugtijœæté, çuvçutigkî, çuvtéxmuçujœ, çuïmuh, çuvûlègmèxv, çuvkêcu, çuvjœtiêçu, çuvjœtiçu, çuvkmulè, etc.

        For example, for the verb çuvxvî, the stem is -xvî and the infinitive prefix is çuv-.

    The third group or third conjugation. This contains all the other verbs.
    
Note that the auxiliaries gçuûz and çuvêmèmu, although they would naturally seem to belong to the third conjugation, are traditionally classed separately. 

**Present indicative

The present indicative is the form of the verb used to describe an action in the present e.g. gtéçumujœgçu gd means "I watch".

The stem of the present indicative is not always regular and can vary (especially in the third conjugation) and there are three main sets of prefixes:

    Verbs beginning with çug- (all verbs of the first group): g-, lèg-, g-, lèxê-, cœg-, ûxg-.
    Verbs beginning with çuv- (all verbs of the second group and most of the third): lèv-, lèv-, ûv-, lèxêlèlèv-, cœglèlèv-, ûxglèlèv-. But there are numerous irregularities, especially in the third group.
    Verbs beginning with gçu- (part of the third group): lè-, lè-, - , lèxê-, cœg-, ûxg-.

**Imperfect indicative

The imperfect indicative is a past tense describing states and actions that were ongoing in the past, e.g. "lèvmutéçumujœgçu gd" means "I was watching".

    The stem of the imperfect indicative is always invariant for a single verb. It is derived in various ways depending on the verb group.

    And for the third group, the stem is derived from the first person plural of the present indicative.

    The conjugation prefixes of this tense are for any of the three groups always: lèvmu-, lèvmu-, ûvmu-, lèxêv-, cœgv-, ûxgvmu-.

**Past participle

Past participles, unlike present participles and gerundives, may be inflected to show gender and number by adding g- and lè- prefixes, as with a normal adjective. Hence, "ûvîxêci ûvtiçuî xti", "gûvîxêci gçuvêcu gxti", "lèûvîxêci lèûvtiçuî lègté", and "lègûvîxêci lègçuvêcu lègté."

The plain (masculine singular) form of a past participle begins with æ- for the 1st group verbs, and with v- for the 2nd group verbs. Third group verbs have more diverse prefixes : ti- (gçutéxgûxg titéxgûxg, gçuvêpè tipè, gçuvk tik, etc. and çuvêmèmulè tilè, çuvêmè timè, çuvêmètiêcu ticu), lèv- (gçuûûgñu lèvñu, gçutéxgçucu lèvçucu, etc.), lèti- (gçutikcixv lètikcixv and gçutikcigçu lètikcigçu and only these verbs), ûv- (gçuvtétimuñu ûvtétimuñu, gçuvté ûvté, etc.), û- (verbs in gçutéxv- : gçutéxvgcu ûxvgcu), ûçug- (çuvçumètiê ûçugmètiê, çuvçumètiêci ûçugmètiêci, çuvçuîîê ûçugîîê and çuvçuîîtiêlè ûçugîîtiêlè), or tig (çuvêmèmu tig). 

*Compound Tenses

hcixgçuî compound tenses are verb forms that combine an auxiliary verb (either çuvêmèmu or gçuûz) with the past participle of the main verb. These tenses are used to indicate actions that are completed or relate to another point in time. There are several compound tenses in Hcixgçuî, each serving a specific purpose and adding nuance to the timeline of events.

**Compound Past

The compound past is perhaps the most commonly used compound tense in Hcixgçuî. It is used to describe actions that have been completed in the past and is translated by the English simple past. The auxiliary verb is either çuvêmèmu or gçuûz in the present tense, preceded by the past participle of the main verb. For example, "æjœxmuñu vmu'd" (I ate) or "æmèvçuçumu ûlèg kv" (He arrived). çuvêmèmu is used with most verbs, while gçuûz is used with a specific group of verbs, particularly those indicating movement or change of state, and with all reflexive verbs. When in doubt, çuvêmèmu should be used by default.

*Past participle agreement

The past participle is used in three ways in Hcixgçuî: as an adjective, in the passive construction, and in the compound tense constructions. When it is used as an adjective, it follows all the regular adjective agreement rules. In passive constructions, it always agrees with the passive subject.

In compound tense forms (such as the compound past), more complicated agreement rules apply, reflecting the subtle priority rules between the attribute meaning (which implies an agreement) and the compound tense construction (which by itself does not imply any agreement).

A. The auxiliary verb is çuvêmèmu.

    If there is no direct object (the verb is intransitive) or the direct object appears before the past participle, then the past participle does not agree (i.e., it takes the default masculine singular form).
        (intransitive) vñuçuêté ûxê lègkkg. ("They (fem.) slept.")
        (direct object before verb) lègxvgkmupè cètigté timè mu gçuvmukci. ("gçuvmukci saw two whales.")
    If there is a direct object and it appears after the past participle, then the participle must agree with it. Three cases:
        (pronoun after the auxiliary) lègxvgkmupè cètigté ûvmumèmu lœ kv. lègtimè mu lègk gçuvmukci. ("There were two whales. gçuvmukci saw them.")
        (clause-final wh-question element)  lègtimè gkkg-û-mu gçuvmukci lègxvgkmupè lègkkgticé? ("Which whales did gçuvmukci see?")
        (relative clause linked by gticé) lègtimè mu gçuvmukci gticé lègxvgkmupè cètigté lègk ("the two whales that gçuvmukci saw")
    The above rule is one of the most difficult in Hcixgçuî.

B. The auxiliary is gçuûz, and the verb is not reflexive. The past participle agrees with the subject:

        lègæmèvçuçumu ûxêlè lègkkg. ("They (fem.) arrived.")

C. The auxiliary is gçuûz and the verb is reflexive. The agreement rules are in fact the same as those for structures with çuvêmèmu in A, keeping in mind that the reflexive pronoun corresponds to either the direct object or the indirect object of the verb.

    There is no direct object, or the direct object appears before the past participle → no agreement. In these cases, the reflexive pronoun expresses the indirect object.
        (no direct object) ætéæcicitilè ûxêlè glè lègkkg. ækçumucu lègñuñuêlè lètiêx lètiêx. ("They (fem.) succeeded one another. We spoke with each other.")

All other nouns beginning with qma-, such as qmazeyx or qmawçi, follow the regular plural pattern and take ze- (e.g., qmawçi > zeqmawçi 'holes').

Nouns that begin with ze-, gé- or p- in the singular do not change in the plural (e.g., géymawr sézi 'the cross' > géymawr zebazi 'the crosses').

Nouns that begin with zisé- typically change to géqsé- in the plural (e.g., ziséçèwqmada > géqséçèwqmada 'newspapers'). However, several nouns beginning with zisé- are exceptions to this rule and form their plural by adding ze- instead. These are ziséx, zisér, ziséhéséçèwsér, zisérséàr, ziséhéyçizebasè, ziséçiyrgèw, ziséhéwbaze and zisélgèw (e.g., ziséhéyçizebasè bazi > zeziséhéyçizebasè zebazi).

Similarly, most nouns beginning with ziysé- change to géqsé- in the plural. Examples of this pattern include ziyséx, ziyséwmar, ziysébegè, ziyséwymeqmaze, ziyséhéséwçi, and ziyséwçiyhé (e.g., ziyséwçiyhé çèq > géqséwçiyhé zebase 'stained-glass windows'). However, some ziysé- nouns do not follow this pattern and form their plural with ze-, notably ziyséw, ziyséwyçiçisé, ziyséseçèséàr, ziyséçigèse, ziyséçèwbahéqmal and ziyséçiwmame (e.g., ziyséw bazi > zeziyséw zebazi 'the rails').

* Case
Nouns in Àrçèbawsè are not inflected for any other grammatical categories. (However, personal pronouns are inflected for case and person.)

----------
ADJECTIVES
----------

An adjective must agree in gender and number with the noun it modifies. Àrçèbawsè adjectives therefore have four forms: masculine singular, feminine singular, masculine plural, and feminine plural. A few adjectives, like qsébax and qsébahéqmaçè, have a fifth form, viz. an additional masculine singular form for use after a noun ending in sé, ba, y, ma, q, f, gè, ga and some occurrences of à, e.g. çèysewséda qsébax çèq (a beautiful garden), babebemaà zibax çèq (a handsome man), babebebasè bazizibax baçèq (a beautiful woman), zeçiçèsésèçèba géqsébax zebazi (the beautiful children), zeçèmazeysébe zebazizibax zebazi (the beautiful houses).

The masculine singular, an adjective's basic form, is listed in dictionaries. Most feminine forms are formed by adding the prefix ba- to the masculine form, e.g., seçèséwl > baseçèséwl, çiçèbazi > baçiçèbazi, çèsézewbame > baçèsézewbame. 

Under certain circumstances, other minor changes occur in the formation of feminine forms. Specifically, masculine adjectives beginning with ziba-, ziy-, çèma-, çèba-, zema- or zesé- double their initial consonant before adding the prefix ba- (e.g., zibaqwr > bazizibaqwr, ziyçiçèbal > baziziyçiçèbal, çèmax > baçèçèmax, çèbayrçèsé > baçèçèbayrçèsé, zemawl > bazezemawl, and zeséx > bazezeséx).

Additionally, adjectives beginning with r- change to baàr- (e.g., rçèsézix > baàrçèsézix); those beginning with wqba- or géqba- change to bazeqba- (e.g., wqbaçiçibabemawme > bazeqbaçiçibabemawme, géqbaywqsè > bazeqbaywqsè), with the exception of the irregular géqbayhé (old) whose feminine form is baziziybayhé; l- changes to baql- (e.g., lçèmazi > baqlçèmazi); sèy- changes to bahéy- (e.g., sèyçirsé > bahéyçirsé); sèba- changes to bahéga- (e.g., sèbawx > bahégawx); wba- changes to bawga- (e.g., wbalçèséwçigè > bawgalçèséwçigè); çiba- changes to baçiga- (e.g., çibayqjçèy > baçigayqjçèy); and adjectives beginning with qma- have a special form zima- (becoming bazizima- in feminine) that appears after sé, ba, y, ma, q, f, gè, ga and some occurrences of à, (e.g., qmasè/zimasè > bazizimasè, qmabe/zimabe > bazizimabe).

If an adjective's basic form beginning with ba-, it does not change in the feminine (cf. baàryw babebemaà çèq 'a rich man' > baàryw babebebasè baçèq 'a rich woman').

The plural is normally formed by adding the prefix ze- to the singular (masculine and feminine; e.g., yzimada > zeyzimada, bayzimada > zebayzimada). If the basic form beginning with ze-, gé-, or p-, an adjective does not change in the masculine plural (e.g., zeséx > zeséx, géqbawgèçègèl > géqbawgèçègèl, géqmase > géqmase), but its feminine plural form follows the rules detailed above. All Àrçèbawsè adjectives beginning with qséba- take the prefix gé- in the masculine plural (e.g., qsébahéqmaçè > géqsébahéqmaçè). Distinctive plural forms occur with adjectives beginning with zisé-, which normally change to géqsé- in the masculine plural (e.g., ziséçèwbahéyà > géqséçèwbahéyà, ziséwçiçèbar > géqséwçiçèbar), with only two exceptions: ziséçisésè > zeziséçisésè and ziséhéséçè > zeziséhéséçè which follow the regular pattern. By contrast, the feminine plural is always formed according to the general rule: baziséwçiçèbar > zebaziséwçiçèbar.

Adjective placement follows specific patterns. Most adjectives are placed after the noun they modify, and this is particularly true for colors, as in balqmaw bazi çèyhé (the red wine). However, certain short, commonly used adjectives – those dealing with beauty, age, goodness, or size (sometimes remembered by the acronym "BAGS") – typically precede their nouns. These are qsébax (beautiful), çèmax (good), sèbawx (brief), seçèséwl (big/tall), zemawl (fat/large), géqsésè (false), çiqséà (high), lçèmazi (long), sèbawx (brief), baçèqbada (young), yzimada (pretty), zeyséhéqsébe (bad), wqbaziziybabe (better), qsébahéqmaçè (new), çiyçibame (small), géqbayhé (old); e.g., babebebasè baçèq bazizibax ("a beautiful woman").

--------
PRONOUNS
--------
In Àrçèbawsè, pronouns are inflected to indicate their role in the sentence (subject, direct object, and so on), as well as to reflect the person, gender, and number of their referents. 

*Personal Pronouns
àrçèbawsè personal pronouns (analogous to English I, you, he/she, we, and they) reflect the person and number of their referent, and in the case of the third person, its gender as well. They also reflect the role they play in their clause: subject, direct object, indirect object, or other.

The personal pronouns change form to reflect the role they play in their clause. The forms used for subjects are called the subject pronouns, subjective pronouns, or nominative pronouns. They are as follows: 

**Subject Pronouns
------------------------
Number   | Person           | Subject Pronoun
------------------------
Singular | 1st              | bada
         | 2nd (informal)   | qçi
         | 2nd (formal)     | zeqmahé
         | 3rd (masculine)  | ziy
         | 3rd (feminine)   | baziziba
         | 3rd (neutral)    | çèma
------------------------
Plural   | 1st              | zeqmaçè
         | 2nd              | zeqmahé
         | 3rd (masculine)  | zeziy
         | 3rd (feminine)   | zebaziziba
------------------------

Note: Whenever the subject pronoun bada occurs after sé, ba, y, ma, q, f, gè, ga, ê and some occurrences of à, it becomes 'da.

*Relative pronouns

àrçèbawsè, like English, uses relative pronouns to link relative clauses to their head nouns, except that in Àrçèbawsè, as in Amharic for instance, the relative clause precedes its head and the relative pronoun, this is why we speak of "head noun" rather than of an "antecedent." The relative pronoun used depends on its grammatical role (such as subject or direct object) within the relative clause.

If the relative pronoun is to be the subject of the relative clause's verb, yqj is ordinarily used: baçiçibazirfryx sébe gèzimahé sé yqj babebemaà'zi ("the man who stole my bike"). Note that yqj in this use does not change form to agree in any way with its head noun: zebagèzimahé gèçigè çiçèma yqj zebaçiçibazirfryx zebazi ("the bikes that were stolen").

If the relative pronoun is to be the direct object of the relative clause's verb, baqj (or 'qj after sé, ba, y, ma, q, f, gè, ga, ê and some occurrences of à) is ordinarily used: bagèzimahé sé ziy'qj baçiçibazirfryx sézi ("the bicycle that he stole"). Like yqj, baqj does not change form to agree with its head noun.


-----
VERBS
-----
Verbs in Àrçèbawsè are conjugated to reflect the following information:

    a mood (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, or conditional)
    a tense (past, present, or future, though not all tenses can be combined with all moods)
    an aspect (perfective or imperfective)
    a voice (active, passive, or reflexive)
    Nonfinite forms (e.g., participles, gerunds, infinitives)


Verbs in the finite moods (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, and conditional) are also conjugated to agree with their subjects in person (first, second, or third) and number (singular or plural). As in English, the subject must be included (except in the imperative mood); in other words Àrçèbawsè is neither a null-subject nor a pro-drop language.

Auxiliary verbs are combined with past participles of main verbs to produce compound tenses, including the compound past. For most main verbs the auxiliary is (the appropriate form of) wymahésé ("to have"), but for reflexive verbs and certain intransitive verbs the auxiliary is a form of bawçiê ("to be"). The participle agrees with the subject when the auxiliary is bawçiê, and with a following direct object (if any) when the auxiliary is wymahésé. Forms of bawçiê are also used with the past participles of transitive verbs to form the passive voice.

*Morphology

In Àrçèbawsè, a verb is inflected to reflect its mood and tense, as well as to agree with its subject in person and number.

**Stems and conjugation prefixes

àrçèbawsè verbs have a large number of simple (one-word) forms. These are composed of two distinct parts: the stem (or root, or radix), which indicates which verb it is, and the prefix (inflection), which indicates the verb's tense (imperfect, present, future etc.) and mood and its subject's person (I, you, he/she etc.) and number, though many prefixes can correspond to multiple tense-mood-subject combinations. In certain parts of the second conjugation there is also a prefix -zezey- between the stem and the ending.

    In çiçèbayséziwséme, the stem -ziwséme indicates that the verb is wbaziwséme (to speak) and the prefix çiçèbaysé- marks the third-person plural imperfect indicative. "Third person plural" meaning the subject of the verb is "they". The "imperfect indicative" being a tense.
    In zeçèmazezeyçèysè, the stem -çèysè indicates that the verb is wyçèysè (to finish), the prefix -zezey- precedes it, and the inflection zeçèma- marks the first-person plural present indicative or imperative. The "first-person plural" is the "we" form of a verb. The "present indicative" being a tense and "imperative" being a mood, but in Àrçèbawsè they are indistinguishable without context.

These verb conjugations are coupled with a subject pronoun in order to convey who the subject of the verb is (i.e. who is doing the action).

***The principle of the fixed stem

The stem normally stays fixed in the first two conjugations:

    wbaziwséme: zeyséwbaziwséme bada, zeséziwséme qçi, çiçèbazezeséziwséme zeziy'qj, zeçèmayziwséme zeqmaçè baqj, pbaziwséme...
    wyçèysè: zeyséwyçèysè bada, zebaçiîçèysè zeqmahé, çiçèbazezeyçèysè zeziy'qj, zeyçèysè, zeçèmayzezeyçèysè zeqmaçè baqj...

In the third it is often modified, sometimes even between persons in the same tense:

    wymaziqmahé: géqbahé bada, géqbahé qçi, çiqbahé ziy, zeçèmaziqmahé zeqmaçè, pbaziqmahé zeqmahé, çiçèbaziqbahé zeziy.

But such irregularities apart, the principle is that nothing is removed from the stem. 


**Conjugation prefixes

The conjugation prefix tells us:

    For all verbs, the mood and the tense;
    For finite verbs, the person and the number; and
    For the past participle alone, the gender and the number.

Apart from a few frequent verbs which are considered totally irregular (mainly wymahésé, bawçiê, wbazizisé and bawysésè), for each tense of each mood a series of six prefixes (one for each person singular and plural) is associated with a group or subgroup of verbs.


*Formation of simple tenses active

These tenses are not formed with an auxiliary, and their formation is discussed in the following section.

**Infinitive

A verb is normally named by its present infinitive. Starting from this infinitive, the conjugations can be classified into three different groups:

    The first group or first conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with wba- (with the exception of wbazizisé, which due to its numerous irregularities is usually classed as being in the third conjugation):

    wbabeysé, wbafséziséx, wbaçiçèséàr, wbafmahéçèba, wbabewbasè, wbalçèsébe, wbazezeséme, wbafséme, wbaçèbabemawme, wbasewsélbaw, etc.

        For example, for the verb wbaziwséme, the stem is -ziwséme and the infinitive prefix is wba-.

    The second group or second conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with wy- whose present participle begins with çiçèsézezey-:

    wyçègèx, wyçisémebemar, wymewbaqlgèse, wywqbazisè, wyseçèséwl, wïséà, wyçizebahéçèy, wyzimame, wylqmaw, wylqw, wyziséze, etc.

        For example, for the verb wyçèysè, the stem is -çèysè and the infinitive prefix is wy-.

    The third group or third conjugation. This contains all the other verbs.
    
Note that the auxiliaries bawçiê and wymahésé, although they would naturally seem to belong to the third conjugation, are traditionally classed separately. 

**Present indicative

The present indicative is the form of the verb used to describe an action in the present e.g. basewsélbaw bada means "I watch".

The stem of the present indicative is not always regular and can vary (especially in the third conjugation) and there are three main sets of prefixes:

    Verbs beginning with wba- (all verbs of the first group): ba-, zeba-, ba-, zeçèma-, pba-, çiçèba-.
    Verbs beginning with wy- (all verbs of the second group and most of the third): zey-, zey-, çiy-, zeçèmazezey-, pbazezey-, çiçèbazezey-. But there are numerous irregularities, especially in the third group.
    Verbs beginning with baw- (part of the third group): ze-, ze-, - , zeçèma-, pba-, çiçèba-.
    
    Example:

-------------------------------
Person         | Singular             | Plural
-------------------------------
1st person     | basewsélbaw bada         | zeçèmasewsélbaw zeqmaçè
2nd person     | zebasewsélbaw qçi        | pbasewsélbaw zeqmahé
3rd person     | basewsélbaw çèma/baziziba/ziy | çiçèbasewsélbaw zebaziziba/zeziy
-------------------------------

-------------------------------

2nd person     | zeyzeymaàr qçi         | pbazezeyzeymaàr zeqmahé
3rd person     | çiyzeymaàr çèma/baziziba/ziy | çiçèbazezeyzeymaàr zebaziziba/zeziy

    Verbs of the second group take an -zezey- in the plural conjugations.
        
        
**Imperfect indicative

The imperfect indicative is a past tense describing states and actions that were ongoing in the past, e.g. "zeysésewsélbaw bada" means "I was watching".

    The stem of the imperfect indicative is always invariant for a single verb. It is derived in various ways depending on the verb group.
    For the first group, the stem is the infinitive minus the wba- prefix, e.g., wbasewsélbaw -> -sewsélbaw.
    For the second group, the stem is the infinitive minus the wy- prefix plus the zezey- prefix, e.g., wyzeymaàr -> -zezeyzeymaàr. 
    And for the third group, the stem is derived from the first person plural of the present indicative.

    The conjugation prefixes of this tense are for any of the three groups always: zeysé-, zeysé-, çiysé-, zeçèmay-, pbay-, çiçèbaysé-.

3rd person     | çiysésewsélbaw çèma/baziziba/ziy | çiçèbaysésewsélbaw zebaziziba/zeziy

3rd person     | çiysézezeyzeymaàr çèma/baziziba/ziy | çiçèbaysézezeyzeymaàr zebaziziba/zeziy

    Verb bawçiê : the stem is -çigè, endings are the same.
    

**Future

The future prefixes correspond to the present indicative of the verb wymahésé. They are always regular: ysé-, zesé-, sé-, zeçèma-, pba-, çiçèma-.

    The future stem is simply the infinitive (dictionary form). In other words, to form the future tense these prefixes are added to the infinitive:

**Past participle

Past participles, unlike present participles and gerundives, may be inflected to show gender and number by adding ba- and ze- prefixes, as with a normal adjective. Hence, "çiysèçèmar çiyqwsè çèq", "baçiysèçèmar bawymame baçèq", "zeçiysèçèmar zeçiyqwsè zebase", and "zebaçiysèçèmar zebawymame zebase."

The plain (masculine singular) form of a past participle begins with gè- for the 1st group verbs, and with y- for the 2nd group verbs. Third group verbs have more diverse prefixes : q- (bawseçèbaçiçèba qseçèbaçiçèba, bawymax qx, bawyzi qzi, etc. and wymahéséze qze, wymahé qhé, wymahéqmame qme), zey- (bawçiçibabe zeybe, bawseçèbawme zeywme, etc.), zeq- (bawqzirçèy zeqzirçèy and bawqzirbaw zeqzirbaw and only these verbs), çiy- (bawyseqsébe çiyseqsébe, bawyse çiyse, etc.), çi- (verbs in bawseçèy- : bawseçèybame çiçèybame), çiwba- (wywhéqma çiwbahéqma, wywhéqmar çiwbahéqmar, wywsèsèma çiwbasèsèma and wywsèsèqmaze çiwbasèsèqmaze), or qba (wymahésé qba). 

*Compound Tenses

àrçèbawsè compound tenses are verb forms that combine an auxiliary verb (either wymahésé or bawçiê) with the past participle of the main verb. These tenses are used to indicate actions that are completed or relate to another point in time. There are several compound tenses in Àrçèbawsè, each serving a specific purpose and adding nuance to the timeline of events.

**Compound Past

The compound past is perhaps the most commonly used compound tense in Àrçèbawsè. It is used to describe actions that have been completed in the past and is translated by the English simple past. The auxiliary verb is either wymahésé or bawçiê in the present tense, preceded by the past participle of the main verb. For example, "gèlçèsébe ysé'da" (I ate) or "gèhéywwsé çizeba ziy" (He arrived). wymahésé is used with most verbs, while bawçiê is used with a specific group of verbs, particularly those indicating movement or change of state, and with all reflexive verbs. When in doubt, wymahésé should be used by default.

Example:

1st Group: wbasewsélbaw (to watch)
-------------------------------
Person         | Singular                     | Plural
-------------------------------
1st person     | gèsewsélbaw ysé'da               | gèsewsélbaw zeçèmahésé zeqmaçè
2nd person     | gèsewsélbaw zesé qçi              | gèsewsélbaw pbahésé zeqmahé
