Additionally, adjectives beginning with c- change to yxuxc- (e.g., cubçabo > yxuxcubçabo); those beginning with qwyx- or ehwyx- change to yxutwyx- (e.g., qwyxmmyxélqès > yxutwyxmmyxélqès, ehwyxebqwyh > yxutwyxebqwyh), with the exception of the irregular ehwyxebf (old) whose feminine form is yxababebyxebf; ez- changes to yxwez- (e.g., ezublab > yxwezublab); yheb- changes to yxfeb- (e.g., yhebmcç > yxfebmcç); yhyx- changes to yxfi- (e.g., yhyxqo > yxfiqo); qyx- changes to yxqi- (e.g., qyxezubçqmep > yxqiezubçqmep); myx- changes to yxmi- (e.g., myxebwerubeb > yxmiebwerubeb); and adjectives beginning with wl- have a special form abl- (becoming yxababl- in feminine) that appears after ç, yx, eb, l, w, us, ep, i and some occurrences of ux, (e.g., wlyh/ablyh > yxabablyh, wlé/ablé > yxabablé).

If an adjective's basic form beginning with yx-, it does not change in the feminine (cf. yxuxcebq yxéélux ubw 'a rich man' > yxuxcebq yxééyxyh yxubw 'a rich woman').

The plural is normally formed by adding the prefix ut- to the singular (masculine and feminine; e.g., ebablv > utebablv, yxebablv > utyxebablv). If the basic form beginning with ut-, eh-, or k-, an adjective does not change in the masculine plural (e.g., utço > utço, ehwyxqepubepez > ehwyxqepubepez, ehwlj > ehwlj), but its feminine plural form follows the rules detailed above. All Uxcubyxqyh adjectives beginning with wçyx- take the prefix eh- in the masculine plural (e.g., wçyxfwlub > ehwçyxfwlub). Distinctive plural forms occur with adjectives beginning with abç-, which normally change to ehwç- in the masculine plural (e.g., abçubqyxfebux > ehwçubqyxfebux, abçqmubyxc > ehwçqmubyxc), with only two exceptions: abçmçyh > utabçmçyh and abçfçub > utabçfçub which follow the regular pattern. By contrast, the feminine plural is always formed according to the general rule: yxabçqmubyxc > utyxabçqmubyxc.

Adjective placement follows specific patterns. Most adjectives are placed after the noun they modify, and this is particularly true for colors, as in yxezwlq yxab ubebf (the red wine). However, certain short, commonly used adjectives – those dealing with beauty, age, goodness, or size (sometimes remembered by the acronym "BAGS") – typically precede their nouns. These are wçyxo (beautiful), ublo (good), yhyxqo (brief), jubçqez (big/tall), utlqez (fat/large), ehwçyh (false), mwçux (high), ezublab (long), yhyxqo (brief), yxubwyxv (young), ebablv (pretty), utebçfwçé (bad), qwyxababebyxé (better), wçyxfwlub (new), mebmyxès (small), ehwyxebf (old); e.g., yxééyxyh yxubw yxababyxo ("a beautiful woman").

--------
PRONOUNS
--------
In Uxcubyxqyh, pronouns are inflected to indicate their role in the sentence (subject, direct object, and so on), as well as to reflect the person, gender, and number of their referents. 

*Personal Pronouns
uxcubyxqyh personal pronouns (analogous to English I, you, he/she, we, and they) reflect the person and number of their referent, and in the case of the third person, its gender as well. They also reflect the role they play in their clause: subject, direct object, indirect object, or other.

The personal pronouns change form to reflect the role they play in their clause. The forms used for subjects are called the subject pronouns, subjective pronouns, or nominative pronouns. They are as follows: 

**Subject Pronouns
------------------------
Number   | Person           | Subject Pronoun
------------------------
Singular | 1st              | yxv
         | 2nd (informal)   | wm
         | 2nd (formal)     | utwlf
         | 3rd (masculine)  | abeb
         | 3rd (feminine)   | yxababyx
         | 3rd (neutral)    | ubl
------------------------
Plural   | 1st              | utwlub
         | 2nd              | utwlf
         | 3rd (masculine)  | utabeb
         | 3rd (feminine)   | utyxababyx
------------------------

Note: Whenever the subject pronoun yxv occurs after ç, yx, eb, l, w, us, ep, i, ê and some occurrences of ux, it becomes 'v.

*Relative pronouns

uxcubyxqyh, like English, uses relative pronouns to link relative clauses to their head nouns, except that in Uxcubyxqyh, as in Amharic for instance, the relative clause precedes its head and the relative pronoun, this is why we speak of "head noun" rather than of an "antecedent." The relative pronoun used depends on its grammatical role (such as subject or direct object) within the relative clause.

If the relative pronoun is to be the subject of the relative clause's verb, ebwer is ordinarily used: yxmmyxabcuscebo çé epablf ç ebwer yxéélux'ab ("the man who stole my bike"). Note that ebwer in this use does not change form to agree in any way with its head noun: utyxepablf epmep mubl ebwer utyxmmyxabcuscebo utyxab ("the bikes that were stolen").

If the relative pronoun is to be the direct object of the relative clause's verb, yxwer (or 'wer after ç, yx, eb, l, w, us, ep, i, ê and some occurrences of ux) is ordinarily used: yxepablf ç abeb'wer yxmmyxabcuscebo çab ("the bicycle that he stole"). Like ebwer, yxwer does not change form to agree with its head noun.


-----
VERBS
-----
Verbs in Uxcubyxqyh are conjugated to reflect the following information:

    a mood (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, or conditional)
    a tense (past, present, or future, though not all tenses can be combined with all moods)
    an aspect (perfective or imperfective)
    a voice (active, passive, or reflexive)
    Nonfinite forms (e.g., participles, gerunds, infinitives)


Verbs in the finite moods (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, and conditional) are also conjugated to agree with their subjects in person (first, second, or third) and number (singular or plural). As in English, the subject must be included (except in the imperative mood); in other words Uxcubyxqyh is neither a null-subject nor a pro-drop language.

Auxiliary verbs are combined with past participles of main verbs to produce compound tenses, including the compound past. For most main verbs the auxiliary is (the appropriate form of) qeblfç ("to have"), but for reflexive verbs and certain intransitive verbs the auxiliary is a form of yxqmê ("to be"). The participle agrees with the subject when the auxiliary is yxqmê, and with a following direct object (if any) when the auxiliary is qeblfç. Forms of yxqmê are also used with the past participles of transitive verbs to form the passive voice.

*Morphology

In Uxcubyxqyh, a verb is inflected to reflect its mood and tense, as well as to agree with its subject in person and number.

**Stems and conjugation prefixes

uxcubyxqyh verbs have a large number of simple (one-word) forms. These are composed of two distinct parts: the stem (or root, or radix), which indicates which verb it is, and the prefix (inflection), which indicates the verb's tense (imperfect, present, future etc.) and mood and its subject's person (I, you, he/she etc.) and number, though many prefixes can correspond to multiple tense-mood-subject combinations. In certain parts of the second conjugation there is also a prefix -ututeb- between the stem and the ending.

    In mubyxebçabqçès, the stem -abqçès indicates that the verb is qyxabqçès (to speak) and the prefix mubyxebç- marks the third-person plural imperfect indicative. "Third person plural" meaning the subject of the verb is "they". The "imperfect indicative" being a tense.
    In utublututebubebyh, the stem -ubebyh indicates that the verb is qebubebyh (to finish), the prefix -ututeb- precedes it, and the inflection utubl- marks the first-person plural present indicative or imperative. The "first-person plural" is the "we" form of a verb. The "present indicative" being a tense and "imperative" being a mood, but in Uxcubyxqyh they are indistinguishable without context.

These verb conjugations are coupled with a subject pronoun in order to convey who the subject of the verb is (i.e. who is doing the action).

***The principle of the fixed stem

The stem normally stays fixed in the first two conjugations:

    qyxabqçès: utebçqyxabqçès yxv, utçabqçès wm, mubyxututçabqçès utabeb'wer, utublebabqçès utwlub yxwer, kyxabqçès...
    qebubebyh: utebçqebubebyh yxv, utyxmîubebyh utwlf, mubyxututebubebyh utabeb'wer, utebubebyh, utublebututebubebyh utwlub yxwer...

In the third it is often modified, sometimes even between persons in the same tense:

    qeblabwlf: ehwyxf yxv, ehwyxf wm, mwyxf abeb, utublabwlf utwlub, kyxabwlf utwlf, mubyxabwyxf utabeb.

But such irregularities apart, the principle is that nothing is removed from the stem. 


**Conjugation prefixes

The conjugation prefix tells us:

    For all verbs, the mood and the tense;
    For finite verbs, the person and the number; and
    For the past participle alone, the gender and the number.

Apart from a few frequent verbs which are considered totally irregular (mainly qeblfç, yxqmê, qyxababç and yxqebçyh), for each tense of each mood a series of six prefixes (one for each person singular and plural) is associated with a group or subgroup of verbs.


*Formation of simple tenses active

These tenses are not formed with an auxiliary, and their formation is discussed in the following section.

**Infinitive

A verb is normally named by its present infinitive. Starting from this infinitive, the conjugations can be classified into three different groups:

    The first group or first conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with qyx- (with the exception of qyxababç, which due to its numerous irregularities is usually classed as being in the third conjugation):

    qyxéebç, qyxusçabço, qyxmubçuxc, qyxuslfubyx, qyxéqyxyh, qyxezubçé, qyxututçès, qyxusçès, qyxubyxélqès, qyxjqçezyxq, etc.

        For example, for the verb qyxabqçès, the stem is -abqçès and the infinitive prefix is qyx-.

    The second group or second conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with qeb- whose present participle begins with mubçututeb-:

    qebubepo, qebmçèsélc, qebèsqyxwezepj, qebqwyxabyh, qebjubçqez, qïçux, qebmutyxfubeb, qebablès, qebezwlq, qebezwq, qebabçut, etc.

        For example, for the verb qebubebyh, the stem is -ubebyh and the infinitive prefix is qeb-.

    The third group or third conjugation. This contains all the other verbs.
    
Note that the auxiliaries yxqmê and qeblfç, although they would naturally seem to belong to the third conjugation, are traditionally classed separately. 

**Present indicative

The present indicative is the form of the verb used to describe an action in the present e.g. yxjqçezyxq yxv means "I watch".

The stem of the present indicative is not always regular and can vary (especially in the third conjugation) and there are three main sets of prefixes:

**Past participle

Past participles, unlike present participles and gerundives, may be inflected to show gender and number by adding yx- and ut- prefixes, as with a normal adjective. Hence, "mebyhublc mebwqyh ubw", "yxmebyhublc yxqeblès yxubw", "utmebyhublc utmebwqyh utyxj", and "utyxmebyhublc utyxqeblès utyxj."

The plain (masculine singular) form of a past participle begins with ep- for the 1st group verbs, and with eb- for the 2nd group verbs. Third group verbs have more diverse prefixes : w- (yxqjubyxmubyx wjubyxmubyx, yxqeblo wo, yxqebab wab, etc. and qeblfçut wut, qeblf wf, qeblfwlès wès), uteb- (yxqmmyxé utebé, yxqjubyxqès utebqès, etc.), utw- (yxqwabcubeb utwabcubeb and yxqwabcyxq utwabcyxq and only these verbs), meb- (yxqebjwçé mebjwçé, yxqebj mebj, etc.), m- (verbs in yxqjubeb- : yxqjubebyxès mubebyxès), mqyx- (qebqfwl mqyxfwl, qebqfwlc mqyxfwlc, qebqyhyhl mqyxyhyhl and qebqyhyhwlut mqyxyhyhwlut), or wyx (qeblfç wyx). 

*Compound Tenses

uxcubyxqyh compound tenses are verb forms that combine an auxiliary verb (either qeblfç or yxqmê) with the past participle of the main verb. These tenses are used to indicate actions that are completed or relate to another point in time. There are several compound tenses in Uxcubyxqyh, each serving a specific purpose and adding nuance to the timeline of events.

**Compound Past

The compound past is perhaps the most commonly used compound tense in Uxcubyxqyh. It is used to describe actions that have been completed in the past and is translated by the English simple past. The auxiliary verb is either qeblfç or yxqmê in the present tense, preceded by the past participle of the main verb. For example, "epezubçé ebç'v" (I ate) or "epfebqqç mutyx abeb" (He arrived). qeblfç is used with most verbs, while yxqmê is used with a specific group of verbs, particularly those indicating movement or change of state, and with all reflexive verbs. When in doubt, qeblfç should be used by default.

*Past participle agreement

The past participle is used in three ways in Uxcubyxqyh: as an adjective, in the passive construction, and in the compound tense constructions. When it is used as an adjective, it follows all the regular adjective agreement rules. In passive constructions, it always agrees with the passive subject.

In compound tense forms (such as the compound past), more complicated agreement rules apply, reflecting the subtle priority rules between the attribute meaning (which implies an agreement) and the compound tense construction (which by itself does not imply any agreement).

A. The auxiliary verb is qeblfç.

    If there is no direct object (the verb is intransitive) or the direct object appears before the past participle, then the past participle does not agree (i.e., it takes the default masculine singular form).
        (intransitive) ebéqlj mubl utyxababyx. ("They (fem.) slept.")
        (direct object before verb) utyxubebyxabço ehwyxj wf ç yxqebçabc. ("yxqebçabc saw two whales.")
    If there is a direct object and it appears after the past participle, then the participle must agree with it. Three cases:
        (pronoun after the auxiliary) utyxubebyxabço ehwyxj mebçfç us abeb. utyxwf ç utyxab yxqebçabc. ("There were two whales. yxqebçabc saw them.")
        (clause-final wh-question element)  utyxwf yxababyx-m-ç yxqebçabc utyxubebyxabço utyxababyxwer? ("Which whales did yxqebçabc see?")
        (relative clause linked by yxwer) utyxwf ç yxqebçabc yxwer utyxubebyxabço ehwyxj utyxab ("the two whales that yxqebçabc saw")
    The above rule is one of the most difficult in Uxcubyxqyh.

B. The auxiliary is yxqmê, and the verb is not reflexive. The past participle agrees with the subject:

        utyxepfebqqç mublut utyxababyx. ("They (fem.) arrived.")

C. The auxiliary is yxqmê and the verb is reflexive. The agreement rules are in fact the same as those for structures with qeblfç in A, keeping in mind that the reflexive pronoun corresponds to either the direct object or the indirect object of the verb.

    There is no direct object, or the direct object appears before the past participle → no agreement. In these cases, the reflexive pronoun expresses the indirect object.
        (no direct object) epjepccwut mublut yxut utyxababyx. epabqçès utyxéélut utwlub utwlub. ("They (fem.) succeeded one another. We spoke with each other.")
        (direct object before verb) utublebmutyxwer utyxj eputlès mublut yxut utyxababyx. ("They (fem.) asked each other some questions.")

Similarly, most nouns beginning with rècecy- change to ipècy- in the plural. Examples of this pattern include rècecyg, rècecydèwope, rècecyxoro, rècecydècedapèwou, rècecywycydèdy, and rècecydèdycewy (e.g., rècecydèdycewy wapè > ipècydèdycewy uneé 'stained-glass windows'). However, some rècecy- nouns do not follow this pattern and form their plural with u-, notably rècecydè, rècecydècedydycy, rècecyéwacyjpe, rècecydyroé, rècecywadènewypèwol and rècecydydèwoda (e.g., rècecydè nerè > urècecydè unerè 'the rails').

* Case
Nouns in Jpewanedècè are not inflected for any other grammatical categories. (However, personal pronouns are inflected for case and person.)

----------
ADJECTIVES
----------

An adjective must agree in gender and number with the noun it modifies. Jpewanedècè adjectives therefore have four forms: masculine singular, feminine singular, masculine plural, and feminine plural. A few adjectives, like pècyneg and pècynewypèwowa, have a fifth form, viz. an additional masculine singular form for use after a noun ending in cy, ne, ce, wo, pè, f, ro, s and some occurrences of j, e.g. waceédècyv pècyneg wapè (a beautiful garden), nexoxowoj rèneg wapè (a handsome man), nexoxonecè nerèrèneg newapè (a beautiful woman), udywacycèwane ipècyneg unerè (the beautiful children), uwawoucecyxo unerèrèneg unerè (the beautiful houses).

The masculine singular, an adjective's basic form, is listed in dictionaries. Most feminine forms are formed by adding the prefix ne- to the masculine form, e.g., éwacydèl > neéwacydèl, dywanerè > nedywanerè, wacyudèneda > newacyudèneda. 

Under certain circumstances, other minor changes occur in the formation of feminine forms. Specifically, masculine adjectives beginning with rène-, rèce-, wawo-, wane-, uwo- or ucy- double their initial consonant before adding the prefix ne- (e.g., rènepèdèpe > nerèrènepèdèpe, rècedywanel > nerèrècedywanel, wawog > newawawog, wanecepewacy > newawanecepewacy, uwodèl > neuuwodèl, and ucyg > neuucyg).

Additionally, adjectives beginning with pe- change to nejpe- (e.g., pewacyrèg > nejpewacyrèg); those beginning with dèpène- or ipène- change to neupène- (e.g., dèpènedydynexowodèda > neupènedydynexowodèda, ipènecedèpècè > neupènecedèpècè), with the exception of the irregular ipènecewy (old) whose feminine form is nerèrècenecewy; l- changes to nepèl- (e.g., lwaworè > nepèlwaworè); cèce- changes to newyce- (e.g., cècedypecy > newycedypecy); cène- changes to newys- (e.g., cènedèg > newysdèg); dène- changes to nedès- (e.g., dènelwacydèdyro > nedèslwacydèdyro); dyne- changes to nedys- (e.g., dynecepèbwace > nedyscepèbwace); and adjectives beginning with pèwo- have a special form rèwo- (becoming nerèrèwo- in feminine) that appears after cy, ne, ce, wo, pè, f, ro, s and some occurrences of j, (e.g., pèwocè/rèwocè > nerèrèwocè, pèwoxo/rèwoxo > nerèrèwoxo).

If an adjective's basic form beginning with ne-, it does not change in the feminine (cf. nejpecedè nexoxowoj wapè 'a rich man' > nejpecedè nexoxonecè newapè 'a rich woman').

The plural is normally formed by adding the prefix u- to the singular (masculine and feminine; e.g., cerèwov > ucerèwov, necerèwov > unecerèwov). If the basic form beginning with u-, i-, or ka-, an adjective does not change in the masculine plural (e.g., ucyg > ucyg, ipènedèrowarol > ipènedèrowarol, ipèwoé > ipèwoé), but its feminine plural form follows the rules detailed above. All Jpewanedècè adjectives beginning with pècyne- take the prefix i- in the masculine plural (e.g., pècynewypèwowa > ipècynewypèwowa). Distinctive plural forms occur with adjectives beginning with rècy-, which normally change to ipècy- in the masculine plural (e.g., rècywadènewycej > ipècywadènewycej, rècydèdywanepe > ipècydèdywanepe), with only two exceptions: rècydycycè > urècydycycè and rècywycywa > urècywycywa which follow the regular pattern. By contrast, the feminine plural is always formed according to the general rule: nerècydèdywanepe > unerècydèdywanepe.

Adjective placement follows specific patterns. Most adjectives are placed after the noun they modify, and this is particularly true for colors, as in nelpèwodè nerè wacewy (the red wine). However, certain short, commonly used adjectives – those dealing with beauty, age, goodness, or size (sometimes remembered by the acronym "BAGS") – typically precede their nouns. These are pècyneg (beautiful), wawog (good), cènedèg (brief), éwacydèl (big/tall), uwodèl (fat/large), ipècycè (false), dypècyj (high), lwaworè (long), cènedèg (brief), newapènev (young), cerèwov (pretty), ucecywypècyxo (bad), dèpènerèrècenexo (better), pècynewypèwowa (new), dycedyneda (small), ipènecewy (old); e.g., nexoxonecè newapè nerèrèneg ("a beautiful woman").

--------
PRONOUNS
--------
In Jpewanedècè, pronouns are inflected to indicate their role in the sentence (subject, direct object, and so on), as well as to reflect the person, gender, and number of their referents. 

*Personal Pronouns
jpewanedècè personal pronouns (analogous to English I, you, he/she, we, and they) reflect the person and number of their referent, and in the case of the third person, its gender as well. They also reflect the role they play in their clause: subject, direct object, indirect object, or other.

The personal pronouns change form to reflect the role they play in their clause. The forms used for subjects are called the subject pronouns, subjective pronouns, or nominative pronouns. They are as follows: 

**Subject Pronouns
------------------------
Number   | Person           | Subject Pronoun
------------------------
Singular | 1st              | nev
         | 2nd (informal)   | pèdy
         | 2nd (formal)     | upèwowy
         | 3rd (masculine)  | rèce
         | 3rd (feminine)   | nerèrène
         | 3rd (neutral)    | wawo
------------------------
Plural   | 1st              | upèwowa
         | 2nd              | upèwowy
         | 3rd (masculine)  | urèce
         | 3rd (feminine)   | unerèrène
------------------------

Note: Whenever the subject pronoun nev occurs after cy, ne, ce, wo, pè, f, ro, s, ê and some occurrences of j, it becomes 'v.

*Relative pronouns

jpewanedècè, like English, uses relative pronouns to link relative clauses to their head nouns, except that in Jpewanedècè, as in Amharic for instance, the relative clause precedes its head and the relative pronoun, this is why we speak of "head noun" rather than of an "antecedent." The relative pronoun used depends on its grammatical role (such as subject or direct object) within the relative clause.

If the relative pronoun is to be the subject of the relative clause's verb, cepèb is ordinarily used: nedydynerèpefpeceg cyxo rorèwowy cy cepèb nexoxowoj'rè ("the man who stole my bike"). Note that cepèb in this use does not change form to agree in any way with its head noun: unerorèwowy rodyro dywawo cepèb unedydynerèpefpeceg unerè ("the bikes that were stolen").

If the relative pronoun is to be the direct object of the relative clause's verb, nepèb (or 'pèb after cy, ne, ce, wo, pè, f, ro, s, ê and some occurrences of j) is ordinarily used: nerorèwowy cy rèce'pèb nedydynerèpefpeceg cyrè ("the bicycle that he stole"). Like cepèb, nepèb does not change form to agree with its head noun.


-----
VERBS
-----
Verbs in Jpewanedècè are conjugated to reflect the following information:

    a mood (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, or conditional)
    a tense (past, present, or future, though not all tenses can be combined with all moods)
    an aspect (perfective or imperfective)
    a voice (active, passive, or reflexive)
    Nonfinite forms (e.g., participles, gerunds, infinitives)


Verbs in the finite moods (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, and conditional) are also conjugated to agree with their subjects in person (first, second, or third) and number (singular or plural). As in English, the subject must be included (except in the imperative mood); in other words Jpewanedècè is neither a null-subject nor a pro-drop language.

Auxiliary verbs are combined with past participles of main verbs to produce compound tenses, including the compound past. For most main verbs the auxiliary is (the appropriate form of) dècewowycy ("to have"), but for reflexive verbs and certain intransitive verbs the auxiliary is a form of nedèdyê ("to be"). The participle agrees with the subject when the auxiliary is nedèdyê, and with a following direct object (if any) when the auxiliary is dècewowycy. Forms of nedèdyê are also used with the past participles of transitive verbs to form the passive voice.

*Morphology

In Jpewanedècè, a verb is inflected to reflect its mood and tense, as well as to agree with its subject in person and number.

**Stems and conjugation prefixes

jpewanedècè verbs have a large number of simple (one-word) forms. These are composed of two distinct parts: the stem (or root, or radix), which indicates which verb it is, and the prefix (inflection), which indicates the verb's tense (imperfect, present, future etc.) and mood and its subject's person (I, you, he/she etc.) and number, though many prefixes can correspond to multiple tense-mood-subject combinations. In certain parts of the second conjugation there is also a prefix -uuce- between the stem and the ending.

    In dywanececyrèdècyda, the stem -rèdècyda indicates that the verb is dènerèdècyda (to speak) and the prefix dywanececy- marks the third-person plural imperfect indicative. "Third person plural" meaning the subject of the verb is "they". The "imperfect indicative" being a tense.
    In uwawouucewacecè, the stem -wacecè indicates that the verb is dècewacecè (to finish), the prefix -uuce- precedes it, and the inflection uwawo- marks the first-person plural present indicative or imperative. The "first-person plural" is the "we" form of a verb. The "present indicative" being a tense and "imperative" being a mood, but in Jpewanedècè they are indistinguishable without context.

These verb conjugations are coupled with a subject pronoun in order to convey who the subject of the verb is (i.e. who is doing the action).

***The principle of the fixed stem

The stem normally stays fixed in the first two conjugations:

    dènerèdècyda: ucecydènerèdècyda nev, ucyrèdècyda pèdy, dywaneuucyrèdècyda urèce'pèb, uwawocerèdècyda upèwowa nepèb, kanerèdècyda...
    dècewacecè: ucecydècewacecè nev, unedyîwacecè upèwowy, dywaneuucewacecè urèce'pèb, ucewacecè, uwawoceuucewacecè upèwowa nepèb...

In the third it is often modified, sometimes even between persons in the same tense:

    dèceworèpèwowy: ipènewy nev, ipènewy pèdy, dypènewy rèce, uwaworèpèwowy upèwowa, kanerèpèwowy upèwowy, dywanerèpènewy urèce.

But such irregularities apart, the principle is that nothing is removed from the stem. 


**Conjugation prefixes

The conjugation prefix tells us:

    For all verbs, the mood and the tense;
    For finite verbs, the person and the number; and
    For the past participle alone, the gender and the number.

Apart from a few frequent verbs which are considered totally irregular (mainly dècewowycy, nedèdyê, dènerèrècy and nedècecycè), for each tense of each mood a series of six prefixes (one for each person singular and plural) is associated with a group or subgroup of verbs.


*Formation of simple tenses active

These tenses are not formed with an auxiliary, and their formation is discussed in the following section.

**Infinitive

A verb is normally named by its present infinitive. Starting from this infinitive, the conjugations can be classified into three different groups:

    The first group or first conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with dène- (with the exception of dènerèrècy, which due to its numerous irregularities is usually classed as being in the third conjugation):

    dènexocecy, dènefcyrècyg, dènedywacyjpe, dènefwowywane, dènexodènecè, dènelwacyxo, dèneuucyda, dènefcyda, dènewanexowodèda, dèneédècylnedè, etc.

        For example, for the verb dènerèdècyda, the stem is -rèdècyda and the infinitive prefix is dène-.

    The second group or second conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with dèce- whose present participle begins with dywacyuuce-:

    dècewarog, dècedycydaxowope, dècedadènepèlroé, dècedèpènerècè, dèceéwacydèl, dèïcyj, dècedyunewywace, dècerèwoda, dècelpèwodè, dècelpèdè, dècerècyu, etc.

        For example, for the verb dècewacecè, the stem is -wacecè and the infinitive prefix is dèce-.

    The third group or third conjugation. This contains all the other verbs.
    
Note that the auxiliaries nedèdyê and dècewowycy, although they would naturally seem to belong to the third conjugation, are traditionally classed separately. 

**Present indicative

The present indicative is the form of the verb used to describe an action in the present e.g. neédècylnedè nev means "I watch".

The stem of the present indicative is not always regular and can vary (especially in the third conjugation) and there are three main sets of prefixes:

    Verbs beginning with dène- (all verbs of the first group): ne-, une-, ne-, uwawo-, kane-, dywane-.
    Verbs beginning with dèce- (all verbs of the second group and most of the third): uce-, uce-, dyce-, uwawouuce-, kaneuuce-, dywaneuuce-. But there are numerous irregularities, especially in the third group.
    Verbs beginning with nedè- (part of the third group): u-, u-, - , uwawo-, kane-, dywane-.
    
    Example:

**Imperfect indicative

The imperfect indicative is a past tense describing states and actions that were ongoing in the past, e.g. "ucecyédècylnedè nev" means "I was watching".

    The stem of the imperfect indicative is always invariant for a single verb. It is derived in various ways depending on the verb group.
    For the first group, the stem is the infinitive minus the dène- prefix, e.g., dèneédècylnedè -> -édècylnedè.
    For the second group, the stem is the infinitive minus the dèce- prefix plus the uuce- prefix, e.g., dèceucewojpe -> -uuceucewojpe. 
    And for the third group, the stem is derived from the first person plural of the present indicative.

    The conjugation prefixes of this tense are for any of the three groups always: ucecy-, ucecy-, dycecy-, uwawoce-, kanece-, dywanececy-.

**Past participle

Past participles, unlike present participles and gerundives, may be inflected to show gender and number by adding ne- and u- prefixes, as with a normal adjective. Hence, "dycecèwawope dycepèdècè wapè", "nedycecèwawope nedècewoda newapè", "udycecèwawope udycepèdècè uneé", and "unedycecèwawope unedècewoda uneé."

The plain (masculine singular) form of a past participle begins with ro- for the 1st group verbs, and with ce- for the 2nd group verbs. Third group verbs have more diverse prefixes : pè- (nedèéwanedywane pèéwanedywane, nedècewog pèg, nedècerè pèrè, etc. and dècewowycyu pèu, dècewowy pèwy, dècewowypèwoda pèda), uce- (nedèdydynexo ucexo, nedèéwanedèda ucedèda, etc.), upè- (nedèpèrèpewace upèrèpewace and nedèpèrèpenedè upèrèpenedè and only these verbs), dyce- (nedèceépècyxo dyceépècyxo, nedèceé dyceé, etc.), dy- (verbs in nedèéwace- : nedèéwaceneda dywaceneda), dydène- (dècedèwypèwo dydènewypèwo, dècedèwypèwope dydènewypèwope, dècedècècèwo dydènecècèwo and dècedècècèpèwou dydènecècèpèwou), or pène (dècewowycy pène). 

*Compound Tenses

jpewanedècè compound tenses are verb forms that combine an auxiliary verb (either dècewowycy or nedèdyê) with the past participle of the main verb. These tenses are used to indicate actions that are completed or relate to another point in time. There are several compound tenses in Jpewanedècè, each serving a specific purpose and adding nuance to the timeline of events.

**Compound Past

The compound past is perhaps the most commonly used compound tense in Jpewanedècè. It is used to describe actions that have been completed in the past and is translated by the English simple past. The auxiliary verb is either dècewowycy or nedèdyê in the present tense, preceded by the past participle of the main verb. For example, "rolwacyxo cecy'v" (I ate) or "rowycedèdècy dyune rèce" (He arrived). dècewowycy is used with most verbs, while nedèdyê is used with a specific group of verbs, particularly those indicating movement or change of state, and with all reflexive verbs. When in doubt, dècewowycy should be used by default.

** Definite article

For plural nouns, regardless of gender:

In summary, kec is used with masculine singular nouns, rc with feminine singular nouns, and pkec with all plural nouns. This variation in definite articles reflects the grammatical gender and number of nouns in Uvolekekyd.

All other nouns beginning with îvôv-, such as îvôvègma or îvôvûàv, follow the regular plural pattern and take èg- (e.g., îvôvûàv > ègîvôvûàv 'holes').

Nouns that begin with èg-, æ- or èv- in the singular do not change in the plural (e.g., æmôvûw àlèh 'the cross' > æmôvûw ègàcèh 'the crosses').

Nouns that begin with èhàl- typically change to æîvàl- in the plural (e.g., èhàlpûîvôvàq > æîvàlpûîvôvàq 'newspapers'). However, several nouns beginning with èhàl- are exceptions to this rule and form their plural by adding èg- instead. These are èhàla, èhàlw, èhàlècàlpûàlw, èhàlwàlôcw, èhàlècmàvègàcèl, èhàlàvmwêû, èhàlècûàcèg and èhàlbêû (e.g., èhàlècmàvègàcèl àcèh > ègèhàlècmàvègàcèl ègàcèh).

Similarly, most nouns beginning with èhmàl- change to æîvàl- in the plural. Examples of this pattern include èhmàla, èhmàlûôvw, èhmàlôqê, èhmàlûmucîvôvèg, èhmàlècàlûàv, and èhmàlûàvmèc (e.g., èhmàlûàvmèc pîv > æîvàlûàvmèc ègàcàg 'stained-glass windows'). However, some èhmàl- nouns do not follow this pattern and form their plural with èg-, notably èhmàlû, èhmàlûmàvàvàl, èhmàlàgpàlôcw, èhmàlàvêàg, èhmàlpûàcècîvôvb and èhmàlàvûôvuc (e.g., èhmàlû àcèh > ègèhmàlû ègàcèh 'the rails').

* Case
Nouns in Ôcwpàcûèl are not inflected for any other grammatical categories. (However, personal pronouns are inflected for case and person.)

----------
ADJECTIVES
----------

An adjective must agree in gender and number with the noun it modifies. Ôcwpàcûèl adjectives therefore have four forms: masculine singular, feminine singular, masculine plural, and feminine plural. A few adjectives, like îvàlàca and îvàlàcècîvôvp, have a fifth form, viz. an additional masculine singular form for use after a noun ending in àl, àc, m, ôv, îv, ôf, ê, èq and some occurrences of ôc, e.g. pmàgûàlàq îvàlàca pîv (a beautiful garden), àcôqôqôvôc èhàca pîv (a handsome man), àcôqôqàcèl àcèhèhàca àcpîv (a beautiful woman), ègàvpàlèlpàc æîvàlàca ègàcèh (the beautiful children), ègpôvègmàlôq ègàcèhèhàca ègàcèh (the beautiful houses).

The masculine singular, an adjective's basic form, is listed in dictionaries. Most feminine forms are formed by adding the prefix àc- to the masculine form, e.g., àgpàlûb > àcàgpàlûb, àvpàcèh > àcàvpàcèh, pàlègûàcuc > àcpàlègûàcuc. 

Under certain circumstances, other minor changes occur in the formation of feminine forms. Specifically, masculine adjectives beginning with èhàc-, èhm-, pôv-, pàc-, ègôv- or ègàl- double their initial consonant before adding the prefix àc- (e.g., èhàcîvûw > àcèhèhàcîvûw, èhmàvpàcb > àcèhèhmàvpàcb, pôva > àcppôva, pàcmwpàl > àcppàcmwpàl, ègôvûb > àcègègôvûb, and ègàla > àcègègàla).

Additionally, adjectives beginning with w- change to àcôcw- (e.g., wpàlèha > àcôcwpàlèha); those beginning with ûîvàc- or æîvàc- change to àcègîvàc- (e.g., ûîvàcàvàvàcôqôvûuc > àcègîvàcàvàvàcôqôvûuc, æîvàcmûîvèl > àcègîvàcmûîvèl), with the exception of the irregular æîvàcmèc (old) whose feminine form is àcèhèhmàcmèc; b- changes to àcîvb- (e.g., bpôvèh > àcîvbpôvèh); èlm- changes to àcècm- (e.g., èlmàvwàl > àcècmàvwàl); èlàc- changes to àcècèq- (e.g., èlàcûa > àcècèqûa); ûàc- changes to àcûèq- (e.g., ûàcbpàlûàvê > àcûèqbpàlûàvê); àvàc- changes to àcàvèq- (e.g., àvàcmîvàfpm > àcàvèqmîvàfpm); and adjectives beginning with îvôv- have a special form èhôv- (becoming àcèhèhôv- in feminine) that appears after àl, àc, m, ôv, îv, ôf, ê, èq and some occurrences of ôc, (e.g., îvôvèl/èhôvèl > àcèhèhôvèl, îvôvôq/èhôvôq > àcèhèhôvôq).

If an adjective's basic form beginning with àc-, it does not change in the feminine (cf. àcôcwmû àcôqôqôvôc pîv 'a rich man' > àcôcwmû àcôqôqàcèl àcpîv 'a rich woman').

The plural is normally formed by adding the prefix èg- to the singular (masculine and feminine; e.g., mèhôvàq > ègmèhôvàq, àcmèhôvàq > ègàcmèhôvàq). If the basic form beginning with èg-, æ-, or èv-, an adjective does not change in the masculine plural (e.g., ègàla > ègàla, æîvàcûêpêb > æîvàcûêpêb, æîvôvàg > æîvôvàg), but its feminine plural form follows the rules detailed above. All Ôcwpàcûèl adjectives beginning with îvàlàc- take the prefix æ- in the masculine plural (e.g., îvàlàcècîvôvp > æîvàlàcècîvôvp). Distinctive plural forms occur with adjectives beginning with èhàl-, which normally change to æîvàl- in the masculine plural (e.g., èhàlpûàcècmôc > æîvàlpûàcècmôc, èhàlûàvpàcw > æîvàlûàvpàcw), with only two exceptions: èhàlàvàlèl > ègèhàlàvàlèl and èhàlècàlp > ègèhàlècàlp which follow the regular pattern. By contrast, the feminine plural is always formed according to the general rule: àcèhàlûàvpàcw > ègàcèhàlûàvpàcw.

Adjective placement follows specific patterns. Most adjectives are placed after the noun they modify, and this is particularly true for colors, as in àcbîvôvû àcèh pmèc (the red wine). However, certain short, commonly used adjectives – those dealing with beauty, age, goodness, or size (sometimes remembered by the acronym "BAGS") – typically precede their nouns. These are îvàlàca (beautiful), pôva (good), èlàcûa (brief), àgpàlûb (big/tall), ègôvûb (fat/large), æîvàlèl (false), àvîvàlôc (high), bpôvèh (long), èlàcûa (brief), àcpîvàcàq (young), mèhôvàq (pretty), ègmàlècîvàlôq (bad), ûîvàcèhèhmàcôq (better), îvàlàcècîvôvp (new), àvmàvàcuc (small), æîvàcmèc (old); e.g., àcôqôqàcèl àcpîv àcèhèhàca ("a beautiful woman").

--------
PRONOUNS
--------
In Ôcwpàcûèl, pronouns are inflected to indicate their role in the sentence (subject, direct object, and so on), as well as to reflect the person, gender, and number of their referents. 

*Personal Pronouns
ôcwpàcûèl personal pronouns (analogous to English I, you, he/she, we, and they) reflect the person and number of their referent, and in the case of the third person, its gender as well. They also reflect the role they play in their clause: subject, direct object, indirect object, or other.

The personal pronouns change form to reflect the role they play in their clause. The forms used for subjects are called the subject pronouns, subjective pronouns, or nominative pronouns. They are as follows: 

**Subject Pronouns
------------------------
Number   | Person           | Subject Pronoun
------------------------
Singular | 1st              | àcàq
         | 2nd (informal)   | îvàv
         | 2nd (formal)     | ègîvôvèc
         | 3rd (masculine)  | èhm
         | 3rd (feminine)   | àcèhèhàc
         | 3rd (neutral)    | pôv
------------------------
Plural   | 1st              | ègîvôvp
         | 2nd              | ègîvôvèc
         | 3rd (masculine)  | ègèhm
         | 3rd (feminine)   | ègàcèhèhàc
------------------------

Note: Whenever the subject pronoun àcàq occurs after àl, àc, m, ôv, îv, ôf, ê, èq, i and some occurrences of ôc, it becomes 'àq.

*Relative pronouns

ôcwpàcûèl, like English, uses relative pronouns to link relative clauses to their head nouns, except that in Ôcwpàcûèl, as in Amharic for instance, the relative clause precedes its head and the relative pronoun, this is why we speak of "head noun" rather than of an "antecedent." The relative pronoun used depends on its grammatical role (such as subject or direct object) within the relative clause.

If the relative pronoun is to be the subject of the relative clause's verb, mîvàf is ordinarily used: àcàvàvàcèhwôfwma àlôq êèhôvèc àl mîvàf àcôqôqôvôc'èh ("the man who stole my bike"). Note that mîvàf in this use does not change form to agree in any way with its head noun: ègàcêèhôvèc êàvê àvpôv mîvàf ègàcàvàvàcèhwôfwma ègàcèh ("the bikes that were stolen").

If the relative pronoun is to be the direct object of the relative clause's verb, àcîvàf (or 'îvàf after àl, àc, m, ôv, îv, ôf, ê, èq, i and some occurrences of ôc) is ordinarily used: àcêèhôvèc àl èhm'îvàf àcàvàvàcèhwôfwma àlèh ("the bicycle that he stole"). Like mîvàf, àcîvàf does not change form to agree with its head noun.


-----
VERBS
-----
Verbs in Ôcwpàcûèl are conjugated to reflect the following information:

    a mood (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, or conditional)
    a tense (past, present, or future, though not all tenses can be combined with all moods)
    an aspect (perfective or imperfective)
    a voice (active, passive, or reflexive)
    Nonfinite forms (e.g., participles, gerunds, infinitives)


Verbs in the finite moods (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, and conditional) are also conjugated to agree with their subjects in person (first, second, or third) and number (singular or plural). As in English, the subject must be included (except in the imperative mood); in other words Ôcwpàcûèl is neither a null-subject nor a pro-drop language.

Auxiliary verbs are combined with past participles of main verbs to produce compound tenses, including the compound past. For most main verbs the auxiliary is (the appropriate form of) ûmôvècàl ("to have"), but for reflexive verbs and certain intransitive verbs the auxiliary is a form of àcûàvi ("to be"). The participle agrees with the subject when the auxiliary is àcûàvi, and with a following direct object (if any) when the auxiliary is ûmôvècàl. Forms of àcûàvi are also used with the past participles of transitive verbs to form the passive voice.

*Morphology

In Ôcwpàcûèl, a verb is inflected to reflect its mood and tense, as well as to agree with its subject in person and number.

**Stems and conjugation prefixes

ôcwpàcûèl verbs have a large number of simple (one-word) forms. These are composed of two distinct parts: the stem (or root, or radix), which indicates which verb it is, and the prefix (inflection), which indicates the verb's tense (imperfect, present, future etc.) and mood and its subject's person (I, you, he/she etc.) and number, though many prefixes can correspond to multiple tense-mood-subject combinations. In certain parts of the second conjugation there is also a prefix -ègègm- between the stem and the ending.

    In àvpàcmàlèhûàluc, the stem -èhûàluc indicates that the verb is ûàcèhûàluc (to speak) and the prefix àvpàcmàl- marks the third-person plural imperfect indicative. "Third person plural" meaning the subject of the verb is "they". The "imperfect indicative" being a tense.
    In ègpôvègègmpmèl, the stem -pmèl indicates that the verb is ûmpmèl (to finish), the prefix -ègègm- precedes it, and the inflection ègpôv- marks the first-person plural present indicative or imperative. The "first-person plural" is the "we" form of a verb. The "present indicative" being a tense and "imperative" being a mood, but in Ôcwpàcûèl they are indistinguishable without context.

These verb conjugations are coupled with a subject pronoun in order to convey who the subject of the verb is (i.e. who is doing the action).

***The principle of the fixed stem

The stem normally stays fixed in the first two conjugations:

    ûàcèhûàluc: ègmàlûàcèhûàluc àcàq, ègàlèhûàluc îvàv, àvpàcègègàlèhûàluc ègèhm'îvàf, ègpôvmèhûàluc ègîvôvp àcîvàf, èvàcèhûàluc...
    ûmpmèl: ègmàlûmpmèl àcàq, ègàcàvjpmèl ègîvôvèc, àvpàcègègmpmèl ègèhm'îvàf, ègmpmèl, ègpôvmègègmpmèl ègîvôvp àcîvàf...

In the third it is often modified, sometimes even between persons in the same tense:

    ûmôvèhîvôvèc: æîvàcèc àcàq, æîvàcèc îvàv, àvîvàcèc èhm, ègpôvèhîvôvèc ègîvôvp, èvàcèhîvôvèc ègîvôvèc, àvpàcèhîvàcèc ègèhm.

But such irregularities apart, the principle is that nothing is removed from the stem. 


**Conjugation prefixes

The conjugation prefix tells us:

    For all verbs, the mood and the tense;
    For finite verbs, the person and the number; and
    For the past participle alone, the gender and the number.

Apart from a few frequent verbs which are considered totally irregular (mainly ûmôvècàl, àcûàvi, ûàcèhèhàl and àcûmàlèl), for each tense of each mood a series of six prefixes (one for each person singular and plural) is associated with a group or subgroup of verbs.


*Formation of simple tenses active

These tenses are not formed with an auxiliary, and their formation is discussed in the following section.

**Infinitive

A verb is normally named by its present infinitive. Starting from this infinitive, the conjugations can be classified into three different groups:

    The first group or first conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with ûàc- (with the exception of ûàcèhèhàl, which due to its numerous irregularities is usually classed as being in the third conjugation):

    ûàcôqmàl, ûàcôfàlèhàla, ûàcàvpàlôcw, ûàcôfôvècpàc, ûàcôqûàcèl, ûàcbpàlôq, ûàcègègàluc, ûàcôfàluc, ûàcpàcôqôvûuc, ûàcàgûàlbàcû, etc.

        For example, for the verb ûàcèhûàluc, the stem is -èhûàluc and the infinitive prefix is ûàc-.

    The second group or second conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with ûm- whose present participle begins with àvpàlègègm-:

    ûmpêa, ûmàvàlucôqôvw, ûmucûàcîvbêàg, ûmûîvàcèhèl, ûmàgpàlûb, ûïàlôc, ûmàvègàcècpm, ûmèhôvuc, ûmbîvôvû, ûmbîvû, ûmèhàlèg, etc.

        For example, for the verb ûmpmèl, the stem is -pmèl and the infinitive prefix is ûm-.

    The third group or third conjugation. This contains all the other verbs.
    
Note that the auxiliaries àcûàvi and ûmôvècàl, although they would naturally seem to belong to the third conjugation, are traditionally classed separately. 

**Present indicative

The present indicative is the form of the verb used to describe an action in the present e.g. àcàgûàlbàcû àcàq means "I watch".

The stem of the present indicative is not always regular and can vary (especially in the third conjugation) and there are three main sets of prefixes:

    Verbs beginning with ûàc- (all verbs of the first group): àc-, ègàc-, àc-, ègpôv-, èvàc-, àvpàc-.
    Verbs beginning with ûm- (all verbs of the second group and most of the third): ègm-, ègm-, àvm-, ègpôvègègm-, èvàcègègm-, àvpàcègègm-. But there are numerous irregularities, especially in the third group.
    Verbs beginning with àcû- (part of the third group): èg-, èg-, - , ègpôv-, èvàc-, àvpàc-.
    
    Example:

1st Group: ûàcàgûàlbàcû (to watch)

Person         | Singular             | Plural
-------------------------------
1st person     | àcàgûàlbàcû àcàq         | ègpôvàgûàlbàcû ègîvôvp
2nd person     | ègàcàgûàlbàcû îvàv        | èvàcàgûàlbàcû ègîvôvèc
3rd person     | àcàgûàlbàcû pôv/àcèhèhàc/èhm | àvpàcàgûàlbàcû ègàcèhèhàc/ègèhm

2nd person     | ègmègmôvôcw îvàv         | èvàcègègmègmôvôcw ègîvôvèc

    Verbs of the second group take an -ègègm- in the plural conjugations.
        
        
**Imperfect indicative

The imperfect indicative is a past tense describing states and actions that were ongoing in the past, e.g. "ègmàlàgûàlbàcû àcàq" means "I was watching".

    The stem of the imperfect indicative is always invariant for a single verb. It is derived in various ways depending on the verb group.
    For the first group, the stem is the infinitive minus the ûàc- prefix, e.g., ûàcàgûàlbàcû -> -àgûàlbàcû.
    For the second group, the stem is the infinitive minus the ûm- prefix plus the ègègm- prefix, e.g., ûmègmôvôcw -> -ègègmègmôvôcw. 
    And for the third group, the stem is derived from the first person plural of the present indicative.

    The conjugation prefixes of this tense are for any of the three groups always: ègmàl-, ègmàl-, àvmàl-, ègpôvm-, èvàcm-, àvpàcmàl-.



    Example:

-------------------------------



    Verb àcûàvi : the stem is -àvê, endings are the same.
    

**Future

The future prefixes correspond to the present indicative of the verb ûmôvècàl. They are always regular: màl-, ègàl-, àl-, ègpôv-, èvàc-, àvpôv-.

    The future stem is simply the infinitive (dictionary form). In other words, to form the future tense these prefixes are added to the infinitive:

        màlûmègmôvôcw àcàq ('I will choose'), ègàlûàcàgûàlbàcû îvàv ('you will watch'), àlûmàvûôvèg àcèhèhàc ('she will exit'), ègpôvûàcèhèhmàlècàlûàv ègîvôvp ('we will work'), èvàcûmbîvôvû ègîvôvèc ('you will blush'), àvpôvûmàvûàluc ègèhm ('they will leave').

    But there are several irregular future stems, especially in the third group.

**Present conditional

The presente conditional prefixes are always regular: ègmàl-, ègmàl-, àvmàl-, ègpôvm-, èvàcm-, àvpàcmàl-.

    The conditional stem is always the same as the future stem:

        ègmàlûmègmôvôcw àcàq ('I would choose'), ègmàlûàcàgûàlbàcû îvàv ('you would watch'), àvmàlûmàvûôvèg àcèhèhàc ('she would exit'), ègpôvmûàcèhèhmàlècàlûàv ègîvôvp ('we would work'), èvàcmûmbîvôvû ègîvôvèc ('you would blush'), àvpàcmàlûmàvûàluc ègèhm ('they would leave').

    Example:

1st Group: ûàcàgûàlbàcû (to look)
-------------------------------
Person         | Singular                | Plural

An adjective must agree in gender and number with the noun it modifies. Îliopîdèol adjectives therefore have four forms: masculine singular, feminine singular, masculine plural, and feminine plural. A few adjectives, like kcîdom and kcîdødkâop, have a fifth form, viz. an additional masculine singular form for use after a noun ending in c, îd, r, â, k, øp, a, z and some occurrences of îl, e.g. oprømècot kcîdom opk (a beautiful garden), îdqqâîl ôîdom opk (a handsome man), îdqqîdol îdôôîdom îdopk (a beautiful woman), uémopcolopîd øgkcîdom uîdô (the beautiful children), uopâurcq uîdôôîdom uîdô (the beautiful houses).

The masculine singular, an adjective's basic form, is listed in dictionaries. Most feminine forms are formed by adding the prefix îd- to the masculine form, e.g., ømopcèv > îdømopcèv, émopîdô > îdémopîdô, opcuèîdøl > îdopcuèîdøl. 

Under certain circumstances, other minor changes occur in the formation of feminine forms. Specifically, masculine adjectives beginning with ôîd-, ôr-, opâ-, opîd-, uâ- or uc- double their initial consonant before adding the prefix îd- (e.g., ôîdkèi > îdôôîdkèi, ôrémopîdv > îdôôrémopîdv, opâom > îdopopâom, opîdriopc > îdopopîdriopc, uâèv > îduuâèv, and ucom > îduucom).

Additionally, adjectives beginning with i- change to îdîli- (e.g., iopcôom > îdîliopcôom); those beginning with èkîd- or øgkîd- change to îdukîd- (e.g., èkîdémémîdqâèøl > îdukîdémémîdqâèøl, øgkîdrèkol > îdukîdrèkol), with the exception of the irregular øgkîdrød (old) whose feminine form is îdôôrîdrød; v- changes to îdkv- (e.g., vopâô > îdkvopâô); olr- changes to îdødr- (e.g., olrémic > îdødrémic); olîd- changes to îdødz- (e.g., olîdèom > îdødzèom); èîd- changes to îdèz- (e.g., èîdvopcèéma > îdèzvopcèéma); émîd- changes to îdémz- (e.g., émîdrkîtopr > îdémzrkîtopr); and adjectives beginning with kâ- have a special form ôâ- (becoming îdôôâ- in feminine) that appears after c, îd, r, â, k, øp, a, z and some occurrences of îl, (e.g., kâol/ôâol > îdôôâol, kâq/ôâq > îdôôâq).

If an adjective's basic form beginning with îd-, it does not change in the feminine (cf. îdîlirè îdqqâîl opk 'a rich man' > îdîlirè îdqqîdol îdopk 'a rich woman').

The plural is normally formed by adding the prefix u- to the singular (masculine and feminine; e.g., rôâot > urôâot, îdrôâot > uîdrôâot). If the basic form beginning with u-, øg-, or øð-, an adjective does not change in the masculine plural (e.g., ucom > ucom, øgkîdèaopav > øgkîdèaopav, øgkâøm > øgkâøm), but its feminine plural form follows the rules detailed above. All Îliopîdèol adjectives beginning with kcîd- take the prefix øg- in the masculine plural (e.g., kcîdødkâop > øgkcîdødkâop). Distinctive plural forms occur with adjectives beginning with ôc-, which normally change to øgkc- in the masculine plural (e.g., ôcopèîdødrîl > øgkcopèîdødrîl, ôcèémopîdi > øgkcèémopîdi), with only two exceptions: ôcémcol > uôcémcol and ôcødcop > uôcødcop which follow the regular pattern. By contrast, the feminine plural is always formed according to the general rule: îdôcèémopîdi > uîdôcèémopîdi.

Adjective placement follows specific patterns. Most adjectives are placed after the noun they modify, and this is particularly true for colors, as in îdvkâè îdô oprød (the red wine). However, certain short, commonly used adjectives – those dealing with beauty, age, goodness, or size (sometimes remembered by the acronym "BAGS") – typically precede their nouns. These are kcîdom (beautiful), opâom (good), olîdèom (brief), ømopcèv (big/tall), uâèv (fat/large), øgkcol (false), émkcîl (high), vopâô (long), olîdèom (brief), îdopkîdot (young), rôâot (pretty), urcødkcq (bad), èkîdôôrîdq (better), kcîdødkâop (new), émrémîdøl (small), øgkîdrød (old); e.g., îdqqîdol îdopk îdôôîdom ("a beautiful woman").

--------
PRONOUNS
--------
In Îliopîdèol, pronouns are inflected to indicate their role in the sentence (subject, direct object, and so on), as well as to reflect the person, gender, and number of their referents. 

*Personal Pronouns
îliopîdèol personal pronouns (analogous to English I, you, he/she, we, and they) reflect the person and number of their referent, and in the case of the third person, its gender as well. They also reflect the role they play in their clause: subject, direct object, indirect object, or other.

The personal pronouns change form to reflect the role they play in their clause. The forms used for subjects are called the subject pronouns, subjective pronouns, or nominative pronouns. They are as follows: 

**Subject Pronouns
------------------------
Number   | Person           | Subject Pronoun
------------------------
Singular | 1st              | îdot
         | 2nd (informal)   | kém
         | 2nd (formal)     | ukâød
         | 3rd (masculine)  | ôr
         | 3rd (feminine)   | îdôôîd
         | 3rd (neutral)    | opâ
------------------------
Plural   | 1st              | ukâop
         | 2nd              | ukâød
         | 3rd (masculine)  | uôr
         | 3rd (feminine)   | uîdôôîd
------------------------

Note: Whenever the subject pronoun îdot occurs after c, îd, r, â, k, øp, a, z, éb and some occurrences of îl, it becomes 'ot.

*Relative pronouns

îliopîdèol, like English, uses relative pronouns to link relative clauses to their head nouns, except that in Îliopîdèol, as in Amharic for instance, the relative clause precedes its head and the relative pronoun, this is why we speak of "head noun" rather than of an "antecedent." The relative pronoun used depends on its grammatical role (such as subject or direct object) within the relative clause.

If the relative pronoun is to be the subject of the relative clause's verb, rkît is ordinarily used: îdémémîdôiøpirom cq aôâød c rkît îdqqâîl'ô ("the man who stole my bike"). Note that rkît in this use does not change form to agree in any way with its head noun: uîdaôâød aéma émopâ rkît uîdémémîdôiøpirom uîdô ("the bikes that were stolen").

If the relative pronoun is to be the direct object of the relative clause's verb, îdkît (or 'kît after c, îd, r, â, k, øp, a, z, éb and some occurrences of îl) is ordinarily used: îdaôâød c ôr'kît îdémémîdôiøpirom cô ("the bicycle that he stole"). Like rkît, îdkît does not change form to agree with its head noun.


-----
VERBS
-----
Verbs in Îliopîdèol are conjugated to reflect the following information:

    a mood (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, or conditional)
    a tense (past, present, or future, though not all tenses can be combined with all moods)
    an aspect (perfective or imperfective)
    a voice (active, passive, or reflexive)
    Nonfinite forms (e.g., participles, gerunds, infinitives)


Verbs in the finite moods (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, and conditional) are also conjugated to agree with their subjects in person (first, second, or third) and number (singular or plural). As in English, the subject must be included (except in the imperative mood); in other words Îliopîdèol is neither a null-subject nor a pro-drop language.

Auxiliary verbs are combined with past participles of main verbs to produce compound tenses, including the compound past. For most main verbs the auxiliary is (the appropriate form of) èrâødc ("to have"), but for reflexive verbs and certain intransitive verbs the auxiliary is a form of îdèéméb ("to be"). The participle agrees with the subject when the auxiliary is îdèéméb, and with a following direct object (if any) when the auxiliary is èrâødc. Forms of îdèéméb are also used with the past participles of transitive verbs to form the passive voice.

*Morphology

In Îliopîdèol, a verb is inflected to reflect its mood and tense, as well as to agree with its subject in person and number.

**Stems and conjugation prefixes

îliopîdèol verbs have a large number of simple (one-word) forms. These are composed of two distinct parts: the stem (or root, or radix), which indicates which verb it is, and the prefix (inflection), which indicates the verb's tense (imperfect, present, future etc.) and mood and its subject's person (I, you, he/she etc.) and number, though many prefixes can correspond to multiple tense-mood-subject combinations. In certain parts of the second conjugation there is also a prefix -uur- between the stem and the ending.

    In émopîdrcôècøl, the stem -ôècøl indicates that the verb is èîdôècøl (to speak) and the prefix émopîdrc- marks the third-person plural imperfect indicative. "Third person plural" meaning the subject of the verb is "they". The "imperfect indicative" being a tense.
    In uopâuuroprol, the stem -oprol indicates that the verb is èroprol (to finish), the prefix -uur- precedes it, and the inflection uopâ- marks the first-person plural present indicative or imperative. The "first-person plural" is the "we" form of a verb. The "present indicative" being a tense and "imperative" being a mood, but in Îliopîdèol they are indistinguishable without context.

These verb conjugations are coupled with a subject pronoun in order to convey who the subject of the verb is (i.e. who is doing the action).

***The principle of the fixed stem

The stem normally stays fixed in the first two conjugations:

    èîdôècøl: urcèîdôècøl îdot, ucôècøl kém, émopîduucôècøl uôr'kît, uopârôècøl ukâop îdkît, øðîdôècøl...
    èroprol: urcèroprol îdot, uîdémeboprol ukâød, émopîduuroprol uôr'kît, uroprol, uopâruuroprol ukâop îdkît...

In the third it is often modified, sometimes even between persons in the same tense:

    èrâôkâød: øgkîdød îdot, øgkîdød kém, émkîdød ôr, uopâôkâød ukâop, øðîdôkâød ukâød, émopîdôkîdød uôr.

But such irregularities apart, the principle is that nothing is removed from the stem. 


**Conjugation prefixes

The conjugation prefix tells us:

    For all verbs, the mood and the tense;
    For finite verbs, the person and the number; and
    For the past participle alone, the gender and the number.

Apart from a few frequent verbs which are considered totally irregular (mainly èrâødc, îdèéméb, èîdôôc and îdèrcol), for each tense of each mood a series of six prefixes (one for each person singular and plural) is associated with a group or subgroup of verbs.


*Formation of simple tenses active

These tenses are not formed with an auxiliary, and their formation is discussed in the following section.

**Infinitive

A verb is normally named by its present infinitive. Starting from this infinitive, the conjugations can be classified into three different groups:

    The first group or first conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with èîd- (with the exception of èîdôôc, which due to its numerous irregularities is usually classed as being in the third conjugation):

    èîdqrc, èîdøpcôcom, èîdémopcîli, èîdøpâødopîd, èîdqèîdol, èîdvopcq, èîduucøl, èîdøpcøl, èîdopîdqâèøl, èîdømècvîdè, etc.

        For example, for the verb èîdôècøl, the stem is -ôècøl and the infinitive prefix is èîd-.

    The second group or second conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with èr- whose present participle begins with émopcuur-:

    èropaom, èrémcølqâi, èrølèîdkvaøm, èrèkîdôol, èrømopcèv, èïcîl, èrémuîdødopr, èrôâøl, èrvkâè, èrvkè, èrôcu, etc.

        For example, for the verb èroprol, the stem is -oprol and the infinitive prefix is èr-.

    The third group or third conjugation. This contains all the other verbs.
    
Note that the auxiliaries îdèéméb and èrâødc, although they would naturally seem to belong to the third conjugation, are traditionally classed separately. 

**Present indicative

The present indicative is the form of the verb used to describe an action in the present e.g. îdømècvîdè îdot means "I watch".

The stem of the present indicative is not always regular and can vary (especially in the third conjugation) and there are three main sets of prefixes:

    Verbs beginning with èr- (all verbs of the second group and most of the third): ur-, ur-, émr-, uopâuur-, øðîduur-, émopîduur-. But there are numerous irregularities, especially in the third group.
    Verbs beginning with îdè- (part of the third group): u-, u-, - , uopâ-, øðîd-, émopîd-.

**Imperfect indicative

The imperfect indicative is a past tense describing states and actions that were ongoing in the past, e.g. "urcømècvîdè îdot" means "I was watching".

**Past participle

Past participles, unlike present participles and gerundives, may be inflected to show gender and number by adding îd- and u- prefixes, as with a normal adjective. Hence, "émrolopâi émrkèol opk", "îdémrolopâi îdèrâøl îdopk", "uémrolopâi uémrkèol uîdøm", and "uîdémrolopâi uîdèrâøl uîdøm."

The plain (masculine singular) form of a past participle begins with a- for the 1st group verbs, and with r- for the 2nd group verbs. Third group verbs have more diverse prefixes : k- (îdèømopîdémopîd kømopîdémopîd, îdèrâom kom, îdèrô kô, etc. and èrâødcu ku, èrâød kød, èrâødkâøl køl), ur- (îdèémémîdq urq, îdèømopîdèøl urèøl, etc.), uk- (îdèkôiopr ukôiopr and îdèkôiîdè ukôiîdè and only these verbs), émr- (îdèrømkcq émrømkcq, îdèrøm émrøm, etc.), ém- (verbs in îdèømopr- : îdèømoprîdøl émoprîdøl), émèîd- (èrèødkâ émèîdødkâ, èrèødkâi émèîdødkâi, èrèololâ émèîdololâ and èrèololkâu émèîdololkâu), or kîd (èrâødc kîd). 

*Compound Tenses

îliopîdèol compound tenses are verb forms that combine an auxiliary verb (either èrâødc or îdèéméb) with the past participle of the main verb. These tenses are used to indicate actions that are completed or relate to another point in time. There are several compound tenses in Îliopîdèol, each serving a specific purpose and adding nuance to the timeline of events.

**Compound Past

The compound past is perhaps the most commonly used compound tense in Îliopîdèol. It is used to describe actions that have been completed in the past and is translated by the English simple past. The auxiliary verb is either èrâødc or îdèéméb in the present tense, preceded by the past participle of the main verb. For example, "avopcq rc'ot" (I ate) or "aødrèèc émuîd ôr" (He arrived). èrâødc is used with most verbs, while îdèéméb is used with a specific group of verbs, particularly those indicating movement or change of state, and with all reflexive verbs. When in doubt, èrâødc should be used by default.

nynahgfab has three articles: a definite article, corresponding in many cases to English the; an indefinite article, corresponding to English a/an; and a partitive article, used roughly like some in English. 

** Definite article
 	
In Nynahgfab, the definite article, analogously to the English word the, is used to indicate a specific noun. However, unlike English, the Nynahgfab article changes based on the noun's gender (masculine or feminine) and number (singular or plural).

The definite article always comes after its noun.

For singular nouns:

- For masculine singular nouns, the article is gx. For example, in the phrase "fuþynyna gx" (the cat), gx shows that the noun fuþynyna (cat) is both singular and masculine.
- For feminine singular nouns, the article is þyx. An example is "htoþoqoþymu þyx" (the house), where þyx shows that htoþoqoþymu (house) is singular and feminine.

For plural nouns, regardless of gender:

- The article is þogx for both masculine and feminine plural nouns. (e.g., "þofuþynyna þogx", the cats; "þohtoþoqoþymu þogx", the houses.)

In summary, gx is used with masculine singular nouns, þyx with feminine singular nouns, and þogx with all plural nouns. This variation in definite articles reflects the grammatical gender and number of nouns in Nynahgfab.

After þy, g, qo, to, þu, e, p, d and some occurrences of ny, the singular masculine article gx becomes 'x.


-----
NOUNS
-----
* Gender
Every Nynahgfab noun has a grammatical gender, either masculine or feminine.

* Number
As in English, Nynahgfab nouns inflect for number, however they do so through prefixation rather than suffixation.

The plural is usually formed from the singular by adding the prefix morpheme þo- (e.g., htoþoqoþymu > þohtoþoqoþymu 'houses'). 

Nouns beginning with þuþy- and þug- take the prefix ð- instead of þo- (e.g., þuþyeþufu > ðþuþyeþufu 'pipes', þugqa > ðþugqa 'games'), except for the nouns þuþyçihþyx, þuþyfafaþyþo, þughþa, and þugxty which form their plural by prefixing the morpheme þo- (e.g., þughþa > þoþughþa 'tires').

Seven nouns beginning with þuto- form their plural with ð-. These are þutohgfi, þutoxxqoþyna, þutotyqony, þutoqaqoty, þutoþa, þutonyna, and þutoqaþutoqa (e.g., þutohgfi > ðþutohgfi 'knees'). All other nouns beginning with þuto-, such as þutoþoqoty or þutofafu, follow the regular plural pattern and take þo- (e.g., þutofafu > þoþutofafu 'holes').

Nouns that begin with þo-, ð- or no- in the singular do not change in the plural (e.g., ðqotofana þyx 'the cross' > ðqotofana þogx 'the crosses').

Nouns that begin with xþy- typically change to ðþuþy- in the plural (e.g., xþyhfaþutoqa > ðþuþyhfaþutoqa 'newspapers'). However, several nouns beginning with xþy- are exceptions to this rule and form their plural by adding þo- instead. These are xþyty, xþyna, xþyèþyhfaþyna, xþynaþynyna, xþyèqofuþogb, xþyfuqonapfa, xþyèfagþo and xþyfipfa (e.g., xþyèqofuþogb gx > þoxþyèqofuþogb þogx).

Similarly, most nouns beginning with xqoþy- change to ðþuþy- in the plural. Examples of this pattern include xqoþyty, xqoþyfatona, xqoþymup, xqoþyfaqoþaþutoþo, xqoþyèþyfafu, and xqoþyfafuqoè (e.g., xqoþyfafuqoè hþu > ðþuþyfafuqoè þogçi 'stained-glass windows'). However, some xqoþy- nouns do not follow this pattern and form their plural with þo-, notably xqoþyfa, xqoþyfaqofufuþy, xqoþyçihþynyna, xqoþyfupçi, xqoþyhfagèþutofi and xqoþyfufatoþa (e.g., xqoþyfa gx > þoxqoþyfa þogx 'the rails').

* Case
Nouns in Nynahgfab are not inflected for any other grammatical categories. (However, personal pronouns are inflected for case and person.)

----------
ADJECTIVES
----------

An adjective must agree in gender and number with the noun it modifies. Nynahgfab adjectives therefore have four forms: masculine singular, feminine singular, masculine plural, and feminine plural. A few adjectives, like þuþygty and þuþygèþutoh, have a fifth form, viz. an additional masculine singular form for use after a noun ending in þy, g, qo, to, þu, e, p, d and some occurrences of ny, e.g. hqoçifaþyqa þuþygty hþu (a beautiful garden), gmumutony xgty hþu (a handsome man), gmumugb gxxgty ghþu (a beautiful woman), þofuhþybhg ðþuþygty þogx (the beautiful children), þohtoþoqoþymu þogxxgty þogx (the beautiful houses).

The masculine singular, an adjective's basic form, is listed in dictionaries. Most feminine forms are formed by adding the prefix g- to the masculine form, e.g., çihþyfafi > gçihþyfafi, fuhgx > gfuhgx, hþyþofagþa > ghþyþofagþa. 

Under certain circumstances, other minor changes occur in the formation of feminine forms. Specifically, masculine adjectives beginning with xg-, xqo-, hto-, hg-, þoto- or þoþy- double their initial consonant before adding the prefix g- (e.g., xgþufana > gxxgþufana, xqofuhgfi > gxxqofuhgfi, htoty > ghhtoty, hgqonahþy > ghhgqonahþy, þotofafi > gþoþotofafi, and þoþyty > gþoþoþyty).

Additionally, adjectives beginning with na- change to gnyna- (e.g., nahþyxty > gnynahþyxty); those beginning with faþug- or ðþug- change to gþoþug- (e.g., faþugfufugmutofaþa > gþoþugfufugmutofaþa, ðþugqofaþub > gþoþugqofaþub), with the exception of the irregular ðþugqoè (old) whose feminine form is gxxqogqoè; fi- changes to gþufi- (e.g., fihtox > gþufihtox); bqo- changes to gèqo- (e.g., bqofunaþy > gèqofunaþy); bg- changes to gèd- (e.g., bgfaty > gèdfaty); fag- changes to gfad- (e.g., fagfihþyfafup > gfadfihþyfafup); fug- changes to gfud- (e.g., fugqoþuçuhqo > gfudqoþuçuhqo); and adjectives beginning with þuto- have a special form xto- (becoming gxxto- in feminine) that appears after þy, g, qo, to, þu, e, p, d and some occurrences of ny, (e.g., þutob/xtob > gxxtob, þutomu/xtomu > gxxtomu).

If an adjective's basic form beginning with g-, it does not change in the feminine (cf. gnynaqofa gmumutony hþu 'a rich man' > gnynaqofa gmumugb ghþu 'a rich woman').

The plural is normally formed by adding the prefix þo- to the singular (masculine and feminine; e.g., qoxtoqa > þoqoxtoqa, gqoxtoqa > þogqoxtoqa). If the basic form beginning with þo-, ð-, or no-, an adjective does not change in the masculine plural (e.g., þoþyty > þoþyty, ðþugfaphpfi > ðþugfaphpfi, ðþutoçi > ðþutoçi), but its feminine plural form follows the rules detailed above. All Nynahgfab adjectives beginning with þuþyg- take the prefix ð- in the masculine plural (e.g., þuþygèþutoh > ðþuþygèþutoh). Distinctive plural forms occur with adjectives beginning with xþy-, which normally change to ðþuþy- in the masculine plural (e.g., xþyhfagèqony > ðþuþyhfagèqony, xþyfafuhgna > ðþuþyfafuhgna), with only two exceptions: xþyfuþyb > þoxþyfuþyb and xþyèþyh > þoxþyèþyh which follow the regular pattern. By contrast, the feminine plural is always formed according to the general rule: gxþyfafuhgna > þogxþyfafuhgna.

Adjective placement follows specific patterns. Most adjectives are placed after the noun they modify, and this is particularly true for colors, as in gfiþutofa gx hqoè (the red wine). However, certain short, commonly used adjectives – those dealing with beauty, age, goodness, or size (sometimes remembered by the acronym "BAGS") – typically precede their nouns. These are þuþygty (beautiful), htoty (good), bgfaty (brief), çihþyfafi (big/tall), þotofafi (fat/large), ðþuþyb (false), fuþuþyny (high), fihtox (long), bgfaty (brief), ghþugqa (young), qoxtoqa (pretty), þoqoþyèþuþymu (bad), faþugxxqogmu (better), þuþygèþutoh (new), fuqofugþa (small), ðþugqoè (old); e.g., gmumugb ghþu gxxgty ("a beautiful woman").

--------
PRONOUNS
--------
In Nynahgfab, pronouns are inflected to indicate their role in the sentence (subject, direct object, and so on), as well as to reflect the person, gender, and number of their referents. 

*Personal Pronouns
nynahgfab personal pronouns (analogous to English I, you, he/she, we, and they) reflect the person and number of their referent, and in the case of the third person, its gender as well. They also reflect the role they play in their clause: subject, direct object, indirect object, or other.

The personal pronouns change form to reflect the role they play in their clause. The forms used for subjects are called the subject pronouns, subjective pronouns, or nominative pronouns. They are as follows: 

**Subject Pronouns
------------------------
Number   | Person           | Subject Pronoun
------------------------
Singular | 1st              | gqa
         | 2nd (informal)   | þufu
         | 2nd (formal)     | þoþutoè
         | 3rd (masculine)  | xqo
         | 3rd (feminine)   | gxxg
         | 3rd (neutral)    | hto
------------------------
Plural   | 1st              | þoþutoh
         | 2nd              | þoþutoè
         | 3rd (masculine)  | þoxqo
         | 3rd (feminine)   | þogxxg
------------------------

Note: Whenever the subject pronoun gqa occurs after þy, g, qo, to, þu, e, p, d, ê and some occurrences of ny, it becomes 'qa.

*Relative pronouns

nynahgfab, like English, uses relative pronouns to link relative clauses to their head nouns, except that in Nynahgfab, as in Amharic for instance, the relative clause precedes its head and the relative pronoun, this is why we speak of "head noun" rather than of an "antecedent." The relative pronoun used depends on its grammatical role (such as subject or direct object) within the relative clause.

If the relative pronoun is to be the subject of the relative clause's verb, qoþuçu is ordinarily used: gfufugxnaenaqoty þymu pxtoè þy qoþuçu gmumutony'x ("the man who stole my bike"). Note that qoþuçu in this use does not change form to agree in any way with its head noun: þogpxtoè pfup fuhto qoþuçu þogfufugxnaenaqoty þogx ("the bikes that were stolen").

If the relative pronoun is to be the direct object of the relative clause's verb, gþuçu (or 'þuçu after þy, g, qo, to, þu, e, p, d, ê and some occurrences of ny) is ordinarily used: gpxtoè þy xqo'þuçu gfufugxnaenaqoty þyx ("the bicycle that he stole"). Like qoþuçu, gþuçu does not change form to agree with its head noun.


-----
VERBS
-----
Verbs in Nynahgfab are conjugated to reflect the following information:

    a mood (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, or conditional)
    a tense (past, present, or future, though not all tenses can be combined with all moods)
    an aspect (perfective or imperfective)
    a voice (active, passive, or reflexive)
    Nonfinite forms (e.g., participles, gerunds, infinitives)


Verbs in the finite moods (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, and conditional) are also conjugated to agree with their subjects in person (first, second, or third) and number (singular or plural). As in English, the subject must be included (except in the imperative mood); in other words Nynahgfab is neither a null-subject nor a pro-drop language.

Auxiliary verbs are combined with past participles of main verbs to produce compound tenses, including the compound past. For most main verbs the auxiliary is (the appropriate form of) faqotoèþy ("to have"), but for reflexive verbs and certain intransitive verbs the auxiliary is a form of gfafuê ("to be"). The participle agrees with the subject when the auxiliary is gfafuê, and with a following direct object (if any) when the auxiliary is faqotoèþy. Forms of gfafuê are also used with the past participles of transitive verbs to form the passive voice.

*Morphology

In Nynahgfab, a verb is inflected to reflect its mood and tense, as well as to agree with its subject in person and number.

**Stems and conjugation prefixes

nynahgfab verbs have a large number of simple (one-word) forms. These are composed of two distinct parts: the stem (or root, or radix), which indicates which verb it is, and the prefix (inflection), which indicates the verb's tense (imperfect, present, future etc.) and mood and its subject's person (I, you, he/she etc.) and number, though many prefixes can correspond to multiple tense-mood-subject combinations. In certain parts of the second conjugation there is also a prefix -þoþoqo- between the stem and the ending.

    In fuhgqoþyxfaþyþa, the stem -xfaþyþa indicates that the verb is fagxfaþyþa (to speak) and the prefix fuhgqoþy- marks the third-person plural imperfect indicative. "Third person plural" meaning the subject of the verb is "they". The "imperfect indicative" being a tense.
    In þohtoþoþoqohqob, the stem -hqob indicates that the verb is faqohqob (to finish), the prefix -þoþoqo- precedes it, and the inflection þohto- marks the first-person plural present indicative or imperative. The "first-person plural" is the "we" form of a verb. The "present indicative" being a tense and "imperative" being a mood, but in Nynahgfab they are indistinguishable without context.

These verb conjugations are coupled with a subject pronoun in order to convey who the subject of the verb is (i.e. who is doing the action).

***The principle of the fixed stem

The stem normally stays fixed in the first two conjugations:

    fagxfaþyþa: þoqoþyfagxfaþyþa gqa, þoþyxfaþyþa þufu, fuhgþoþoþyxfaþyþa þoxqo'þuçu, þohtoqoxfaþyþa þoþutoh gþuçu, nogxfaþyþa...
    faqohqob: þoqoþyfaqohqob gqa, þogfuîhqob þoþutoè, fuhgþoþoqohqob þoxqo'þuçu, þoqohqob, þohtoqoþoþoqohqob þoþutoh gþuçu...

In the third it is often modified, sometimes even between persons in the same tense:

    faqotoxþutoè: ðþugè gqa, ðþugè þufu, fuþugè xqo, þohtoxþutoè þoþutoh, nogxþutoè þoþutoè, fuhgxþugè þoxqo.

But such irregularities apart, the principle is that nothing is removed from the stem. 


**Conjugation prefixes

The conjugation prefix tells us:

    For all verbs, the mood and the tense;
    For finite verbs, the person and the number; and
    For the past participle alone, the gender and the number.

Apart from a few frequent verbs which are considered totally irregular (mainly faqotoèþy, gfafuê, fagxxþy and gfaqoþyb), for each tense of each mood a series of six prefixes (one for each person singular and plural) is associated with a group or subgroup of verbs.


*Formation of simple tenses active

These tenses are not formed with an auxiliary, and their formation is discussed in the following section.

**Infinitive

A verb is normally named by its present infinitive. Starting from this infinitive, the conjugations can be classified into three different groups:

    The first group or first conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with fag- (with the exception of fagxxþy, which due to its numerous irregularities is usually classed as being in the third conjugation):

    fagmuqoþy, fageþyxþyty, fagfuhþynyna, fagetoèhg, fagmufagb, fagfihþymu, fagþoþoþyþa, fageþyþa, faghgmutofaþa, fagçifaþyfigfa, etc.

        For example, for the verb fagxfaþyþa, the stem is -xfaþyþa and the infinitive prefix is fag-.

    The second group or second conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with faqo- whose present participle begins with fuhþyþoþoqo-:

    faqohpty, faqofuþyþamutona, faqoþafagþufipçi, faqofaþugxb, faqoçihþyfafi, faïþyny, faqofuþogèhqo, faqoxtoþa, faqofiþutofa, faqofiþufa, faqoxþyþo, etc.

        For example, for the verb faqohqob, the stem is -hqob and the infinitive prefix is faqo-.

    The third group or third conjugation. This contains all the other verbs.
    
Note that the auxiliaries gfafuê and faqotoèþy, although they would naturally seem to belong to the third conjugation, are traditionally classed separately. 

**Present indicative

The present indicative is the form of the verb used to describe an action in the present e.g. gçifaþyfigfa gqa means "I watch".

The stem of the present indicative is not always regular and can vary (especially in the third conjugation) and there are three main sets of prefixes:

    Verbs beginning with fag- (all verbs of the first group): g-, þog-, g-, þohto-, nog-, fuhg-.
    Verbs beginning with faqo- (all verbs of the second group and most of the third): þoqo-, þoqo-, fuqo-, þohtoþoþoqo-, nogþoþoqo-, fuhgþoþoqo-. But there are numerous irregularities, especially in the third group.
    Verbs beginning with gfa- (part of the third group): þo-, þo-, - , þohto-, nog-, fuhg-.
    
    Example:

-------------------------------

2nd person     | þogçifaþyfigfa þufu        | nogçifaþyfigfa þoþutoè

2nd person     | þoqoþoqotonyna þufu         | nogþoþoqoþoqotonyna þoþutoè

**Imperfect indicative

The imperfect indicative is a past tense describing states and actions that were ongoing in the past, e.g. "þoqoþyçifaþyfigfa gqa" means "I was watching".

    The stem of the imperfect indicative is always invariant for a single verb. It is derived in various ways depending on the verb group.
    For the first group, the stem is the infinitive minus the fag- prefix, e.g., fagçifaþyfigfa -> -çifaþyfigfa.
    For the second group, the stem is the infinitive minus the faqo- prefix plus the þoþoqo- prefix, e.g., faqoþoqotonyna -> -þoþoqoþoqotonyna. 
    And for the third group, the stem is derived from the first person plural of the present indicative.

    The conjugation prefixes of this tense are for any of the three groups always: þoqoþy-, þoqoþy-, fuqoþy-, þohtoqo-, nogqo-, fuhgqoþy-.

-------------------------------
