**Imperfect indicative

The imperfect indicative is a past tense describing states and actions that were ongoing in the past, e.g. "ktezoñiezweñi eñéc" means "I was watching".

    The stem of the imperfect indicative is always invariant for a single verb. It is derived in various ways depending on the verb group.
    For the first group, the stem is the infinitive minus the ieñ- prefix, e.g., ieñoñiezweñi -> -oñiezweñi.
    For the second group, the stem is the infinitive minus the it- prefix plus the kkt- prefix, e.g., itktgvéf -> -kktktgvéf. 
    And for the third group, the stem is derived from the first person plural of the present indicative.

    The conjugation prefixes of this tense are for any of the three groups always: ktez-, ktez-, ntez-, kéñgt-, efeñt-, néñeñtez-.

3rd person     | ntezoñiezweñi éñg/eñyyeñ/yt | néñeñtezoñiezweñi keñyyeñ/kyt

**Future

The future prefixes correspond to the present indicative of the verb itgdez. They are always regular: tez-, kez-, ez-, kéñg-, efeñ-, néñg-.

    The future stem is simply the infinitive (dictionary form). In other words, to form the future tense these prefixes are added to the infinitive:

        tezitktgvéf eñéc ('I will choose'), kezieñoñiezweñi acn ('you will watch'), ezitnigk eñyyeñ ('she will exit'), kéñgieñyytezdezin kacgéñ ('we will work'), efeñitwacgi kacgd ('you will blush'), néñgitniezéj kyt ('they will leave').

    But there are several irregular future stems, especially in the third group.

**Past participle

Past participles, unlike present participles and gerundives, may be inflected to show gender and number by adding eñ- and k- prefixes, as with a normal adjective. Hence, "ntqéñgéf ntaciq éñac", "eñntqéñgéf eñitgéj eñéñac", "kntqéñgéf kntaciq keñoñ", and "keñntqéñgéf keñitgéj keñoñ."

The plain (masculine singular) form of a past participle begins with ém- for the 1st group verbs, and with t- for the 2nd group verbs. Under certain circumstances, other minor changes occur in the formation of feminine forms. Specifically, masculine adjectives beginning with wila-, wir-, lèti-, lèla-, biti- or biç- double their initial consonant before adding the prefix la- (e.g., wilalinatè > lawiwilalinatè, wirmlèlac > lawiwirmlèlac, lètie > lalèlètie, lèlartèlèç > lalèlèlartèlèç, bitinac > labibitinac, and biçe > labibiçe).

Additionally, adjectives beginning with tè- change to laztè- (e.g., tèlèçwie > laztèlèçwie); those beginning with nalila- or galila- change to labilila- (e.g., nalilammlahtinaly > labililammlahtinaly, galilarnalij > labililarnalij), with the exception of the irregular galilarta (old) whose feminine form is lawiwirlarta; c- changes to lalic- (e.g., clètiwi > laliclètiwi); jr- changes to latar- (e.g., jrmtèç > latarmtèç); jla- changes to latau- (e.g., jlanae > lataunae); nala- changes to lanau- (e.g., nalaclèçnamxi > lanauclèçnamxi); mla- changes to lamu- (e.g., mlarliàlèr > lamurliàlèr); and adjectives beginning with liti- have a special form witi- (becoming lawiwiti- in feminine) that appears after ç, la, r, ti, li, lé, xi, u and some occurrences of z, (e.g., litij/witij > lawiwitij, litih/witih > lawiwitih).

If an adjective's basic form beginning with la-, it does not change in the feminine (cf. laztèrna lahhtiz lèli 'a rich man' > laztèrna lahhlaj lalèli 'a rich woman').

The plural is normally formed by adding the prefix bi- to the singular (masculine and feminine; e.g., rwitid > birwitid, larwitid > bilarwitid). If the basic form beginning with bi-, ga-, or xy-, an adjective does not change in the masculine plural (e.g., biçe > biçe, galilanaxilèxic > galilanaxilèxic, galitik > galitik), but its feminine plural form follows the rules detailed above. All Ztèlèlanaj adjectives beginning with liçla- take the prefix ga- in the masculine plural (e.g., liçlatalitilè > galiçlatalitilè). Distinctive plural forms occur with adjectives beginning with wiç-, which normally change to galiç- in the masculine plural (e.g., wiçlènalatarz > galiçlènalatarz, wiçnamlèlatè > galiçnamlèlatè), with only two exceptions: wiçmçj > biwiçmçj and wiçtaçlè > biwiçtaçlè which follow the regular pattern. By contrast, the feminine plural is always formed according to the general rule: lawiçnamlèlatè > bilawiçnamlèlatè.

Adjective placement follows specific patterns. Most adjectives are placed after the noun they modify, and this is particularly true for colors, as in laclitina lawi lèrta (the red wine). However, certain short, commonly used adjectives – those dealing with beauty, age, goodness, or size (sometimes remembered by the acronym "BAGS") – typically precede their nouns. These are liçlae (beautiful), lètie (good), jlanae (brief), klèçnac (big/tall), bitinac (fat/large), galiçj (false), mliçz (high), clètiwi (long), jlanae (brief), lalèlilad (young), rwitid (pretty), birçtaliçh (bad), nalilawiwirlah (better), liçlatalitilè (new), mrmlaly (small), galilarta (old); e.g., lahhlaj lalèli lawiwilae ("a beautiful woman").

--------
PRONOUNS
--------
In Ztèlèlanaj, pronouns are inflected to indicate their role in the sentence (subject, direct object, and so on), as well as to reflect the person, gender, and number of their referents. 

*Personal Pronouns
ztèlèlanaj personal pronouns (analogous to English I, you, he/she, we, and they) reflect the person and number of their referent, and in the case of the third person, its gender as well. They also reflect the role they play in their clause: subject, direct object, indirect object, or other.

The personal pronouns change form to reflect the role they play in their clause. The forms used for subjects are called the subject pronouns, subjective pronouns, or nominative pronouns. They are as follows: 

**Subject Pronouns
------------------------
Number   | Person           | Subject Pronoun
------------------------
Singular | 1st              | lad
         | 2nd (informal)   | lim
         | 2nd (formal)     | bilitita
         | 3rd (masculine)  | wir
         | 3rd (feminine)   | lawiwila
         | 3rd (neutral)    | lèti
------------------------
Plural   | 1st              | bilitilè
         | 2nd              | bilitita
         | 3rd (masculine)  | biwir
         | 3rd (feminine)   | bilawiwila
------------------------

Note: Whenever the subject pronoun lad occurs after ç, la, r, ti, li, lé, xi, u, ê and some occurrences of z, it becomes 'd.

*Relative pronouns

ztèlèlanaj, like English, uses relative pronouns to link relative clauses to their head nouns, except that in Ztèlèlanaj, as in Amharic for instance, the relative clause precedes its head and the relative pronoun, this is why we speak of "head noun" rather than of an "antecedent." The relative pronoun used depends on its grammatical role (such as subject or direct object) within the relative clause.

If the relative pronoun is to be the subject of the relative clause's verb, rlià is ordinarily used: lammlawitèlétère çh xiwitita ç rlià lahhtiz'wi ("the man who stole my bike"). Note that rlià in this use does not change form to agree in any way with its head noun: bilaxiwitita ximxi mlèti rlià bilammlawitèlétère bilawi ("the bikes that were stolen").

If the relative pronoun is to be the direct object of the relative clause's verb, lalià (or 'lià after ç, la, r, ti, li, lé, xi, u, ê and some occurrences of z) is ordinarily used: laxiwitita ç wir'lià lammlawitèlétère çwi ("the bicycle that he stole"). Like rlià, lalià does not change form to agree with its head noun.


-----
VERBS
-----
Verbs in Ztèlèlanaj are conjugated to reflect the following information:

    a mood (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, or conditional)
    a tense (past, present, or future, though not all tenses can be combined with all moods)
    an aspect (perfective or imperfective)
    a voice (active, passive, or reflexive)
    Nonfinite forms (e.g., participles, gerunds, infinitives)


Verbs in the finite moods (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, and conditional) are also conjugated to agree with their subjects in person (first, second, or third) and number (singular or plural). As in English, the subject must be included (except in the imperative mood); in other words Ztèlèlanaj is neither a null-subject nor a pro-drop language.

Auxiliary verbs are combined with past participles of main verbs to produce compound tenses, including the compound past. For most main verbs the auxiliary is (the appropriate form of) nartitaç ("to have"), but for reflexive verbs and certain intransitive verbs the auxiliary is a form of lanamê ("to be"). The participle agrees with the subject when the auxiliary is lanamê, and with a following direct object (if any) when the auxiliary is nartitaç. Forms of lanamê are also used with the past participles of transitive verbs to form the passive voice.

*Morphology

In Ztèlèlanaj, a verb is inflected to reflect its mood and tense, as well as to agree with its subject in person and number.

**Stems and conjugation prefixes

ztèlèlanaj verbs have a large number of simple (one-word) forms. These are composed of two distinct parts: the stem (or root, or radix), which indicates which verb it is, and the prefix (inflection), which indicates the verb's tense (imperfect, present, future etc.) and mood and its subject's person (I, you, he/she etc.) and number, though many prefixes can correspond to multiple tense-mood-subject combinations. In certain parts of the second conjugation there is also a prefix -bibir- between the stem and the ending.

    In mlèlarçwinaçly, the stem -winaçly indicates that the verb is nalawinaçly (to speak) and the prefix mlèlarç- marks the third-person plural imperfect indicative. "Third person plural" meaning the subject of the verb is "they". The "imperfect indicative" being a tense.
    In bilètibibirlèrj, the stem -lèrj indicates that the verb is narlèrj (to finish), the prefix -bibir- precedes it, and the inflection bilèti- marks the first-person plural present indicative or imperative. The "first-person plural" is the "we" form of a verb. The "present indicative" being a tense and "imperative" being a mood, but in Ztèlèlanaj they are indistinguishable without context.

These verb conjugations are coupled with a subject pronoun in order to convey who the subject of the verb is (i.e. who is doing the action).

***The principle of the fixed stem

The stem normally stays fixed in the first two conjugations:

    nalawinaçly: birçnalawinaçly lad, biçwinaçly lim, mlèlabibiçwinaçly biwir'lià, bilètirwinaçly bilitilè lalià, xylawinaçly...
    narlèrj: birçnarlèrj lad, bilamîlèrj bilitita, mlèlabibirlèrj biwir'lià, birlèrj, bilètirbibirlèrj bilitilè lalià...

In the third it is often modified, sometimes even between persons in the same tense:

    nartiwilitita: galilata lad, galilata lim, mlilata wir, bilètiwilitita bilitilè, xylawilitita bilitita, mlèlawililata biwir.

But such irregularities apart, the principle is that nothing is removed from the stem. 


**Conjugation prefixes

The conjugation prefix tells us:

    For all verbs, the mood and the tense;
    For finite verbs, the person and the number; and
    For the past participle alone, the gender and the number.

Apart from a few frequent verbs which are considered totally irregular (mainly nartitaç, lanamê, nalawiwiç and lanarçj), for each tense of each mood a series of six prefixes (one for each person singular and plural) is associated with a group or subgroup of verbs.


*Formation of simple tenses active

These tenses are not formed with an auxiliary, and their formation is discussed in the following section.

**Infinitive

A verb is normally named by its present infinitive. Starting from this infinitive, the conjugations can be classified into three different groups:

    The first group or first conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with nala- (with the exception of nalawiwiç, which due to its numerous irregularities is usually classed as being in the third conjugation):

    nalahrç, nalaléçwiçe, nalamlèçztè, nalalétitalèla, nalahnalaj, nalaclèçh, nalabibiçly, nalaléçly, nalalèlahtinaly, nalaknaçclana, etc.

        For example, for the verb nalawinaçly, the stem is -winaçly and the infinitive prefix is nala-.

    The second group or second conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with nar- whose present participle begins with mlèçbibir-:

    narlèxie, narmçlyhtitè, narlynalalicxik, narnalilawij, narklèçnac, naïçz, narmbilatalèr, narwitily, narclitina, narclina, narwiçbi, etc.

        For example, for the verb narlèrj, the stem is -lèrj and the infinitive prefix is nar-.

    The third group or third conjugation. This contains all the other verbs.
    
Note that the auxiliaries lanamê and nartitaç, although they would naturally seem to belong to the third conjugation, are traditionally classed separately. 

**Present indicative

The present indicative is the form of the verb used to describe an action in the present e.g. laknaçclana lad means "I watch".

The stem of the present indicative is not always regular and can vary (especially in the third conjugation) and there are three main sets of prefixes:

    Verbs beginning with nala- (all verbs of the first group): la-, bila-, la-, bilèti-, xyla-, mlèla-.
    Verbs beginning with nar- (all verbs of the second group and most of the third): bir-, bir-, mr-, bilètibibir-, xylabibir-, mlèlabibir-. But there are numerous irregularities, especially in the third group.
    Verbs beginning with lana- (part of the third group): bi-, bi-, - , bilèti-, xyla-, mlèla-.
    
    Example:

-------------------------------
1st person     | laknaçclana lad         | bilètiknaçclana bilitilè
2nd person     | bilaknaçclana lim        | xylaknaçclana bilitita
3rd person     | laknaçclana lèti/lawiwila/wir | mlèlaknaçclana bilawiwila/biwir
-------------------------------

-------------------------------

2nd person     | birbirtiztè lim         | xylabibirbirtiztè bilitita
3rd person     | mrbirtiztè lèti/lawiwila/wir | mlèlabibirbirtiztè bilawiwila/biwir

**Imperfect indicative

The imperfect indicative is a past tense describing states and actions that were ongoing in the past, e.g. "birçknaçclana lad" means "I was watching".

    The stem of the imperfect indicative is always invariant for a single verb. It is derived in various ways depending on the verb group.
    For the first group, the stem is the infinitive minus the nala- prefix, e.g., nalaknaçclana -> -knaçclana.
    For the second group, the stem is the infinitive minus the nar- prefix plus the bibir- prefix, e.g., narbirtiztè -> -bibirbirtiztè. 
    And for the third group, the stem is derived from the first person plural of the present indicative.

    The conjugation prefixes of this tense are for any of the three groups always: birç-, birç-, mrç-, bilètir-, xylar-, mlèlarç-.

**Future

The future prefixes correspond to the present indicative of the verb nartitaç. They are always regular: rç-, biç-, ç-, bilèti-, xyla-, mlèti-.

**Past participle

Past participles, unlike present participles and gerundives, may be inflected to show gender and number by adding la- and bi- prefixes, as with a normal adjective. Hence, "mrjlètitè mrlinaj lèli", "lamrjlètitè lanartily lalèli", "bimrjlètitè bimrlinaj bilak", and "bilamrjlètitè bilanartily bilak."

The plain (masculine singular) form of a past participle begins with xi- for the 1st group verbs, and with r- for the 2nd group verbs. Third group verbs have more diverse prefixes : li- (lanaklèlamlèla liklèlamlèla, lanartie lie, lanarwi liwi, etc. and nartitaçbi libi, nartita lita, nartitalitily lily), bir- (lanammlah birh, lanaklèlanaly birnaly, etc.), bili- (lanaliwitèlèr biliwitèlèr and lanaliwitèlana biliwitèlana and only these verbs), mr- (lanarkliçh mrkliçh, lanark mrk, etc.), m- (verbs in lanaklèr- : lanaklèrlaly mlèrlaly), mnala- (narnataliti mnalataliti, narnatalititè mnalatalititè, narnajjti mnalajjti and narnajjlitibi mnalajjlitibi), or lila (nartitaç lila). 

*Compound Tenses

ztèlèlanaj compound tenses are verb forms that combine an auxiliary verb (either nartitaç or lanamê) with the past participle of the main verb. These tenses are used to indicate actions that are completed or relate to another point in time. There are several compound tenses in Ztèlèlanaj, each serving a specific purpose and adding nuance to the timeline of events.

**Compound Past

The compound past is perhaps the most commonly used compound tense in Ztèlèlanaj. It is used to describe actions that have been completed in the past and is translated by the English simple past. The auxiliary verb is either nartitaç or lanamê in the present tense, preceded by the past participle of the main verb. For example, "xiclèçh rç'd" (I ate) or "xitarnanaç mbila wir" (He arrived). nartitaç is used with most verbs, while lanamê is used with a specific group of verbs, particularly those indicating movement or change of state, and with all reflexive verbs. When in doubt, nartitaç should be used by default.

*Past participle agreement

The past participle is used in three ways in Ztèlèlanaj: as an adjective, in the passive construction, and in the compound tense constructions. When it is used as an adjective, it follows all the regular adjective agreement rules. In passive constructions, it always agrees with the passive subject.

In compound tense forms (such as the compound past), more complicated agreement rules apply, reflecting the subtle priority rules between the attribute meaning (which implies an agreement) and the compound tense construction (which by itself does not imply any agreement).

A. The auxiliary verb is nartitaç.

    If there is no direct object (the verb is intransitive) or the direct object appears before the past participle, then the past participle does not agree (i.e., it takes the default masculine singular form).
        (intransitive) rhnatik mlèti bilawiwila. ("They (fem.) slept.")
        (direct object before verb) bilalèrlawiçe galilak lita ç lanarçwitè. ("lanarçwitè saw two whales.")
    If there is a direct object and it appears after the past participle, then the participle must agree with it. Three cases:
        (pronoun after the auxiliary) bilalèrlawiçe galilak mrçtaç lé wir. bilalita ç bilawi lanarçwitè. ("There were two whales. lanarçwitè saw them.")
        (clause-final wh-question element)  bilalita lawiwila-m-ç lanarçwitè bilalèrlawiçe bilawiwilalià? ("Which whales did lanarçwitè see?")
        (relative clause linked by lalià) bilalita ç lanarçwitè lalià bilalèrlawiçe galilak bilawi ("the two whales that lanarçwitè saw")
    The above rule is one of the most difficult in Ztèlèlanaj.

B. The auxiliary is lanamê, and the verb is not reflexive. The past participle agrees with the subject:

        bilaxitarnanaç mlètibi bilawiwila. ("They (fem.) arrived.")

C. The auxiliary is lanamê and the verb is reflexive. The agreement rules are in fact the same as those for structures with nartitaç in A, keeping in mind that the reflexive pronoun corresponds to either the direct object or the indirect object of the verb.

    There is no direct object, or the direct object appears before the past participle → no agreement. In these cases, the reflexive pronoun expresses the indirect object.
        (no direct object) xikxitètèlibi mlètibi labi bilawiwila. xiwinaçly bilahhtibi bilitilè bilitilè. ("They (fem.) succeeded one another. We spoke with each other.")
        (direct object before verb) bilètirmbilalià bilak xibitily mlètibi labi bilawiwila. ("They (fem.) asked each other some questions.")
        
    There is a direct object and it appears after the past participle. → The past participle agrees with this object.

    The first three cases are the same as in A.2 above (the reflexive pronoun is the indirect object).
        (direct object pronoun) lamnaçm lalèli mrçj rç'd. laxicçmnaçly mlètibi çwi labi bimlèçjlèla bilawi. ("I made a pie. The children shared it.")
        (wh-question)  laxicçmnaçly biwir-mlètibi labi lamnaçm lawiwilalià? ("Which pie did they share?")
        (lalià relative) laxicçmnaçly mlètibi labi bimlèçjlèla bilawi lalià lamnaçm çwi ("the pie that the children shared")

    The reflexive pronoun can itself be the direct object, in which case the participle agrees with it (and therefore with the subject). This also includes "inherently reflexive" verbs, for which the reflexive pronoun cannot be interpreted semantically as an object (direct or indirect) of the verb.

For singular nouns:

- For masculine singular nouns, the article is avx. For example, in the phrase "evuþlo avx" (the cat), avx shows that the noun evuþlo (cat) is both singular and masculine.
- For feminine singular nouns, the article is uþx. An example is "àybehajuþc uþx" (the house), where uþx shows that àybehajuþc (house) is singular and feminine.

For plural nouns, regardless of gender:

- The article is ehavx for both masculine and feminine plural nouns. (e.g., "ehevuþlo ehavx", the cats; "ehàybehajuþc ehavx", the houses.)

In summary, avx is used with masculine singular nouns, uþx with feminine singular nouns, and ehavx with all plural nouns. This variation in definite articles reflects the grammatical gender and number of nouns in Loàavigw.

After uþ, av, aj, yb, n, r, z, è and some occurrences of l, the singular masculine article avx becomes 'x.


-----
NOUNS
-----
* Gender
Every Loàavigw noun has a grammatical gender, either masculine or feminine.

* Number
As in English, Loàavigw nouns inflect for number, however they do so through prefixation rather than suffixation.

The plural is usually formed from the singular by adding the prefix morpheme eh- (e.g., àybehajuþc > ehàybehajuþc 'houses'). 

Nouns beginning with nuþ- and nav- take the prefix ug- instead of eh- (e.g., nuþrnev > ugnuþrnev 'pipes', navd > ugnavd 'games'), except for the nouns nuþñàuþx, nuþigiguþeh, navàé, and navxç which form their plural by prefixing the morpheme eh- (e.g., navàé > ehnavàé 'tires').

Seven nouns beginning with nyb- form their plural with ug-. These are nybàavm, nybxxajuþo, nybçajl, nybdajç, nybé, nyblo, and nybdnybd (e.g., nybàavm > ugnybàavm 'knees'). All other nouns beginning with nyb-, such as nybehajç or nybigev, follow the regular plural pattern and take eh- (e.g., nybigev > ehnybigev 'holes').

Nouns that begin with eh-, ug- or eb- in the singular do not change in the plural (e.g., ugajybigo uþx 'the cross' > ugajybigo ehavx 'the crosses').

Nouns that begin with xuþ- typically change to ugnuþ- in the plural (e.g., xuþàignybd > ugnuþàignybd 'newspapers'). However, several nouns beginning with xuþ- are exceptions to this rule and form their plural by adding eh- instead. These are xuþç, xuþo, xuþyvuþàiguþo, xuþouþlo, xuþyvajevehavw, xuþevajozig, xuþyvigaveh and xuþmzig (e.g., xuþyvajevehavw avx > ehxuþyvajevehavw ehavx).

Similarly, most nouns beginning with xajuþ- change to ugnuþ- in the plural. Examples of this pattern include xajuþç, xajuþigybo, xajuþcz, xajuþigajénybeh, xajuþyvuþigev, and xajuþigevajyv (e.g., xajuþigevajyv àn > ugnuþigevajyv ehavñ 'stained-glass windows'). However, some xajuþ- nouns do not follow this pattern and form their plural with eh-, notably xajuþig, xajuþigajevevuþ, xajuþñàuþlo, xajuþevzñ, xajuþàigavyvnybm and xajuþevigybé (e.g., xajuþig avx > ehxajuþig ehavx 'the rails').

* Case
Nouns in Loàavigw are not inflected for any other grammatical categories. (However, personal pronouns are inflected for case and person.)

----------
ADJECTIVES
----------

An adjective must agree in gender and number with the noun it modifies. Loàavigw adjectives therefore have four forms: masculine singular, feminine singular, masculine plural, and feminine plural. A few adjectives, like nuþavç and nuþavyvnybà, have a fifth form, viz. an additional masculine singular form for use after a noun ending in uþ, av, aj, yb, n, r, z, è and some occurrences of l, e.g. àajñiguþd nuþavç àn (a beautiful garden), avccybl xavç àn (a handsome man), avccavw avxxavç avàn (a beautiful woman), ehevàuþwàav ugnuþavç ehavx (the beautiful children), ehàybehajuþc ehavxxavç ehavx (the beautiful houses).

The masculine singular, an adjective's basic form, is listed in dictionaries. Most feminine forms are formed by adding the prefix av- to the masculine form, e.g., ñàuþigm > avñàuþigm, evàavx > avevàavx, àuþehigavé > avàuþehigavé. 

Under certain circumstances, other minor changes occur in the formation of feminine forms. Specifically, masculine adjectives beginning with xav-, xaj-, àyb-, àav-, ehyb- or ehuþ- double their initial consonant before adding the prefix av- (e.g., xavnigo > avxxavnigo, xajevàavm > avxxajevàavm, àybç > avààybç, àavajoàuþ > avààavajoàuþ, ehybigm > avehehybigm, and ehuþç > avehehuþç).

Additionally, adjectives beginning with o- change to avlo- (e.g., oàuþxç > avloàuþxç); those beginning with ignav- or ugnav- change to avehnav- (e.g., ignavevevavcybigé > avehnavevevavcybigé, ugnavajignw > avehnavajignw), with the exception of the irregular ugnavajyv (old) whose feminine form is avxxajavajyv; m- changes to avnm- (e.g., màybx > avnmàybx); waj- changes to avyvaj- (e.g., wajevouþ > avyvajevouþ); wav- changes to avyvè- (e.g., wavigç > avyvèigç); igav- changes to avigè- (e.g., igavmàuþigevz > avigèmàuþigevz); evav- changes to avevè- (e.g., evavajnujàaj > avevèajnujàaj); and adjectives beginning with nyb- have a special form xyb- (becoming avxxyb- in feminine) that appears after uþ, av, aj, yb, n, r, z, è and some occurrences of l, (e.g., nybw/xybw > avxxybw, nybc/xybc > avxxybc).

If an adjective's basic form beginning with av-, it does not change in the feminine (cf. avloajig avccybl àn 'a rich man' > avloajig avccavw avàn 'a rich woman').

The plural is normally formed by adding the prefix eh- to the singular (masculine and feminine; e.g., ajxybd > ehajxybd, avajxybd > ehavajxybd). If the basic form beginning with eh-, ug-, or eb-, an adjective does not change in the masculine plural (e.g., ehuþç > ehuþç, ugnavigzàzm > ugnavigzàzm, ugnybñ > ugnybñ), but its feminine plural form follows the rules detailed above. All Loàavigw adjectives beginning with nuþav- take the prefix ug- in the masculine plural (e.g., nuþavyvnybà > ugnuþavyvnybà). Distinctive plural forms occur with adjectives beginning with xuþ-, which normally change to ugnuþ- in the masculine plural (e.g., xuþàigavyvajl > ugnuþàigavyvajl, xuþigevàavo > ugnuþigevàavo), with only two exceptions: xuþevuþw > ehxuþevuþw and xuþyvuþà > ehxuþyvuþà which follow the regular pattern. By contrast, the feminine plural is always formed according to the general rule: avxuþigevàavo > ehavxuþigevàavo.

Adjective placement follows specific patterns. Most adjectives are placed after the noun they modify, and this is particularly true for colors, as in avmnybig avx àajyv (the red wine). However, certain short, commonly used adjectives – those dealing with beauty, age, goodness, or size (sometimes remembered by the acronym "BAGS") – typically precede their nouns. These are nuþavç (beautiful), àybç (good), wavigç (brief), ñàuþigm (big/tall), ehybigm (fat/large), ugnuþw (false), evnuþl (high), màybx (long), wavigç (brief), avànavd (young), ajxybd (pretty), ehajuþyvnuþc (bad), ignavxxajavc (better), nuþavyvnybà (new), evajevavé (small), ugnavajyv (old); e.g., avccavw avàn avxxavç ("a beautiful woman").

--------
PRONOUNS
--------
In Loàavigw, pronouns are inflected to indicate their role in the sentence (subject, direct object, and so on), as well as to reflect the person, gender, and number of their referents. 

*Personal Pronouns
loàavigw personal pronouns (analogous to English I, you, he/she, we, and they) reflect the person and number of their referent, and in the case of the third person, its gender as well. They also reflect the role they play in their clause: subject, direct object, indirect object, or other.

The personal pronouns change form to reflect the role they play in their clause. The forms used for subjects are called the subject pronouns, subjective pronouns, or nominative pronouns. They are as follows: 

**Subject Pronouns
------------------------
Number   | Person           | Subject Pronoun
------------------------
Singular | 1st              | avd
         | 2nd (informal)   | nev
         | 2nd (formal)     | ehnybyv
         | 3rd (masculine)  | xaj
         | 3rd (feminine)   | avxxav
         | 3rd (neutral)    | àyb
------------------------
Plural   | 1st              | ehnybà
         | 2nd              | ehnybyv
         | 3rd (masculine)  | ehxaj
         | 3rd (feminine)   | ehavxxav
------------------------

Note: Whenever the subject pronoun avd occurs after uþ, av, aj, yb, n, r, z, è, ê and some occurrences of l, it becomes 'd.

*Relative pronouns

loàavigw, like English, uses relative pronouns to link relative clauses to their head nouns, except that in Loàavigw, as in Amharic for instance, the relative clause precedes its head and the relative pronoun, this is why we speak of "head noun" rather than of an "antecedent." The relative pronoun used depends on its grammatical role (such as subject or direct object) within the relative clause.

If the relative pronoun is to be the subject of the relative clause's verb, ajnuj is ordinarily used: avevevavxoroajç uþc zxybyv uþ ajnuj avccybl'x ("the man who stole my bike"). Note that ajnuj in this use does not change form to agree in any way with its head noun: ehavzxybyv zevz evàyb ajnuj ehavevevavxoroajç ehavx ("the bikes that were stolen").

If the relative pronoun is to be the direct object of the relative clause's verb, avnuj (or 'nuj after uþ, av, aj, yb, n, r, z, è, ê and some occurrences of l) is ordinarily used: avzxybyv uþ xaj'nuj avevevavxoroajç uþx ("the bicycle that he stole"). Like ajnuj, avnuj does not change form to agree with its head noun.


-----
VERBS
-----
Verbs in Loàavigw are conjugated to reflect the following information:

    a mood (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, or conditional)
    a tense (past, present, or future, though not all tenses can be combined with all moods)
    an aspect (perfective or imperfective)
    a voice (active, passive, or reflexive)
    Nonfinite forms (e.g., participles, gerunds, infinitives)


Verbs in the finite moods (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, and conditional) are also conjugated to agree with their subjects in person (first, second, or third) and number (singular or plural). As in English, the subject must be included (except in the imperative mood); in other words Loàavigw is neither a null-subject nor a pro-drop language.

Auxiliary verbs are combined with past participles of main verbs to produce compound tenses, including the compound past. For most main verbs the auxiliary is (the appropriate form of) igajybyvuþ ("to have"), but for reflexive verbs and certain intransitive verbs the auxiliary is a form of avigevê ("to be"). The participle agrees with the subject when the auxiliary is avigevê, and with a following direct object (if any) when the auxiliary is igajybyvuþ. Forms of avigevê are also used with the past participles of transitive verbs to form the passive voice.

*Morphology

In Loàavigw, a verb is inflected to reflect its mood and tense, as well as to agree with its subject in person and number.

**Stems and conjugation prefixes

loàavigw verbs have a large number of simple (one-word) forms. These are composed of two distinct parts: the stem (or root, or radix), which indicates which verb it is, and the prefix (inflection), which indicates the verb's tense (imperfect, present, future etc.) and mood and its subject's person (I, you, he/she etc.) and number, though many prefixes can correspond to multiple tense-mood-subject combinations. In certain parts of the second conjugation there is also a prefix -ehehaj- between the stem and the ending.

    In evàavajuþxiguþé, the stem -xiguþé indicates that the verb is igavxiguþé (to speak) and the prefix evàavajuþ- marks the third-person plural imperfect indicative. "Third person plural" meaning the subject of the verb is "they". The "imperfect indicative" being a tense.
    In ehàybehehajàajw, the stem -àajw indicates that the verb is igajàajw (to finish), the prefix -ehehaj- precedes it, and the inflection ehàyb- marks the first-person plural present indicative or imperative. The "first-person plural" is the "we" form of a verb. The "present indicative" being a tense and "imperative" being a mood, but in Loàavigw they are indistinguishable without context.

These verb conjugations are coupled with a subject pronoun in order to convey who the subject of the verb is (i.e. who is doing the action).

***The principle of the fixed stem

The stem normally stays fixed in the first two conjugations:

    igavxiguþé: ehajuþigavxiguþé avd, ehuþxiguþé nev, evàavehehuþxiguþé ehxaj'nuj, ehàybajxiguþé ehnybà avnuj, ebavxiguþé...
    igajàajw: ehajuþigajàajw avd, ehavevîàajw ehnybyv, evàavehehajàajw ehxaj'nuj, ehajàajw, ehàybajehehajàajw ehnybà avnuj...

In the third it is often modified, sometimes even between persons in the same tense:

    igajybxnybyv: ugnavyv avd, ugnavyv nev, evnavyv xaj, ehàybxnybyv ehnybà, ebavxnybyv ehnybyv, evàavxnavyv ehxaj.

But such irregularities apart, the principle is that nothing is removed from the stem. 


**Conjugation prefixes

The conjugation prefix tells us:

    For all verbs, the mood and the tense;
    For finite verbs, the person and the number; and
    For the past participle alone, the gender and the number.

Apart from a few frequent verbs which are considered totally irregular (mainly igajybyvuþ, avigevê, igavxxuþ and avigajuþw), for each tense of each mood a series of six prefixes (one for each person singular and plural) is associated with a group or subgroup of verbs.


*Formation of simple tenses active

These tenses are not formed with an auxiliary, and their formation is discussed in the following section.

**Infinitive

A verb is normally named by its present infinitive. Starting from this infinitive, the conjugations can be classified into three different groups:

    The first group or first conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with igav- (with the exception of igavxxuþ, which due to its numerous irregularities is usually classed as being in the third conjugation):

    igavcajuþ, igavruþxuþç, igavevàuþlo, igavrybyvàav, igavcigavw, igavmàuþc, igavehehuþé, igavruþé, igavàavcybigé, igavñiguþmavig, etc.

        For example, for the verb igavxiguþé, the stem is -xiguþé and the infinitive prefix is igav-.

    The second group or second conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with igaj- whose present participle begins with evàuþehehaj-:

    igajàzç, igajevuþécybo, igajéigavnmzñ, igajignavxw, igajñàuþigm, igïuþl, igajevehavyvàaj, igajxybé, igajmnybig, igajmnig, igajxuþeh, etc.

        For example, for the verb igajàajw, the stem is -àajw and the infinitive prefix is igaj-.

    The third group or third conjugation. This contains all the other verbs.
    
Note that the auxiliaries avigevê and igajybyvuþ, although they would naturally seem to belong to the third conjugation, are traditionally classed separately. 

**Present indicative

The present indicative is the form of the verb used to describe an action in the present e.g. avñiguþmavig avd means "I watch".

The stem of the present indicative is not always regular and can vary (especially in the third conjugation) and there are three main sets of prefixes:

    Verbs beginning with igav- (all verbs of the first group): av-, ehav-, av-, ehàyb-, ebav-, evàav-.
    Verbs beginning with igaj- (all verbs of the second group and most of the third): ehaj-, ehaj-, evaj-, ehàybehehaj-, ebavehehaj-, evàavehehaj-. But there are numerous irregularities, especially in the third group.
    Verbs beginning with avig- (part of the third group): eh-, eh-, - , ehàyb-, ebav-, evàav-.
    
    Example:

Person         | Singular             | Plural
-------------------------------
1st person     | avñiguþmavig avd         | ehàybñiguþmavig ehnybà
2nd person     | ehavñiguþmavig nev        | ebavñiguþmavig ehnybyv
3rd person     | avñiguþmavig àyb/avxxav/xaj | evàavñiguþmavig ehavxxav/ehxaj
-------------------------------

-------------------------------

2nd person     | ehajehajyblo nev         | ebavehehajehajyblo ehnybyv

    Verbs of the second group take an -ehehaj- in the plural conjugations.
        
        
**Imperfect indicative

The imperfect indicative is a past tense describing states and actions that were ongoing in the past, e.g. "ehajuþñiguþmavig avd" means "I was watching".

    The stem of the imperfect indicative is always invariant for a single verb. It is derived in various ways depending on the verb group.
    For the first group, the stem is the infinitive minus the igav- prefix, e.g., igavñiguþmavig -> -ñiguþmavig.
    For the second group, the stem is the infinitive minus the igaj- prefix plus the ehehaj- prefix, e.g., igajehajyblo -> -ehehajehajyblo. 
    And for the third group, the stem is derived from the first person plural of the present indicative.

    The conjugation prefixes of this tense are for any of the three groups always: ehajuþ-, ehajuþ-, evajuþ-, ehàybaj-, ebavaj-, evàavajuþ-.

    Verb avigevê : the stem is -evz, endings are the same.
    

**Future

The future prefixes correspond to the present indicative of the verb igajybyvuþ. They are always regular: ajuþ-, ehuþ-, uþ-, ehàyb-, ebav-, evàyb-.

**Past participle

Past participles, unlike present participles and gerundives, may be inflected to show gender and number by adding av- and eh- prefixes, as with a normal adjective. Hence, "evajwàybo evajnigw àn", "avevajwàybo avigajybé avàn", "ehevajwàybo ehevajnigw ehavñ", and "ehavevajwàybo ehavigajybé ehavñ."

The plain (masculine singular) form of a past participle begins with z- for the 1st group verbs, and with aj- for the 2nd group verbs. All Làtijfecé adjectives beginning with eçegf- take the prefix p- in the masculine plural (e.g., eçegfreçèvij > peçegfreçèvij). Distinctive plural forms occur with adjectives beginning with weg-, which normally change to peçeg- in the masculine plural (e.g., wegijecfryl > peçegijecfryl, wegecbijfàt > peçegecbijfàt), with only two exceptions: wegbegé > imwegbegé and wegregij > imwegregij which follow the regular pattern. By contrast, the feminine plural is always formed according to the general rule: fwegecbijfàt > imfwegecbijfàt.

Adjective placement follows specific patterns. Most adjectives are placed after the noun they modify, and this is particularly true for colors, as in foveçèvec fw ijyr (the red wine). However, certain short, commonly used adjectives – those dealing with beauty, age, goodness, or size (sometimes remembered by the acronym "BAGS") – typically precede their nouns. These are eçegfz (beautiful), ijèvz (good), éfecz (brief), otijegecov (big/tall), imèvecov (fat/large), peçegé (false), beçegl (high), ovijèvw (long), éfecz (brief), fijeçfèj (young), ywèvèj (pretty), imyegreçegèn (bad), eceçfwwyfèn (better), eçegfreçèvij (new), bybfq (small), peçfyr (old); e.g., fènènfé fijeç fwwfz ("a beautiful woman").

PRONOUNS
--------
In Làtijfecé, pronouns are inflected to indicate their role in the sentence (subject, direct object, and so on), as well as to reflect the person, gender, and number of their referents. 

*Personal Pronouns
làtijfecé personal pronouns (analogous to English I, you, he/she, we, and they) reflect the person and number of their referent, and in the case of the third person, its gender as well. They also reflect the role they play in their clause: subject, direct object, indirect object, or other.

The personal pronouns change form to reflect the role they play in their clause. The forms used for subjects are called the subject pronouns, subjective pronouns, or nominative pronouns. They are as follows: 

**Subject Pronouns
------------------------
Number   | Person           | Subject Pronoun
------------------------
Singular | 1st              | fèj
         | 2nd (informal)   | eçb
         | 2nd (formal)     | imeçèvr
         | 3rd (masculine)  | wy
         | 3rd (feminine)   | fwwf
         | 3rd (neutral)    | ijèv
------------------------
Plural   | 1st              | imeçèvij
         | 2nd              | imeçèvr
         | 3rd (masculine)  | imwy
         | 3rd (feminine)   | imfwwf
------------------------

Note: Whenever the subject pronoun fèj occurs after eg, f, y, èv, eç, àd, h, a, ê and some occurrences of l, it becomes 'èj.

*Relative pronouns

làtijfecé, like English, uses relative pronouns to link relative clauses to their head nouns, except that in Làtijfecé, as in Amharic for instance, the relative clause precedes its head and the relative pronoun, this is why we speak of "head noun" rather than of an "antecedent." The relative pronoun used depends on its grammatical role (such as subject or direct object) within the relative clause.

If the relative pronoun is to be the subject of the relative clause's verb, yeçod is ordinarily used: fbbfwàtàdàtyz egèn hwèvr eg yeçod fènènèvl'w ("the man who stole my bike"). Note that yeçod in this use does not change form to agree in any way with its head noun: imfhwèvr hbh bijèv yeçod imfbbfwàtàdàtyz imfw ("the bikes that were stolen").

If the relative pronoun is to be the direct object of the relative clause's verb, feçod (or 'eçod after eg, f, y, èv, eç, àd, h, a, ê and some occurrences of l) is ordinarily used: fhwèvr eg wy'eçod fbbfwàtàdàtyz egw ("the bicycle that he stole"). Like yeçod, feçod does not change form to agree with its head noun.


-----
VERBS
-----
Verbs in Làtijfecé are conjugated to reflect the following information:

    a mood (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, or conditional)
    a tense (past, present, or future, though not all tenses can be combined with all moods)
    an aspect (perfective or imperfective)
    a voice (active, passive, or reflexive)
    Nonfinite forms (e.g., participles, gerunds, infinitives)


Verbs in the finite moods (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, and conditional) are also conjugated to agree with their subjects in person (first, second, or third) and number (singular or plural). As in English, the subject must be included (except in the imperative mood); in other words Làtijfecé is neither a null-subject nor a pro-drop language.

Auxiliary verbs are combined with past participles of main verbs to produce compound tenses, including the compound past. For most main verbs the auxiliary is (the appropriate form of) ecyèvreg ("to have"), but for reflexive verbs and certain intransitive verbs the auxiliary is a form of fecbê ("to be"). The participle agrees with the subject when the auxiliary is fecbê, and with a following direct object (if any) when the auxiliary is ecyèvreg. Forms of fecbê are also used with the past participles of transitive verbs to form the passive voice.

*Morphology

In Làtijfecé, a verb is inflected to reflect its mood and tense, as well as to agree with its subject in person and number.

**Stems and conjugation prefixes

làtijfecé verbs have a large number of simple (one-word) forms. These are composed of two distinct parts: the stem (or root, or radix), which indicates which verb it is, and the prefix (inflection), which indicates the verb's tense (imperfect, present, future etc.) and mood and its subject's person (I, you, he/she etc.) and number, though many prefixes can correspond to multiple tense-mood-subject combinations. In certain parts of the second conjugation there is also a prefix -imimy- between the stem and the ending.

    In bijfyegwecegq, the stem -wecegq indicates that the verb is ecfwecegq (to speak) and the prefix bijfyeg- marks the third-person plural imperfect indicative. "Third person plural" meaning the subject of the verb is "they". The "imperfect indicative" being a tense.
    In imijèvimimyijyé, the stem -ijyé indicates that the verb is ecyijyé (to finish), the prefix -imimy- precedes it, and the inflection imijèv- marks the first-person plural present indicative or imperative. The "first-person plural" is the "we" form of a verb. The "present indicative" being a tense and "imperative" being a mood, but in Làtijfecé they are indistinguishable without context.

These verb conjugations are coupled with a subject pronoun in order to convey who the subject of the verb is (i.e. who is doing the action).

***The principle of the fixed stem

The stem normally stays fixed in the first two conjugations:

    ecfwecegq: imyegecfwecegq fèj, imegwecegq eçb, bijfimimegwecegq imwy'eçod, imijèvywecegq imeçèvij feçod, etfwecegq...
    ecyijyé: imyegecyijyé fèj, imfbîijyé imeçèvr, bijfimimyijyé imwy'eçod, imyijyé, imijèvyimimyijyé imeçèvij feçod...

In the third it is often modified, sometimes even between persons in the same tense:

    ecyèvweçèvr: peçfr fèj, peçfr eçb, beçfr wy, imijèvweçèvr imeçèvij, etfweçèvr imeçèvr, bijfweçfr imwy.

But such irregularities apart, the principle is that nothing is removed from the stem. 


**Conjugation prefixes

The conjugation prefix tells us:

    For all verbs, the mood and the tense;
    For finite verbs, the person and the number; and
    For the past participle alone, the gender and the number.

Apart from a few frequent verbs which are considered totally irregular (mainly ecyèvreg, fecbê, ecfwweg and fecyegé), for each tense of each mood a series of six prefixes (one for each person singular and plural) is associated with a group or subgroup of verbs.


*Formation of simple tenses active

These tenses are not formed with an auxiliary, and their formation is discussed in the following section.

**Infinitive

A verb is normally named by its present infinitive. Starting from this infinitive, the conjugations can be classified into three different groups:

    The first group or first conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with ecf- (with the exception of ecfwweg, which due to its numerous irregularities is usually classed as being in the third conjugation):

    ecfènyeg, ecfàdegwegz, ecfbijeglàt, ecfàdèvrijf, ecfènecfé, ecfovijegèn, ecfimimegq, ecfàdegq, ecfijfènèvecq, ecfotecegovfec, etc.

        For example, for the verb ecfwecegq, the stem is -wecegq and the infinitive prefix is ecf-.

    The second group or second conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with ecy- whose present participle begins with bijegimimy-:

    ecyijhz, ecybegqènèvàt, ecyqecfeçovhot, ecyeceçfwé, ecyotijegecov, ecïegl, ecybimfrijy, ecywèvq, ecyoveçèvec, ecyoveçec, ecywegim, etc.

        For example, for the verb ecyijyé, the stem is -ijyé and the infinitive prefix is ecy-.

    The third group or third conjugation. This contains all the other verbs.
    
Note that the auxiliaries fecbê and ecyèvreg, although they would naturally seem to belong to the third conjugation, are traditionally classed separately. 

**Present indicative

The present indicative is the form of the verb used to describe an action in the present e.g. fotecegovfec fèj means "I watch".

The stem of the present indicative is not always regular and can vary (especially in the third conjugation) and there are three main sets of prefixes:

    Verbs beginning with ecf- (all verbs of the first group): f-, imf-, f-, imijèv-, etf-, bijf-.
    Verbs beginning with ecy- (all verbs of the second group and most of the third): imy-, imy-, by-, imijèvimimy-, etfimimy-, bijfimimy-. But there are numerous irregularities, especially in the third group.
    Verbs beginning with fec- (part of the third group): im-, im-, - , imijèv-, etf-, bijf-.

**Imperfect indicative

The imperfect indicative is a past tense describing states and actions that were ongoing in the past, e.g. "imyegotecegovfec fèj" means "I was watching".

    The stem of the imperfect indicative is always invariant for a single verb. It is derived in various ways depending on the verb group.

**Past participle

Past participles, unlike present participles and gerundives, may be inflected to show gender and number by adding f- and im- prefixes, as with a normal adjective. Hence, "byéijèvàt byeçecé ijeç", "fbyéijèvàt fecyèvq fijeç", "imbyéijèvàt imbyeçecé imfot", and "imfbyéijèvàt imfecyèvq imfot."

The plain (masculine singular) form of a past participle begins with h- for the 1st group verbs, and with y- for the 2nd group verbs. Third group verbs have more diverse prefixes : eç- (fecotijfbijf eçotijfbijf, fecyèvz eçz, fecyw eçw, etc. and ecyèvregim eçim, ecyèvr eçr, ecyèvreçèvq eçq), imy- (fecbbfèn imyèn, fecotijfecq imyecq, etc.), imeç- (feceçwàtijy imeçwàtijy and feceçwàtfec imeçwàtfec and only these verbs), by- (fecyoteçegèn byoteçegèn, fecyot byot, etc.), b- (verbs in fecotijy- : fecotijyfq bijyfq), becf- (ecyecreçèv becfreçèv, ecyecreçèvàt becfreçèvàt, ecyecééèv becfééèv and ecyecééeçèvim becfééeçèvim), or eçf (ecyèvreg eçf). 

*Compound Tenses

làtijfecé compound tenses are verb forms that combine an auxiliary verb (either ecyèvreg or fecbê) with the past participle of the main verb. These tenses are used to indicate actions that are completed or relate to another point in time. There are several compound tenses in Làtijfecé, each serving a specific purpose and adding nuance to the timeline of events.

**Compound Past

The compound past is perhaps the most commonly used compound tense in Làtijfecé. It is used to describe actions that have been completed in the past and is translated by the English simple past. The auxiliary verb is either ecyèvreg or fecbê in the present tense, preceded by the past participle of the main verb. For example, "hovijegèn yeg'èj" (I ate) or "hryececeg bimf wy" (He arrived). ecyèvreg is used with most verbs, while fecbê is used with a specific group of verbs, particularly those indicating movement or change of state, and with all reflexive verbs. When in doubt, ecyèvreg should be used by default.

*Past participle agreement

The past participle is used in three ways in Làtijfecé: as an adjective, in the passive construction, and in the compound tense constructions. When it is used as an adjective, it follows all the regular adjective agreement rules. In passive constructions, it always agrees with the passive subject.

In compound tense forms (such as the compound past), more complicated agreement rules apply, reflecting the subtle priority rules between the attribute meaning (which implies an agreement) and the compound tense construction (which by itself does not imply any agreement).

A. The auxiliary verb is ecyèvreg.

    If there is no direct object (the verb is intransitive) or the direct object appears before the past participle, then the past participle does not agree (i.e., it takes the default masculine singular form).
        (intransitive) yènecèvot bijèv imfwwf. ("They (fem.) slept.")
        (direct object before verb) imfijyfwegz peçfot eçr eg fecyegwàt. ("fecyegwàt saw two whales.")
    If there is a direct object and it appears after the past participle, then the participle must agree with it. Three cases:
        (pronoun after the auxiliary) imfijyfwegz peçfot byegreg àd wy. imfeçr eg imfw fecyegwàt. ("There were two whales. fecyegwàt saw them.")
        (clause-final wh-question element)  imfeçr fwwf-b-eg fecyegwàt imfijyfwegz imfwwfeçod? ("Which whales did fecyegwàt see?")
        (relative clause linked by feçod) imfeçr eg fecyegwàt feçod imfijyfwegz peçfot imfw ("the two whales that fecyegwàt saw")
    The above rule is one of the most difficult in Làtijfecé.

B. The auxiliary is fecbê, and the verb is not reflexive. The past participle agrees with the subject:

        imfhryececeg bijèvim imfwwf. ("They (fem.) arrived.")

C. The auxiliary is fecbê and the verb is reflexive. The agreement rules are in fact the same as those for structures with ecyèvreg in A, keeping in mind that the reflexive pronoun corresponds to either the direct object or the indirect object of the verb.

    There is no direct object, or the direct object appears before the past participle → no agreement. In these cases, the reflexive pronoun expresses the indirect object.
        (no direct object) hothàtàteçim bijèvim fim imfwwf. hwecegq imfènènèvim imeçèvij imeçèvij. ("They (fem.) succeeded one another. We spoke with each other.")
        (direct object before verb) imijèvybimfeçod imfot himèvq bijèvim fim imfwwf. ("They (fem.) asked each other some questions.")
        
    There is a direct object and it appears after the past participle. → The past participle agrees with this object.

    The first three cases are the same as in A.2 above (the reflexive pronoun is the indirect object).
        (direct object pronoun) fbecegb fijeç byegé yeg'èj. fhovegbecegq bijèvim egw fim imbijegéijf imfw. ("I made a pie. The children shared it.")
        (wh-question)  fhovegbecegq imwy-bijèvim fim fbecegb fwwfeçod? ("Which pie did they share?")
        (feçod relative) fhovegbecegq bijèvim fim imbijegéijf imfw feçod fbecegb egw ("the pie that the children shared")

    The reflexive pronoun can itself be the direct object, in which case the participle agrees with it (and therefore with the subject). This also includes "inherently reflexive" verbs, for which the reflexive pronoun cannot be interpreted semantically as an object (direct or indirect) of the verb.
        (ordinary reflexive) imfyryeçim bijèvim fim imfwwf. imheçwegim imfènènèvim imeçèvij imeçèvij. ("They (fem.) followed each other. We greeted each other.")
        (inherently reflexive) yèvèn fot imheçodèvèn bijèvim fim imwy. bijfènfijhrh'w fot imeçijfreçèvim imfènènèvim imeçèvij imeçèvij. ("They made fun of me. We remembered the event.")

In summary, qw is used with masculine singular nouns, ðw with feminine singular nouns, and tqw with all plural nouns. This variation in definite articles reflects the grammatical gender and number of nouns in Uhcyrqèreh.

After ð, q, þ, eb, o, l, à, yh and some occurrences of uh, the singular masculine article qw becomes 'w.


-----
NOUNS
-----
* Gender
Every Uhcyrqèreh noun has a grammatical gender, either masculine or feminine.

* Number
As in English, Uhcyrqèreh nouns inflect for number, however they do so through prefixation rather than suffixation.

The plural is usually formed from the singular by adding the prefix morpheme t- (e.g., yrebtþðyk > tyrebtþðyk 'houses'). 

Nouns beginning with oð- and oq- take the prefix en- instead of t- (e.g., oðloyb > enoðloyb 'pipes', oqé > enoqé 'games'), except for the nouns oðyjyrðw, oðèrèrðt, oqyrv, and oqwñ which form their plural by prefixing the morpheme t- (e.g., oqyrv > toqyrv 'tires').

Seven nouns beginning with oeb- form their plural with en-. These are oebyrqar, oebwwþðc, oebñþuh, oebéþñ, oebv, oebuhc, and oebéoebé (e.g., oebyrqar > enoebyrqar 'knees'). All other nouns beginning with oeb-, such as oebtþñ or oebèryb, follow the regular plural pattern and take t- (e.g., oebèryb > toebèryb 'holes').

Nouns that begin with t-, en- or z- in the singular do not change in the plural (e.g., enþebèrc ðw 'the cross' > enþebèrc tqw 'the crosses').

Nouns that begin with wð- typically change to enoð- in the plural (e.g., wðyrèroebé > enoðyrèroebé 'newspapers'). However, several nouns beginning with wð- are exceptions to this rule and form their plural by adding t- instead. These are wðñ, wðc, wðuçðyrèrðc, wðcðuhc, wðuçþybtqeh, wðybþcàèr, wðuçèrqt and wðaràèr (e.g., wðuçþybtqeh qw > twðuçþybtqeh tqw).

Similarly, most nouns beginning with wþð- change to enoð- in the plural. Examples of this pattern include wþðñ, wþðèrebc, wþðykà, wþðèrþvoebt, wþðuçðèryb, and wþðèrybþuç (e.g., wþðèrybþuç yro > enoðèrybþuç tqyj 'stained-glass windows'). However, some wþð- nouns do not follow this pattern and form their plural with t-, notably wþðèr, wþðèrþybybð, wþðyjyrðuhc, wþðybàyj, wþðyrèrquçoebar and wþðybèrebv (e.g., wþðèr qw > twþðèr tqw 'the rails').

* Case
Nouns in Uhcyrqèreh are not inflected for any other grammatical categories. (However, personal pronouns are inflected for case and person.)

----------
ADJECTIVES
----------

An adjective must agree in gender and number with the noun it modifies. Uhcyrqèreh adjectives therefore have four forms: masculine singular, feminine singular, masculine plural, and feminine plural. A few adjectives, like oðqñ and oðquçoebyr, have a fifth form, viz. an additional masculine singular form for use after a noun ending in ð, q, þ, eb, o, l, à, yh and some occurrences of uh, e.g. yrþyjèrðé oðqñ yro (a beautiful garden), qykykebuh wqñ yro (a handsome man), qykykqeh qwwqñ qyro (a beautiful woman), tybyrðehyrq enoðqñ tqw (the beautiful children), tyrebtþðyk tqwwqñ tqw (the beautiful houses).

The masculine singular, an adjective's basic form, is listed in dictionaries. Most feminine forms are formed by adding the prefix q- to the masculine form, e.g., yjyrðèrar > qyjyrðèrar, ybyrqw > qybyrqw, yrðtèrqv > qyrðtèrqv. 

Under certain circumstances, other minor changes occur in the formation of feminine forms. Specifically, masculine adjectives beginning with wq-, wþ-, yreb-, yrq-, teb- or tð- double their initial consonant before adding the prefix q- (e.g., wqoèrc > qwwqoèrc, wþybyrqar > qwwþybyrqar, yrebñ > qyryrebñ, yrqþcyrð > qyryrqþcyrð, tebèrar > qttebèrar, and tðñ > qttðñ).

Additionally, adjectives beginning with c- change to quhc- (e.g., cyrðwñ > quhcyrðwñ); those beginning with èroq- or enoq- change to qtoq- (e.g., èroqybybqykebèrv > qtoqybybqykebèrv, enoqþèroeh > qtoqþèroeh), with the exception of the irregular enoqþuç (old) whose feminine form is qwwþqþuç; ar- changes to qoar- (e.g., aryrebw > qoaryrebw); ehþ- changes to quçþ- (e.g., ehþybcð > quçþybcð); ehq- changes to quçyh- (e.g., ehqèrñ > quçyhèrñ); èrq- changes to qèryh- (e.g., èrqaryrðèrybà > qèryharyrðèrybà); ybq- changes to qybyh- (e.g., ybqþogyrþ > qybyhþogyrþ); and adjectives beginning with oeb- have a special form web- (becoming qwweb- in feminine) that appears after ð, q, þ, eb, o, l, à, yh and some occurrences of uh, (e.g., oebeh/webeh > qwwebeh, oebyk/webyk > qwwebyk).

If an adjective's basic form beginning with q-, it does not change in the feminine (cf. quhcþèr qykykebuh yro 'a rich man' > quhcþèr qykykqeh qyro 'a rich woman').

The plural is normally formed by adding the prefix t- to the singular (masculine and feminine; e.g., þwebé > tþwebé, qþwebé > tqþwebé). If the basic form beginning with t-, en-, or z-, an adjective does not change in the masculine plural (e.g., tðñ > tðñ, enoqèràyràar > enoqèràyràar, enoebyj > enoebyj), but its feminine plural form follows the rules detailed above. All Uhcyrqèreh adjectives beginning with oðq- take the prefix en- in the masculine plural (e.g., oðquçoebyr > enoðquçoebyr). Distinctive plural forms occur with adjectives beginning with wð-, which normally change to enoð- in the masculine plural (e.g., wðyrèrquçþuh > enoðyrèrquçþuh, wðèrybyrqc > enoðèrybyrqc), with only two exceptions: wðybðeh > twðybðeh and wðuçðyr > twðuçðyr which follow the regular pattern. By contrast, the feminine plural is always formed according to the general rule: qwðèrybyrqc > tqwðèrybyrqc.

Adjective placement follows specific patterns. Most adjectives are placed after the noun they modify, and this is particularly true for colors, as in qaroebèr qw yrþuç (the red wine). However, certain short, commonly used adjectives – those dealing with beauty, age, goodness, or size (sometimes remembered by the acronym "BAGS") – typically precede their nouns. These are oðqñ (beautiful), yrebñ (good), ehqèrñ (brief), yjyrðèrar (big/tall), tebèrar (fat/large), enoðeh (false), yboðuh (high), aryrebw (long), ehqèrñ (brief), qyroqé (young), þwebé (pretty), tþðuçoðyk (bad), èroqwwþqyk (better), oðquçoebyr (new), ybþybqv (small), enoqþuç (old); e.g., qykykqeh qyro qwwqñ ("a beautiful woman").

--------
PRONOUNS
--------
In Uhcyrqèreh, pronouns are inflected to indicate their role in the sentence (subject, direct object, and so on), as well as to reflect the person, gender, and number of their referents. 

*Personal Pronouns
uhcyrqèreh personal pronouns (analogous to English I, you, he/she, we, and they) reflect the person and number of their referent, and in the case of the third person, its gender as well. They also reflect the role they play in their clause: subject, direct object, indirect object, or other.

The personal pronouns change form to reflect the role they play in their clause. The forms used for subjects are called the subject pronouns, subjective pronouns, or nominative pronouns. They are as follows: 

**Subject Pronouns
------------------------

------------------------
Singular | 1st              | qé
         | 2nd (informal)   | oyb
         | 2nd (formal)     | toebuç
         | 3rd (masculine)  | wþ
         | 3rd (feminine)   | qwwq
         | 3rd (neutral)    | yreb
------------------------
Plural   | 1st              | toebyr
         | 2nd              | toebuç
         | 3rd (masculine)  | twþ
         | 3rd (feminine)   | tqwwq
------------------------

Note: Whenever the subject pronoun qé occurs after ð, q, þ, eb, o, l, à, yh, ê and some occurrences of uh, it becomes 'é.

*Relative pronouns

uhcyrqèreh, like English, uses relative pronouns to link relative clauses to their head nouns, except that in Uhcyrqèreh, as in Amharic for instance, the relative clause precedes its head and the relative pronoun, this is why we speak of "head noun" rather than of an "antecedent." The relative pronoun used depends on its grammatical role (such as subject or direct object) within the relative clause.

If the relative pronoun is to be the subject of the relative clause's verb, þog is ordinarily used: qybybqwclcþñ ðyk àwebuç ð þog qykykebuh'w ("the man who stole my bike"). Note that þog in this use does not change form to agree in any way with its head noun: tqàwebuç àybà ybyreb þog tqybybqwclcþñ tqw ("the bikes that were stolen").

If the relative pronoun is to be the direct object of the relative clause's verb, qog (or 'og after ð, q, þ, eb, o, l, à, yh, ê and some occurrences of uh) is ordinarily used: qàwebuç ð wþ'og qybybqwclcþñ ðw ("the bicycle that he stole"). Like þog, qog does not change form to agree with its head noun.


-----
VERBS
-----
Verbs in Uhcyrqèreh are conjugated to reflect the following information:

    a mood (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, or conditional)
    a tense (past, present, or future, though not all tenses can be combined with all moods)
    an aspect (perfective or imperfective)
    a voice (active, passive, or reflexive)
    Nonfinite forms (e.g., participles, gerunds, infinitives)


Verbs in the finite moods (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, and conditional) are also conjugated to agree with their subjects in person (first, second, or third) and number (singular or plural). As in English, the subject must be included (except in the imperative mood); in other words Uhcyrqèreh is neither a null-subject nor a pro-drop language.

Auxiliary verbs are combined with past participles of main verbs to produce compound tenses, including the compound past. For most main verbs the auxiliary is (the appropriate form of) èrþebuçð ("to have"), but for reflexive verbs and certain intransitive verbs the auxiliary is a form of qèrybê ("to be"). The participle agrees with the subject when the auxiliary is qèrybê, and with a following direct object (if any) when the auxiliary is èrþebuçð. Forms of qèrybê are also used with the past participles of transitive verbs to form the passive voice.

*Morphology

In Uhcyrqèreh, a verb is inflected to reflect its mood and tense, as well as to agree with its subject in person and number.

**Stems and conjugation prefixes

uhcyrqèreh verbs have a large number of simple (one-word) forms. These are composed of two distinct parts: the stem (or root, or radix), which indicates which verb it is, and the prefix (inflection), which indicates the verb's tense (imperfect, present, future etc.) and mood and its subject's person (I, you, he/she etc.) and number, though many prefixes can correspond to multiple tense-mood-subject combinations. In certain parts of the second conjugation there is also a prefix -ttþ- between the stem and the ending.

    In ybyrqþðwèrðv, the stem -wèrðv indicates that the verb is èrqwèrðv (to speak) and the prefix ybyrqþð- marks the third-person plural imperfect indicative. "Third person plural" meaning the subject of the verb is "they". The "imperfect indicative" being a tense.
    In tyrebttþyrþeh, the stem -yrþeh indicates that the verb is èrþyrþeh (to finish), the prefix -ttþ- precedes it, and the inflection tyreb- marks the first-person plural present indicative or imperative. The "first-person plural" is the "we" form of a verb. The "present indicative" being a tense and "imperative" being a mood, but in Uhcyrqèreh they are indistinguishable without context.

These verb conjugations are coupled with a subject pronoun in order to convey who the subject of the verb is (i.e. who is doing the action).

***The principle of the fixed stem

The stem normally stays fixed in the first two conjugations:

    èrqwèrðv: tþðèrqwèrðv qé, tðwèrðv oyb, ybyrqttðwèrðv twþ'og, tyrebþwèrðv toebyr qog, zqwèrðv...
    èrþyrþeh: tþðèrþyrþeh qé, tqybîyrþeh toebuç, ybyrqttþyrþeh twþ'og, tþyrþeh, tyrebþttþyrþeh toebyr qog...

In the third it is often modified, sometimes even between persons in the same tense:

    èrþebwoebuç: enoquç qé, enoquç oyb, yboquç wþ, tyrebwoebuç toebyr, zqwoebuç toebuç, ybyrqwoquç twþ.

But such irregularities apart, the principle is that nothing is removed from the stem. 


**Conjugation prefixes

The conjugation prefix tells us:

    For all verbs, the mood and the tense;
    For finite verbs, the person and the number; and
    For the past participle alone, the gender and the number.

Apart from a few frequent verbs which are considered totally irregular (mainly èrþebuçð, qèrybê, èrqwwð and qèrþðeh), for each tense of each mood a series of six prefixes (one for each person singular and plural) is associated with a group or subgroup of verbs.


*Formation of simple tenses active

These tenses are not formed with an auxiliary, and their formation is discussed in the following section.

**Infinitive

A verb is normally named by its present infinitive. Starting from this infinitive, the conjugations can be classified into three different groups:

    The first group or first conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with èrq- (with the exception of èrqwwð, which due to its numerous irregularities is usually classed as being in the third conjugation):

    èrqykþð, èrqlðwðñ, èrqybyrðuhc, èrqlebuçyrq, èrqykèrqeh, èrqaryrðyk, èrqttðv, èrqlðv, èrqyrqykebèrv, èrqyjèrðarqèr, etc.

        For example, for the verb èrqwèrðv, the stem is -wèrðv and the infinitive prefix is èrq-.

    The second group or second conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with èrþ- whose present participle begins with ybyrðttþ-:

    èrþyràñ, èrþybðvykebc, èrþvèrqoaràyj, èrþèroqweh, èrþyjyrðèrar, èrïðuh, èrþybtquçyrþ, èrþwebv, èrþaroebèr, èrþaroèr, èrþwðt, etc.

    The third group or third conjugation. This contains all the other verbs.
    
Note that the auxiliaries qèrybê and èrþebuçð, although they would naturally seem to belong to the third conjugation, are traditionally classed separately.

If the basic form beginning with g-, ñ-, or t-, an adjective does not change in the masculine plural (e.g., gédj > gédj, ñqfuçuheduhud > ñqfuçuheduhud, ñqépa > ñqépa), but its feminine plural form follows the rules detailed above. All Èébedfuçuk adjectives beginning with qédf- take the prefix ñ- in the masculine plural (e.g., qédfikqéped > ñqédfikqéped). Distinctive plural forms occur with adjectives beginning with éwéd-, which normally change to ñqéd- in the masculine plural (e.g., éwédeduçfikizè > ñqédeduçfikizè, éwéduçmedféb > ñqéduçmedféb), with only two exceptions: éwédméduk > géwédméduk and éwédikéded > géwédikéded which follow the regular pattern. By contrast, the feminine plural is always formed according to the general rule: féwéduçmedféb > gféwéduçmedféb.

Adjective placement follows specific patterns. Most adjectives are placed after the noun they modify, and this is particularly true for colors, as in fudqépuç féw edizik (the red wine). However, certain short, commonly used adjectives – those dealing with beauty, age, goodness, or size (sometimes remembered by the acronym "BAGS") – typically precede their nouns. These are qédfj (beautiful), edépj (good), ukfuçj (brief), aedéduçud (big/tall), gépuçud (fat/large), ñqéduk (false), mqédè (high), udedépéw (long), ukfuçj (brief), fedqfy (young), izéwépy (pretty), gizédikqédeh (bad), uçqféwéwizfeh (better), qédfikqéped (new), mizmfoç (small), ñqfizik (old); e.g., fehehfuk fedq féwéwfj ("a beautiful woman").

--------
PRONOUNS
--------
In Èébedfuçuk, pronouns are inflected to indicate their role in the sentence (subject, direct object, and so on), as well as to reflect the person, gender, and number of their referents. 

*Personal Pronouns
èébedfuçuk personal pronouns (analogous to English I, you, he/she, we, and they) reflect the person and number of their referent, and in the case of the third person, its gender as well. They also reflect the role they play in their clause: subject, direct object, indirect object, or other.

The personal pronouns change form to reflect the role they play in their clause. The forms used for subjects are called the subject pronouns, subjective pronouns, or nominative pronouns. They are as follows: 

**Subject Pronouns
------------------------
Number   | Person           | Subject Pronoun
------------------------
Singular | 1st              | fy
         | 2nd (informal)   | qm
         | 2nd (formal)     | gqépik
         | 3rd (masculine)  | éwiz
         | 3rd (feminine)   | féwéwf
         | 3rd (neutral)    | edép
------------------------
Plural   | 1st              | gqéped
         | 2nd              | gqépik
         | 3rd (masculine)  | géwiz
         | 3rd (feminine)   | gféwéwf
------------------------

Note: Whenever the subject pronoun fy occurs after éd, f, iz, ép, q, eç, uh, uw, ê and some occurrences of è, it becomes 'y.

*Relative pronouns

èébedfuçuk, like English, uses relative pronouns to link relative clauses to their head nouns, except that in Èébedfuçuk, as in Amharic for instance, the relative clause precedes its head and the relative pronoun, this is why we speak of "head noun" rather than of an "antecedent." The relative pronoun used depends on its grammatical role (such as subject or direct object) within the relative clause.

If the relative pronoun is to be the subject of the relative clause's verb, izqob is ordinarily used: fmmféwébeçébizj édeh uhéwépik éd izqob fehehépè'éw ("the man who stole my bike"). Note that izqob in this use does not change form to agree in any way with its head noun: gfuhéwépik uhmuh medép izqob gfmmféwébeçébizj gféw ("the bikes that were stolen").

If the relative pronoun is to be the direct object of the relative clause's verb, fqob (or 'qob after éd, f, iz, ép, q, eç, uh, uw, ê and some occurrences of è) is ordinarily used: fuhéwépik éd éwiz'qob fmmféwébeçébizj édéw ("the bicycle that he stole"). Like izqob, fqob does not change form to agree with its head noun.


-----
VERBS
-----
Verbs in Èébedfuçuk are conjugated to reflect the following information:

    a mood (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, or conditional)
    a tense (past, present, or future, though not all tenses can be combined with all moods)
    an aspect (perfective or imperfective)
    a voice (active, passive, or reflexive)
    Nonfinite forms (e.g., participles, gerunds, infinitives)


Verbs in the finite moods (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, and conditional) are also conjugated to agree with their subjects in person (first, second, or third) and number (singular or plural). As in English, the subject must be included (except in the imperative mood); in other words Èébedfuçuk is neither a null-subject nor a pro-drop language.

Auxiliary verbs are combined with past participles of main verbs to produce compound tenses, including the compound past. For most main verbs the auxiliary is (the appropriate form of) uçizépikéd ("to have"), but for reflexive verbs and certain intransitive verbs the auxiliary is a form of fuçmê ("to be"). The participle agrees with the subject when the auxiliary is fuçmê, and with a following direct object (if any) when the auxiliary is uçizépikéd. Forms of fuçmê are also used with the past participles of transitive verbs to form the passive voice.

*Morphology

In Èébedfuçuk, a verb is inflected to reflect its mood and tense, as well as to agree with its subject in person and number.

**Stems and conjugation prefixes

èébedfuçuk verbs have a large number of simple (one-word) forms. These are composed of two distinct parts: the stem (or root, or radix), which indicates which verb it is, and the prefix (inflection), which indicates the verb's tense (imperfect, present, future etc.) and mood and its subject's person (I, you, he/she etc.) and number, though many prefixes can correspond to multiple tense-mood-subject combinations. In certain parts of the second conjugation there is also a prefix -ggiz- between the stem and the ending.

    In medfizédéwuçédoç, the stem -éwuçédoç indicates that the verb is uçféwuçédoç (to speak) and the prefix medfizéd- marks the third-person plural imperfect indicative. "Third person plural" meaning the subject of the verb is "they". The "imperfect indicative" being a tense.
    In gedépggizedizuk, the stem -edizuk indicates that the verb is uçizedizuk (to finish), the prefix -ggiz- precedes it, and the inflection gedép- marks the first-person plural present indicative or imperative. The "first-person plural" is the "we" form of a verb. The "present indicative" being a tense and "imperative" being a mood, but in Èébedfuçuk they are indistinguishable without context.

These verb conjugations are coupled with a subject pronoun in order to convey who the subject of the verb is (i.e. who is doing the action).

***The principle of the fixed stem

The stem normally stays fixed in the first two conjugations:

    uçféwuçédoç: gizéduçféwuçédoç fy, gédéwuçédoç qm, medfggédéwuçédoç géwiz'qob, gedépizéwuçédoç gqéped fqob, tféwuçédoç...
    uçizedizuk: gizéduçizedizuk fy, gfmîedizuk gqépik, medfggizedizuk géwiz'qob, gizedizuk, gedépizggizedizuk gqéped fqob...

In the third it is often modified, sometimes even between persons in the same tense:

    uçizépéwqépik: ñqfik fy, ñqfik qm, mqfik éwiz, gedépéwqépik gqéped, tféwqépik gqépik, medféwqfik géwiz.

But such irregularities apart, the principle is that nothing is removed from the stem. 


**Conjugation prefixes

The conjugation prefix tells us:

    For all verbs, the mood and the tense;
    For finite verbs, the person and the number; and
    For the past participle alone, the gender and the number.

Apart from a few frequent verbs which are considered totally irregular (mainly uçizépikéd, fuçmê, uçféwéwéd and fuçizéduk), for each tense of each mood a series of six prefixes (one for each person singular and plural) is associated with a group or subgroup of verbs.


*Formation of simple tenses active

These tenses are not formed with an auxiliary, and their formation is discussed in the following section.

**Infinitive

A verb is normally named by its present infinitive. Starting from this infinitive, the conjugations can be classified into three different groups:

    The first group or first conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with uçf- (with the exception of uçféwéwéd, which due to its numerous irregularities is usually classed as being in the third conjugation):

    uçfehizéd, uçfeçédéwédj, uçfmedédèéb, uçfeçépikedf, uçfehuçfuk, uçfudedédeh, uçfggédoç, uçfeçédoç, uçfedfehépuçoç, uçfauçédudfuç, etc.

        For example, for the verb uçféwuçédoç, the stem is -éwuçédoç and the infinitive prefix is uçf-.

    The second group or second conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with uçiz- whose present participle begins with medédggiz-:

    uçizeduhj, uçizmédoçehépéb, uçizoçuçfquduha, uçizuçqféwuk, uçizaedéduçud, uçïédè, uçizmgfikediz, uçizéwépoç, uçizudqépuç, uçizudquç, uçizéwédg, etc.

        For example, for the verb uçizedizuk, the stem is -edizuk and the infinitive prefix is uçiz-.

    The third group or third conjugation. This contains all the other verbs.
    
Note that the auxiliaries fuçmê and uçizépikéd, although they would naturally seem to belong to the third conjugation, are traditionally classed separately. 

**Present indicative

The present indicative is the form of the verb used to describe an action in the present e.g. fauçédudfuç fy means "I watch".

The stem of the present indicative is not always regular and can vary (especially in the third conjugation) and there are three main sets of prefixes:

    Verbs beginning with uçf- (all verbs of the first group): f-, gf-, f-, gedép-, tf-, medf-.
    Verbs beginning with uçiz- (all verbs of the second group and most of the third): giz-, giz-, miz-, gedépggiz-, tfggiz-, medfggiz-. But there are numerous irregularities, especially in the third group.
    Verbs beginning with fuç- (part of the third group): g-, g-, - , gedép-, tf-, medf-.

**Imperfect indicative

The imperfect indicative is a past tense describing states and actions that were ongoing in the past, e.g. "gizédauçédudfuç fy" means "I was watching".

    The stem of the imperfect indicative is always invariant for a single verb. It is derived in various ways depending on the verb group.

    The conjugation prefixes of this tense are for any of the three groups always: gizéd-, gizéd-, mizéd-, gedépiz-, tfiz-, medfizéd-.
